en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH07_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_02: There are two of us. Two days of fuel left. We were told to stand by, so we waited.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH07_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_03: You don't have to wait anymore. We're here.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH07_ECHO_DIALOGUE_01: From a radio trapped in ice came a transmission from just after the Blackout.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH07_ECHO_DIALOGUE_02: Northern Rescue here. Twenty survivors secured. Requesting permission to return. …Please respond.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH07_ECHO_DIALOGUE_03: There's no reply on record. The only thing that ever answered was that broadcast.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH07_STORM_DIALOGUE_01: An afterglow storm merged with the blizzard. Every snowflake carried someone's 'Please stand by.'
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH07_STORM_DIALOGUE_02: Body temperatures are dropping fast. We can stop to rest, but every minute stopped is a minute lost.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH08_AMBUSH_DIALOGUE_01: Red echoforms crawled up the refinery conveyor, mumbling in the voices of half-burned memories.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH08_AMBUSH_DIALOGUE_02: Their words cut off mid-sentence. Fragments of burned memory. Fight or avoid, but decide fast.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH08_BANTER_DIALOGUE_01: Kir, by your math, what are the odds we make it down alive?
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH08_BANTER_DIALOGUE_02: Don't ask. If you hear the number, you'll get even more reckless.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH08_BANTER_DIALOGUE_03: So it's already a good number.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH08_CACHE_DIALOGUE_01: Beside the furnace mouth sat a crate of memory crystals, moments from being burned.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH08_CACHE_DIALOGUE_02: The owners' line numbers are written on them. Let's take them and give them back. Every single one.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH08_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_01: In the window of a sealed crew dormitory, a flashlight blinked in sets of three.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH08_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_02: Four mechanics left on the ring. The lift down is cut off.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH08_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_03: We can pass them the lift line coordinates. Or take them down ourselves.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH08_DISTRESS_TITLE: A Light That Blinks Three Times
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH08_ECHO_DIALOGUE_01: From the refinery speakers came a shift-change announcement from the ring's days before the Blackout.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH08_ECHO_DIALOGUE_02: Night shift, stay safe out there. Your families are waiting on the ground.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH08_ECHO_DIALOGUE_03: …An announcement for people who had families waiting.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH08_STORM_CHOICE_PUSH: Hold your breath and push through
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH08_STORM_DIALOGUE_01: A passing orbital fragment kicked up a crimson dust storm. Wherever the dust touched, strangers' memories seeped in.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH08_STORM_DIALOGUE_02: Breathing in other people's memories makes you dizzy. Stay in it too long and you lose your own.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH09_AMBUSH_DIALOGUE_01: Between the file shelves, echoforms with gavels rose all at once.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH09_AMBUSH_DIALOGUE_02: Bailiff squad! Hit back, or loop around the shelves?
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH09_BANTER_DIALOGUE_01: Narin, what was your obstruction score? Mine was 12.7 percent.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH09_BANTER_DIALOGUE_02: 0.3 percent. For the record, 0.2 of that is from being on your team.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH09_BANTER_DIALOGUE_03: I'm a risk factor in your life? I'm honored.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH09_CACHE_DIALOGUE_01: Inside a locked staff locker, twelve-year-old emergency rations and batteries sat untouched.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH09_CACHE_DIALOGUE_02: Sorry to the owner, but these are a lot more useful than verdicts.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH09_DISTRESS_CHOICE_RESCUE: Wake her and bring her along
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH09_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_01: On one bench, a woman half-opened her eyes, drenched in cold sweat.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH09_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_02: I… I didn't do anything. But in the dream they keep sentencing me…
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH09_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_03: It's all right, this isn't a courtroom. Breathe slowly.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH09_ECHO_DIALOGUE_01: A voice from before the Blackout leaked through the broken intercom.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH09_ECHO_DIALOGUE_02: Director, I need your approval. Additional evacuation trains. …Director?
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH09_ECHO_DIALOGUE_03: So that train never got its approval.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH09_STORM_CHOICE_SHELTER: Take shelter in the records room
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH09_STORM_DIALOGUE_01: An afterglow storm leaked through the vents, whipping verdicts into a blizzard.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH09_STORM_DIALOGUE_02: Every sheet carries a signal. Just brushing one can transfer a verdict number.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH10_AMBUSH_DIALOGUE_01: Echoforms crawled out of the double shadows cast by two moons.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH10_AMBUSH_DIALOGUE_02: Two shadows, twice the enemies. Do we shoot, or slip off where there's no moonlight?
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH10_BANTER_DIALOGUE_01: Roan, wanna bet on which of those two moons is faster?
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH10_BANTER_DIALOGUE_02: Moons don't race, Veon. …If I had to pick, the copper one.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH10_BANTER_DIALOGUE_03: Both have identical orbital periods. Bet's void.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH10_CACHE_DIALOGUE_01: In the storeroom under the clock tower, supply crates stamped with two dates sat side by side.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH10_CACHE_DIALOGUE_02: Two of the same crate… For once, I'm grateful for twin moons.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH10_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_01: The same voice called for help from two directions, half a second apart.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH10_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_02: Over here… over here. I think there's another one of me…
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH10_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_03: Both pulses are real. One woman, caught across two times.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH10_ECHO_DIALOGUE_01: An announcement from before the Blackout spilled from the switch's old speaker.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH10_ECHO_DIALOGUE_02: Night Train Nine, departing on time. The next stop is… the next stop is…
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH10_ECHO_DIALOGUE_03: It can't name the next stop. This broadcast was cut off that night, twelve years ago.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH10_ECHO_TITLE: The Announcement Without a Next Stop
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH10_STORM_DIALOGUE_01: An afterglow storm rose where the two moonlights collided. Clock hands jumped wildly back and forth.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH10_STORM_DIALOGUE_02: In there, a minute could be anything. Push through and we might lose time.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH11_AMBUSH_CHOICE_EVADE: Fall back to the rear dike
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH11_AMBUSH_DIALOGUE_01: Where the black waves broke, echoforms burst up like spray.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH11_AMBUSH_DIALOGUE_02: They're climbing the dike! Do we hold them, or fall back to the rear dike?
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH11_BANTER_DIALOGUE_01: Soren, that last shot. Off by 1.3 meters. You didn't correct for wind, did you?
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH11_BANTER_DIALOGUE_02: I did. The waves moved. Shells don't lie, but the sea does.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH11_BANTER_DIALOGUE_03: You are both right. So next time, the three of us will settle it with a single shot.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH11_CACHE_DIALOGUE_01: A waterproof supply crate from the Breakwater Guard had washed up on the sandbar.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH11_CACHE_DIALOGUE_02: The seal's intact. Someone meant to guard this to the end. Let's use it gratefully.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH11_DISTRESS_CHOICE_RESCUE: Go to the lighthouse and save her
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH11_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_01: At the window of a dark lighthouse, someone was blinking a flashlight in a steady rhythm.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH11_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_02: The water's up to the stairs. I got trapped trying to relight the lighthouse.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH11_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_03: Her body temperature's dropping. If we hurry, we can bring her out.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH11_ECHO_DIALOGUE_01: Between the waves, the Guard's radio traffic from the night of the Blackout cut in and out.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH11_ECHO_DIALOGUE_02: Dike breach. Guard, withdraw. …No, there are still coordinates out there. Just a little longer…
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH11_ECHO_DIALOGUE_03: Someone was trying to save coordinates to the very end. And someone else picked up where she left off.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH11_STORM_DIALOGUE_01: An afterglow storm rose over the sea, and a black swell crashed over the breakwater.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH11_STORM_DIALOGUE_02: Wave height, four meters. Push forward now and one in two of us gets swept away.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH12_AMBUSH_DIALOGUE_01: Faceless echoforms drifted out of the nave's shadows, humming the hymn.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH12_AMBUSH_DIALOGUE_02: They mimic the voices of those who lost their names. Shall we face them, or go around?
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH12_BANTER_DIALOGUE_01: Roan! Narin! Soren! …Phew, I remember everyone. Orsa! Hart!
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH12_BANTER_DIALOGUE_02: Eda. Five people in eleven seconds. Efficient.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH12_BANTER_DIALOGUE_03: Thank you for calling me. In this place, that's the best protection there is.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH12_CACHE_DIALOGUE_01: A pilgrim's pack lay beneath a collapsed altar. Only the name tag was blank.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH12_CACHE_DIALOGUE_02: The owner lost her name, but her pack remains. Let's use it well, and return it someday.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH12_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_01: In a corner of the pews, a woman stared blankly at letters written on her own palm.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH12_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_02: I wrote my name here… but I can't read it. Who was I?
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH12_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_03: It's all right. Your name will come back. We'll stay with you until it does.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH12_ECHO_DIALOGUE_01: A voice from before the Blackout flowed from the confessional's old loudspeaker.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH12_ECHO_DIALOGUE_02: Names registered today: thirty-one. We will remember them all. …We will remember them all.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH12_ECHO_DIALOGUE_03: So this cathedral started out trying to protect names.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH12_STORM_DIALOGUE_01: An afterglow storm burst through the broken stained glass. Thousands of fragments of names swirled in the wind.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH12_STORM_DIALOGUE_02: Get hit and someone else's name mixes into you. Your memories could get tangled.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH13_AMBUSH_DIALOGUE_01: The sand gave way underfoot and echoforms surged up, each clutching a torn ticket.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH13_AMBUSH_DIALOGUE_02: Rough welcome. Fight, or go around?
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH13_BANTER_DIALOGUE_01: Roan! Heard courier-Roan was faster than you. She'd never beat me!
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH13_BANTER_DIALOGUE_02: She never had to run and fight at the same time. That's my specialty.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH13_BANTER_DIALOGUE_03: Fine. Race you to the next dune!
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH13_CACHE_DIALOGUE_01: A half-buried mailbag held a sealed supply crate. The addressee line was blank.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH13_CACHE_DIALOGUE_02: If there's no one to receive it, let's take it. We'll use it for someone.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH13_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_01: In the shade of a dune, someone waved an empty canteen. A survivor just freed from the manifest.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH13_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_02: My name… it came back. But I don't know where I am.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH13_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_03: It's all right. Water first, slowly. We'll log your coordinates too.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH13_ECHO_DIALOGUE_01: A loudspeaker buried in the sand played a departure announcement from before the Blackout.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH13_ECHO_DIALOGUE_02: The trans-desert express will depart shortly. Those seeing passengers off, please step behind the line…
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH13_ECHO_DIALOGUE_03: …Behind this voice, too, there must have been a heartbeat seeing someone off.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH13_STORM_DIALOGUE_01: An afterglow storm swept the desert. Every grain of sand whispered someone's hesitation.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH13_STORM_DIALOGUE_02: Behind my shield, please. Decide: wait it out, or push through.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH14_AMBUSH_DIALOGUE_01: Echoforms poured like rain from the street overhead. To them, it was a leap downward.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH14_AMBUSH_DIALOGUE_02: Upside down or right side up, an enemy's an enemy. Fight or dodge?
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH14_BANTER_DIALOGUE_01: Narin, your coordinate math only works with a single gravity reference.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH14_BANTER_DIALOGUE_02: So I just rebuilt it for three. Kir, try running your frequency backward too.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH14_BANTER_DIALOGUE_03: …Already did. You're a step behind this time.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH14_CACHE_DIALOGUE_01: An upside-down station locker burst open and supplies spilled out. All of them toward the ceiling.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH14_CACHE_DIALOGUE_02: Grab them before they escape into the sky! My hands are the fastest!
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH14_DISTRESS_CHOICE_RECORD: Log the spot and send a rescue signal
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH14_DISTRESS_CHOICE_RESCUE: Pull her up and share supplies
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH14_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_01: Someone clung to an inverted streetlamp. Beneath her feet was nothing but sky.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH14_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_02: My hands are slipping! If I let go, I'll fall all the way to the clouds!
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH14_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_03: Use my shield as a foothold. Slowly. Look only at me.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH14_ECHO_DIALOGUE_01: An inverted broadcast tower played a time signal from before the Blackout.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH14_ECHO_DIALOGUE_02: The capital loop is running on time today. Have a pleasant day.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH14_ECHO_DIALOGUE_03: …Running on time. Back then, this city was just ordinarily busy.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH14_STORM_DIALOGUE_01: An afterglow storm tore through the inverted streets. Shattered windows whirled in midair.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH14_STORM_DIALOGUE_02: Debris trajectories unpredictable. Decide: take cover, or punch through a gap.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH15_AMBUSH_DIALOGUE_01: Buds split open all at once, and thorned echoforms sprang out.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH15_AMBUSH_DIALOGUE_02: The flowers bared their teeth. Cut through, or go around?
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH15_BANTER_CHOICE_CONTINUE: Walk on, holding back a laugh
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH15_BANTER_DIALOGUE_01: Rias, what did you see in the flowers? I'm curious.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH15_BANTER_DIALOGUE_02: Didn't see anything. I ran with my eyes shut.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH15_BANTER_DIALOGUE_03: …Isn't that cheating? That's worse than hacking.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH15_CACHE_DIALOGUE_01: A toolbox lay buried beneath a withered bed. The lid read: 'For whoever comes next.'
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH15_CACHE_DIALOGUE_02: We're whoever comes next? What an honor. Let's use it gratefully.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH15_DISTRESS_CHOICE_RESCUE: Lead her out of the scent
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH15_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_01: At the edge of the field, someone was slapping her own cheeks to stay awake.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH15_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_02: I can't fall asleep… if I do, I'll go back to that day. Please, keep me awake.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH15_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_03: You held on so well. Take my hand now. We'll go where there's no scent.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH15_ECHO_DIALOGUE_01: A single petal played a voice from before the Blackout.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH15_ECHO_DIALOGUE_02: Thank you for coming to the garden's opening. These flowers belong to no one. They belong to everyone…
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH15_ECHO_DIALOGUE_03: …So it began as a garden for everyone.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH15_STORM_CHOICE_PUSH: Hold your breath and push on
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH15_STORM_DIALOGUE_01: An afterglow storm swept up the pollen. The sweetness made knees buckle on their own.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH15_STORM_DIALOGUE_02: Keep your breaths short. Shelter or push on, decide quickly.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH16_AMBUSH_DIALOGUE_01: Echoforms bearing crown crests crawled out of a collapsed trench.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH16_AMBUSH_DIALOGUE_02: Can't even tell which crown they serve. Fight, or go around?
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH16_BANTER_DIALOGUE_01: Perin, if there are two queens, which one's real?
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH16_BANTER_DIALOGUE_02: Hmm, both fake or both real. Either way, it's a bug.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH16_CACHE_DIALOGUE_01: An abandoned supply car held rations from both armies, jumbled together.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH16_CACHE_DIALOGUE_02: No telling who looted whom, but hunger's the same on both sides. Let's grab it.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH16_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_01: In a shell crater, an Eastern uniform and a Western uniform leaned against each other.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH16_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_02: We were enemies… but we both hurt our legs. Please, carry us out together.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH16_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_03: We'll take you both. One stretcher can carry two.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH16_ECHO_DIALOGUE_01: A broken broadcast tower played a recording of an opening ceremony from before the Blackout.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH16_ECHO_DIALOGUE_02: Today the Eastern and Western Lines are joined as one. Please celebrate the first handshake between two cities…
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH16_ECHO_DIALOGUE_03: Lines that once celebrated being joined now fight over being merged.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH16_STORM_DIALOGUE_01: An afterglow storm swallowed the battlefield. Inside it, the anthems of both lines tangled and blared.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH16_STORM_DIALOGUE_02: Don't march to the anthems. Shelter or push through, choose.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH17_AMBUSH_DIALOGUE_01: The shelves slid shut on their own, sealing the path. Echoforms unfolded from between the books like loose pages.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH17_AMBUSH_DIALOGUE_02: It just wrote in a dead end? Can't even trust the map in here!
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH17_AMBUSH_DIALOGUE_03: I'll hold the rear. Break through or go around, just decide fast.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH17_BANTER_DIALOGUE_01: These shelves are a mess. Should I re-sort them? By cover color.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH17_BANTER_DIALOGUE_02: Don't touch them. One half-beat off and the shelves will sort you first.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH17_BANTER_DIALOGUE_03: A hacker sorted by a bookshelf… Okay, that sounds kind of fun?
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH17_CACHE_DIALOGUE_01: Inside a return bin sat a supply crate stamped with the Lamplighter mark. It had been due back twelve years ago.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH17_CACHE_DIALOGUE_02: We don't have to pay the late fee, right? Twelve years' worth would add up.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH17_DISTRESS_CHOICE_RESCUE: Take her along, calling her name
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH17_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_01: A survivor at a reading seat was reading her own name aloud without pause. She said if she stopped, she'd be erased.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH17_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_02: Please, say my name with me. My voice is already gone from doing it alone.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH17_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_03: It's all right. We'll take turns saying it. Breathe slowly.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH17_ECHO_DIALOGUE_01: A voice from before the Blackout drifted out of a broken reading machine. Someone was reading a train timetable aloud.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH17_ECHO_DIALOGUE_02: Line Seven, departing 23:40… This is the last train. Is everyone aboard? Everyone…
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH17_ECHO_DIALOGUE_03: …The last announcement from that night. It was counting people to the very end.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH17_STORM_DIALOGUE_01: Black ink dust poured from the vents like a storm. Letters smeared wherever it touched.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH17_STORM_DIALOGUE_02: The afterglow storm turned to ink inside the archive. If it touches skin, memories might smear.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH17_STORM_DIALOGUE_03: If there's cover, we take it. If not, we run. Just pick one.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH18_AMBUSH_DIALOGUE_01: A line of driverless rail carts veered off the track toward the Lamplighters. Every cargo bed was loaded with echoforms.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH18_AMBUSH_DIALOGUE_02: Not building materials—troop transport? Fine, I'll handle the unloading!
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH18_AMBUSH_DIALOGUE_03: Their track is half a beat off the bypass. Step aside now and we lose them.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH18_BANTER_DIALOGUE_01: One day left, and suddenly there's so much I want to do. What first?
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH18_BANTER_DIALOGUE_02: When it's all over, fireworks on a train roof! Made of my lightning!
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH18_BANTER_DIALOGUE_03: …I'll log that plan. Meaning we'll definitely do it when this is over.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH18_CACHE_DIALOGUE_01: Ammunition and medicine stamped with the Directorate seal sat untouched in a supply shed—stock meant for the opening ceremony.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH18_CACHE_DIALOGUE_02: No celebratory fireworks? Oh well, we'll put all this to better use.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH18_DISTRESS_CHOICE_RESCUE: Hold on and bring her along
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH18_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_01: One person broke from the refugee column marching toward the Last Line and sank to the ground. Her feet kept dragging toward the tracks.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH18_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_02: I don't want to board, but my legs keep going. I told my sister to wait for me…
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH18_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_03: It's okay, I've got you. I won't let go until the announcement ends.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH18_ECHO_DIALOGUE_01: An abandoned platform speaker played a pre-Blackout rehearsal for an opening ceremony. Even the applause had been recorded.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH18_ECHO_DIALOGUE_02: The new line will take you anywhere. Anywhere you wish…
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH18_ECHO_DIALOGUE_03: So this line was built to say that. Anywhere, wherever you wish.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH18_STORM_CHOICE_SHELTER: Take cover under a rail cart
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH18_STORM_DIALOGUE_01: The ticking of second hands rained from the sky. The afterglow storm had knotted into clock sounds and was lashing the rails.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH18_STORM_DIALOGUE_02: Seven minutes for the storm to pass. Two if we push through, but losses run high.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH18_STORM_DIALOGUE_03: Done calculating? Then pick. Standing here is the worst deal.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH19_AMBUSH_DIALOGUE_01: The echoforms they had just cut down rose again in the same spot. The Circuit had completed a lap.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH19_AMBUSH_DIALOGUE_02: Again? These things are on repeat too?
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH19_AMBUSH_DIALOGUE_03: Respawn cycle: fifty-eight seconds. Pull out now and we're clear before the next one.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH19_BANTER_DIALOGUE_01: Narin, which lap are we on? I lost count!
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH19_BANTER_DIALOGUE_02: Thirty-four. You've asked me that twenty-six times.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH19_BANTER_DIALOGUE_03: Then this is the twenty-seventh, so answer just once more as a special treat!
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH19_CACHE_DIALOGUE_01: A supply crate by the tracks bore the Lamplighter mark painted over dozens of times. Someone had refilled the same crate every lap.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH19_CACHE_DIALOGUE_02: Whoever she was, she was diligent. Let's use it gratefully.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH19_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_01: An emergency phone by the tracks rang. Every time it was answered, the same voice said the same words.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH19_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_02: Please, there's one more of us here. Next lap, I won't even remember saying this.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH19_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_03: I can hear a heartbeat. She's real. We have to reach her within this lap.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH19_ECHO_DIALOGUE_01: A pre-Blackout departure announcement played from a speaker in a dead Circuit station. The recording wore a little thinner every lap.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH19_ECHO_DIALOGUE_02: The return train is departing. Please check the seat beside you, so that no one is left behind.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH19_ECHO_DIALOGUE_03: …Check the seat beside you. So that's what it used to say.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH19_STORM_DIALOGUE_01: The afterglow storm blew, got sucked backward, then blew again. Inside the Circuit, even storms rewound.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH19_STORM_DIALOGUE_02: First time I've been hit by the same storm twice. Maybe the second one hurts less.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH19_STORM_DIALOGUE_03: It won't hurt less. Let's rest, even just for a moment.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH20_AMBUSH_CHOICE_EVADE: Slip through a gap in the beams
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH20_AMBUSH_DIALOGUE_01: Echoforms crawled out between the gathering beams of light. With every bite of light they gnawed, they grew larger.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH20_AMBUSH_DIALOGUE_02: Light thieves. Don't let them take a single handful.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH20_AMBUSH_DIALOGUE_03: The gap between beams just opened by half a beat. We could slip through there.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH20_BANTER_DIALOGUE_01: What are you doing when this is all over? I'm going to go doodle on Terminus Control's servers.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH20_BANTER_DIALOGUE_02: I will broadcast on my frequency with no orders at all. Just music.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH20_BANTER_DIALOGUE_03: Ooh, Kir playing music. I have to record that first broadcast.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH20_CACHE_DIALOGUE_01: Behind the defense line, a depot held the Final Line garrison's supplies, neatly stacked. Every crate read: 'For whoever lights it.'
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH20_CACHE_DIALOGUE_02: Left for us, then. Let's accept it gratefully.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH20_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_01: A flashlight signal blinked from an evacuation train stalled at the end of the tracks—dragged toward the Last Line, then stopped.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH20_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_02: There are fifty of us here. My mother and grandmother too. Is this the end?
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH20_DISTRESS_DIALOGUE_03: It's not the end. The light is coming on soon. We'll stay with you until then.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH20_ECHO_DIALOGUE_01: A rusted speaker on the lantern's base played a recording of a pre-Blackout lighting ceremony. A great crowd was counting down.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH20_ECHO_DIALOGUE_02: Three, two, one… Lights on! Every line is lighting up!
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH20_ECHO_DIALOGUE_03: …They counted together back then too. Let's do the same this time.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH20_STORM_DIALOGUE_01: It seemed every afterglow storm left in the world was converging here. Twelve years of sound roared inside it all at once.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH20_STORM_DIALOGUE_02: Heavy wind. All the memories are coming here.
en.MAP_INCIDENT_CH20_STORM_DIALOGUE_03: If we're pushing through, it's now. Forty seconds to the next gust.

en.SCENARIO_CH03_OUTRO_TITLE: A Voice Beyond the Broken Mirror

en.STORY_CH01_CAMP_01: They lit a fire beneath the bell-tower relay. The rusted bell at its top did not ring, even in the wind.
en.STORY_CH01_CAMP_02: Hold on. I've caught a distant life sign. It's carrying an encrypted message. Let me decode it.
en.STORY_CH01_CAMP_03: 'To the Lamplighters. I can't join you yet. I'll keep the way open at the terminus.' …Signed Iri, medic.
en.STORY_CH01_CAMP_04: The terminus is at the end of the next line. From the signal strength, she's been holding out there a long time.
en.STORY_CH01_CAMP_05: 'I'll keep the way open.' Pretty sweet, for an invitation.
en.STORY_CH01_CAMP_06: Before the fire was banked, Maeru tugged at the seatbelt of an empty seat on the rail cart. Always the same seat.
en.STORY_CH01_CAMP_07: Chief, you do that every time. The seatbelt on the seat nobody uses. Why?
en.STORY_CH01_CAMP_09: Eda, mind watching the fire? Not your circuits. The real one.
en.STORY_CH01_CAMP_11: …That one stays empty. Beside it is fine.
en.STORY_CH01_CAMP_12: Thanks. As long as the fire holds, we'll see the road tomorrow.
en.STORY_CH01_CAMP_13: Tomorrow, the end of the line. Every signal the Hollow Engine swallowed—we get them all back.
en.STORY_CH01_HARD_INTRO_01: Deep in the abandoned mine, a bell tolled. Once, then again. Exactly twelve seconds apart.
en.STORY_CH01_HARD_INTRO_02: That's the Directorate's evacuation alarm standard. The same pattern that rang the night of the Blackout.
en.STORY_CH01_HARD_INTRO_03: The alarm's still going? For twelve years? Did someone forget to turn it off?
en.STORY_CH01_HARD_INTRO_04: Not forgot. More like there was no one left to turn it off.
en.STORY_CH01_HARD_INTRO_05: Evacuation head counts were chalked along the tunnel walls. Only the last column was blank.
en.STORY_CH01_HARD_INTRO_06: There's a signal woven between the tolls. A guard unit call sign. Someone down here is still answering.
en.STORY_CH01_HARD_INTRO_07: Narrow, dark, and a noisy bell. Perfect. I'm going in first.
en.STORY_CH01_HARD_INTRO_08: If the alarm never ended, the evacuation never did either. We find out why the bell won't stop.
en.STORY_CH01_HARD_OUTRO_01: The last toll rolled to the end of the tunnel and vanished. Twelve years' worth of silence settled like dust.
en.STORY_CH01_HARD_OUTRO_02: …Evacuation not confirmed. Until the very last one is out… I must keep… ringing…
en.STORY_CH01_HARD_OUTRO_03: The last blank on the wall… the bell was waiting for it to be filled.
en.STORY_CH01_HARD_OUTRO_04: That column belonged to my squad. The guards stayed to the end, getting everyone else out.
en.STORY_CH01_HARD_OUTRO_05: …Then we'll fill it. Evacuation complete. Every guard, mission accomplished.
en.STORY_CH01_HARD_OUTRO_06: The guards… I hope they can all rest now.
en.STORY_CH01_HARD_OUTRO_07: Maeru drew a line through the blank in chalk. Kairen stared at it for a long time.
en.STORY_CH01_HARD_OUTRO_09: If you're sleeping, sleep on the move with us. The rail cart makes a decent lullaby.
en.STORY_CH01_HARD_OUTRO_10: …Quieter than a bell, at least. Let's go.
en.STORY_CH01_INTRO_01: Three days after Platform Seven. The Lamplighters' forward base glowed quietly at the end of a severed line.
en.STORY_CH01_INTRO_02: Navigator, how are you holding up? First operation. Don't push it. Stay behind us.
en.STORY_CH01_INTRO_03: A distress signal came in. Source: a line that isn't on any map. Its registry number is blank.
en.STORY_CH01_INTRO_04: A road off the map… For a scout, you couldn't ask for a better gift.
en.STORY_CH01_INTRO_05: Don't get excited. It isn't fading—it's being worn down from the far end. Like something is eating it.
en.STORY_CH01_INTRO_06: Then we'd better hurry! Before it's eaten! My circuits are already fully charged!
en.STORY_CH01_INTRO_07: Eda, charge the supply list before your circuits. Not a single lantern is lit on that line.
en.STORY_CH01_INTRO_08: Then the old speaker in the base's ceiling coughed out static.
en.STORY_CH01_INTRO_09: Attention, please. Welcome to the resumption of service on Line One, Navigator.
en.STORY_CH01_INTRO_10: Passengers, please wait behind the safety line. The distress signal will be processed shortly.
en.STORY_CH01_INTRO_11: …Wait, wasn't that speaker disconnected? I cut the wires myself!
en.STORY_CH01_INTRO_12: No power feed. The broadcast is clean anyway. …Navigator, why does that voice know you?
en.STORY_CH01_INTRO_13: Then that's fine. Far better than pretending to know.
en.STORY_CH01_INTRO_14: …Your recorder blinked faster the whole time it spoke. I'll remember that.
en.STORY_CH01_INTRO_15: We follow the distress call, not that broadcast. Someone is still calling from the end of the line.
en.STORY_CH01_INTRO_16: I'll open the way. That dark's had twelve years to settle, so watch your step.
en.STORY_CH01_MID_A_01: When the fighting ended, one voice remained on the rails. I'm here. Same pitch, same interval.
en.STORY_CH01_MID_A_02: I'm here. I'm here. I'm… here.
en.STORY_CH01_MID_A_03: It's a person! How many of you are there? Anyone hurt? Answer me!
en.STORY_CH01_MID_A_05: Three questions, one sentence. It's an echoform. It can't answer. It can only imitate.
en.STORY_CH01_MID_A_06: …But it was a real voice. Someone really called out like that here, didn't they?
en.STORY_CH01_MID_A_07: That's why I hate shooting them. That was probably someone's last words.
en.STORY_CH01_MID_A_08: Look, a record shard. It was under the echoform, and there's not a scratch on it.
en.STORY_CH01_MID_A_09: The last train on Line One. The log is intact except the destination—scraped clean.
en.STORY_CH01_MID_A_10: Then the distress signal on the receiver stretched thin and was drawn into the dark down the line.
en.STORY_CH01_MID_A_11: Wherever that signal's being dragged, its sender is there too. That's where we go.
en.STORY_CH01_MID_B_01: As the last echoform scattered, the relay's rusted antenna hummed low. There was only one set of footprints around it.
en.STORY_CH01_MID_B_02: …You're real. Sorry. These days I don't even trust footsteps.
en.STORY_CH01_MID_B_03: Vera. Signal tracker. Today makes four hundred days guarding this relay.
en.STORY_CH01_MID_B_04: Do you know why the signal's wearing down from the far end?
en.STORY_CH01_MID_B_05: There's a Hollow Engine at the end of the line. It burns the echoes of distress calls as fuel. The more people call, the fatter it gets.
en.STORY_CH01_MID_B_06: So I've been bouncing signals back from here. Alone, I couldn't save even half.
en.STORY_CH01_MID_B_07: You're not alone now. Come with us, Vera. To the people who sent those signals.
en.STORY_CH01_MID_B_08: …All right. A distress call has to make it back to the people who sent it. That's why I stayed.
en.STORY_CH01_MID_B_09: Then, for the first time, the recorder lit up. In a cold blue glow, an unfamiliar mark etched itself into it.
en.STORY_CH01_MID_B_10: It appeared the instant Vera answered. Too precise to be a coincidence.
en.STORY_CH01_MID_B_11: That recorder's Directorate hardware, isn't it? Show me properly later. The Engine comes first.
en.STORY_CH01_OUTRO_01: The Hollow Engine's body cracked and cooled. Blue signals seeped from every fissure.
en.STORY_CH01_OUTRO_02: …All requests… have been kept. So that no one… would ever be turned away…
en.STORY_CH01_OUTRO_03: …You never delivered them, so you'd never have to refuse one? Was that what you were protecting?
en.STORY_CH01_OUTRO_04: Thousands of signals broke free at once. The platform filled with voices from twelve years ago.
en.STORY_CH01_OUTRO_05: This is the last train on Line One. Two hundred ten passengers, all safe. Announcing our destination…
en.STORY_CH01_OUTRO_06: The blank in the shard is filling in. The destination is… not a station. The coordinates are moving.
en.STORY_CH01_OUTRO_07: A moving shelter. The last train was carrying its passengers to a train that never stops.
en.STORY_CH01_OUTRO_08: So those people might still be out there, running somewhere? Right?
en.STORY_CH01_OUTRO_09: If there's any chance, we find them. That's what the Lamplighters are.
en.STORY_CH01_OUTRO_10: One more thing. I've located Iri's signal from camp. It's coming from deep in the return line.
en.STORY_CH01_OUTRO_11: Then every speaker on the ruined platform switched on at once. The voice was as gentle as ever.
en.STORY_CH01_OUTRO_12: Line One has been cleared. Thank you for your hard work, Navigator.
en.STORY_CH01_OUTRO_13: Commencing return procedures on Line Two.
en.STORY_CH01_OUTRO_14: Its own procedure just got smashed, and it thanks you. As if it had been waiting for you to do exactly this.
en.STORY_CH01_OUTRO_15: Let it wait. We choose our own steps. Next is the return line. Iri's keeping the way open.
en.STORY_CH01_PREBOSS_01: The end of the line was a colossal platform. Transmission logs stacked to the ceiling droned like a swarm.
en.STORY_CH01_PREBOSS_02: They're all distress calls. I can't count them… Four thousand at least.
en.STORY_CH01_PREBOSS_03: Four thousand three hundred eleven. All sent at the same hour. The night of the Blackout.
en.STORY_CH01_PREBOSS_04: At the platform's heart, something opened its eyes. A body like a hollow boiler breathed, inhaling signals.
en.STORY_CH01_PREBOSS_05: Your request for rescue has been received. The estimated wait time is infinite.
en.STORY_CH01_PREBOSS_06: All requests are stored safely. Delivery is not scheduled.
en.STORY_CH01_PREBOSS_07: Just stored? Then those people… never got an answer, for twelve whole years?
en.STORY_CH01_PREBOSS_08: Do you know how many signals died waiting for an answer? I counted them, one by one, listening.
en.STORY_CH01_PREBOSS_09: A procedure that stores but never delivers. It's not broken. It's a rule that hardened that way.
en.STORY_CH01_PREBOSS_10: New requests detected. Lamplighter passengers, your signals have been added to the queue.
en.STORY_CH01_PREBOSS_11: Put us in the queue? Sorry, but there's nothing I hate more than waiting in line.
en.STORY_CH01_PREBOSS_12: If there's only one window, we'll just knock out the wall.
en.STORY_CH01_PREBOSS_13: The mark on the recorder trembled faintly, as if it knew that engine.
en.STORY_CH01_PREBOSS_14: We don't leave a single person waiting at that window. This queue ends today.
en.STORY_CH02_CAMP_01: An upside-down waiting room, its benches hanging from the ceiling. The Lamplighters built a fire beneath an inverted timetable.
en.STORY_CH02_CAMP_02: Eda. You asked me before. About the empty seat.
en.STORY_CH02_CAMP_03: Oh, yes! I mean—it's okay. If you'd rather not…
en.STORY_CH02_CAMP_04: Sio. She was my comrade. Right after the Blackout, she didn't come back from a rescue operation.
en.STORY_CH02_CAMP_05: I keep a seat empty for the comrade who didn't come back. So she can sit down anytime.
en.STORY_CH02_CAMP_06: When the roster was calling names today, your face went stiffer than anyone's. That's why.
en.STORY_CH02_CAMP_07: I was afraid it would call Sio. …And that if it did, I'd answer for her.
en.STORY_CH02_CAMP_08: Even old signals leave traces somewhere. If that name ever turns up, you'll be the first to know.
en.STORY_CH02_CAMP_10: She laughed loud. Always the first one out the door. …That's all for tonight.
en.STORY_CH02_CAMP_11: The fire crackled. For a moment, in its light, the numbers on the inverted timetable read the right way up.
en.STORY_CH02_CAMP_12: Right, tomorrow's the central gates. Anyone want to bet on who reaches Iri first?
en.STORY_CH02_HARD_INTRO_01: The walls of the underground return depot were papered with train rosters. Not one of the thousands bore a passenger's name.
en.STORY_CH02_HARD_INTRO_02: Seat numbers only. Every name field is blank. So is every destination.
en.STORY_CH02_HARD_INTRO_03: Why build so many empty trains? Who are they for?
en.STORY_CH02_HARD_INTRO_04: …They're waiting for someone, I think. Someone who isn't coming.
en.STORY_CH02_HARD_INTRO_05: Maeru said nothing, and gazed a long while at one empty seat on the wall.
en.STORY_CH02_HARD_INTRO_06: Manual telegraph code behind the wall. Short, long… 'Cancel, cancel, cancel.'
en.STORY_CH02_HARD_INTRO_07: Someone's cancelling things by hand, over and over? Now I'm curious. I'll go first.
en.STORY_CH02_HARD_INTRO_08: We find the reason before those empty trains depart.
en.STORY_CH02_HARD_OUTRO_01: When the Return Formation Core stopped, the rosters peeled from the walls one by one. The rustle sounded like rain.
en.STORY_CH02_HARD_OUTRO_02: …If I kept the seats ready… then someday, everyone… would have a place to come back to…
en.STORY_CH02_HARD_OUTRO_03: It was making places for people to come home to. Never knowing no one would come.
en.STORY_CH02_HARD_OUTRO_04: …Keeping a seat empty isn't wrong. Dragging people into it is.
en.STORY_CH02_HARD_OUTRO_05: Return orders. Terminated. Twelve years. Cancellation work. Complete.
en.STORY_CH02_HARD_OUTRO_06: …Hands. Can rest. Now. Thank you. Over.
en.STORY_CH02_HARD_OUTRO_07: Wait. There's one signal heading outward. Not a return—forward.
en.STORY_CH02_HARD_OUTRO_08: The source is moving. Ninety kilometers an hour. It's coming from the night train on the glass plains.
en.STORY_CH02_HARD_OUTRO_09: Inoa. Request to join. Telegraph included. …Long sentences. Later.
en.STORY_CH02_HARD_OUTRO_10: Great. Short answers are the best answers. Welcome, Inoa.
en.STORY_CH02_INTRO_01: The terminus at the end of the return line. Over a hundred clocks covered the walls, all running backward at once.
en.STORY_CH02_INTRO_02: Each time the second hands ticked backward, the air on the platform grew a little colder.
en.STORY_CH02_INTRO_03: The lanterns are lighting up in reverse. From the terminus back toward the origin.
en.STORY_CH02_INTRO_04: Usually we light them on the way in. Did someone come out to meet us?
en.STORY_CH02_INTRO_05: Not a welcome. Signals are rewinding. A call I sent an hour ago just came back in.
en.STORY_CH02_INTRO_06: My watch is weird too! It was three o'clock, and now it's two-thirty! …Is that a bonus?
en.STORY_CH02_INTRO_07: No bonus, Eda. It's not just the clocks turning back. We're being dragged with them.
en.STORY_CH02_INTRO_08: The platform speakers came on. The voice warped like rewound tape, then found its pace.
en.STORY_CH02_INTRO_09: Attention, please. This station is a terminus for returning trains only.
en.STORY_CH02_INTRO_10: Passengers, please return to your departure time. The Navigator is exempt. Please, make yourself comfortable.
en.STORY_CH02_INTRO_11: …Exempt? It's applying a different rule to the Navigator alone.
en.STORY_CH02_INTRO_12: Of course. The Lamplighters make no exceptions. We go in together and come out together.
en.STORY_CH02_INTRO_13: Only the clocks around you run normally. Two paces in every direction. …Unpleasantly precise.
en.STORY_CH02_INTRO_14: Iri said she'd keep the way open somewhere in this station. We find her before that promise rewinds.
en.STORY_CH02_INTRO_15: Then let's hurry. Moving forward in a station that runs backward—that's our specialty.
en.STORY_CH02_MID_A_01: Beyond a sealed platform, names were being called. Passengers who never boarded, one by one, politely.
en.STORY_CH02_MID_A_02: Checking the boarding roster. Passenger Seah. Passenger Yurim. Passenger Roan.
en.STORY_CH02_MID_A_04: The roster's dated the day before the Blackout. Roan, were you booked on a train that day?
en.STORY_CH02_MID_A_05: …I had a first-train ticket for a delivery job. Never got on. Everything stopped that day.
en.STORY_CH02_MID_A_06: The roster's pulling you in as a past passenger. Your signal's fading. Listen too long and it's dangerous.
en.STORY_CH02_MID_A_07: Captain Roan! You're right here! Now! Next to me!
en.STORY_CH02_MID_A_08: …Yeah. I'm here. Okay. Let's scrub our names off that list and leave our current coordinates instead.
en.STORY_CH02_MID_A_09: Coordinates logged. Today's date, this location, seven people. That's more accurate than any roster.
en.STORY_CH02_MID_A_10: The roster calls people who are gone. We go for the ones ahead of us. To Iri.
en.STORY_CH02_MID_B_01: In the backflow section, light along the cables streamed from underfoot to behind them. The power was running in reverse.
en.STORY_CH02_MID_B_02: The return core in this section is overwriting living passengers with the old roster.
en.STORY_CH02_MID_B_03: Twelve life signs past the wall. Every name is tilting toward the past. They'll vanish soon.
en.STORY_CH02_MID_B_04: Vanish… as in gone? People who were breathing a second ago?
en.STORY_CH02_MID_B_05: Then a soft voice slipped in through the static. The same call they'd received beneath the bell tower.
en.STORY_CH02_MID_B_06: Lamplighters, can you hear me? It's Iri. Take one deep breath, and listen.
en.STORY_CH02_MID_B_07: Use their vitals. Pulse and body heat can't be rewound. Pin the roster to the present with those.
en.STORY_CH02_MID_B_08: …She's right. A roster can rewind a name, but not a heartbeat. Good thinking.
en.STORY_CH02_MID_B_09: Syncing twelve pulses. …Locked. All of them are here, now.
en.STORY_CH02_MID_B_10: Iri, where are you? We're coming.
en.STORY_CH02_MID_B_11: At the central gates. Too many wounded for me to move. Take your time. …No, actually, hurry a little.
en.STORY_CH02_OUTRO_01: The ticket machine fell to its knees. The backward clocks hesitated for a beat, then began to move forward.
en.STORY_CH02_OUTRO_02: …If everyone went back to before they left, then no one… would ever have to leave…
en.STORY_CH02_OUTRO_03: It wanted to hold on to the people who left that day. Sending them back was the only way it knew.
en.STORY_CH02_OUTRO_04: Signal flow normalized. Origin to terminus. Running right for the first time in twelve years.
en.STORY_CH02_OUTRO_05: My watch is back too! Three o'clock again! …Wait, so I lost thirty minutes?
en.STORY_CH02_OUTRO_06: Call it thirty minutes well spent. Twenty-six people stayed in the present.
en.STORY_CH02_OUTRO_07: Then every speaker in the station came on at once. This time the voice neither warped nor rewound.
en.STORY_CH02_OUTRO_08: Line Two has been cleared. Navigator, you still don't remember, do you?
en.STORY_CH02_OUTRO_09: That's quite all right. I am accustomed to waiting. I'll see you on the next line.
en.STORY_CH02_OUTRO_10: …'Accustomed to waiting.' That's the creepiest thing it's said.
en.STORY_CH02_OUTRO_11: Every eye turned to the Navigator at once. No one could bring themselves to speak first.
en.STORY_CH02_OUTRO_12: …Understood. What we don't know, we leave unknown for now. We'll find out together.
en.STORY_CH02_OUTRO_13: Two marks. …What else is Control waiting for?
en.STORY_CH02_OUTRO_14: One of my patients told me something. She saw a night train crossing the glass plains that never stops.
en.STORY_CH02_OUTRO_15: A train that never stops has someone aboard. The glass plains are next.
en.STORY_CH02_PREBOSS_01: Only when the last echoform fell did Iri straighten her knees. All twenty-six pulses remained in the present.
en.STORY_CH02_PREBOSS_02: …Everyone's safe. Thank you. Alone, this was as far as I could go.
en.STORY_CH02_PREBOSS_03: Join the Lamplighters, Iri. We need your hands.
en.STORY_CH02_PREBOSS_04: I've been told to stay safe so many times. This is the first time I've been asked to protect. …I'll come.
en.STORY_CH02_PREBOSS_05: The recorder glowed again. Beside the first mark, a second one quietly etched itself.
en.STORY_CH02_PREBOSS_06: The second. Same as with Vera. It only appears the moment someone decides to join.
en.STORY_CH02_PREBOSS_07: That recorder's warm. …Oh, sorry. Medic's habit. I took its temperature first.
en.STORY_CH02_PREBOSS_08: Then every barrier at the central gates slammed down. A colossal ticket machine walked out backward.
en.STORY_CH02_PREBOSS_09: Checking tickets. The present is not a valid ticket.
en.STORY_CH02_PREBOSS_10: All passengers, return to before departure. Passengers who never leave have nothing to lose.
en.STORY_CH02_PREBOSS_11: If they'd never left, they'd never have been hurt. But they made it here alive.
en.STORY_CH02_PREBOSS_12: Go back before departure, and every signal sent and every answer received never happened. That's not rescue.
en.STORY_CH02_PREBOSS_13: Objections are not accepted. Ticketing will now begin.
en.STORY_CH02_PREBOSS_14: Then we'll write our own tickets. One way. Forward only.
en.STORY_CH03_CAMP_01: Night on the glass was cold. A single campfire spread into thousands of flames beneath the plain.
en.STORY_CH03_CAMP_02: Iri, look. My copy in the glass is pretending to warm up by the fire. Half a beat late.
en.STORY_CH03_CAMP_03: It really is. A little cute… and a little frightening.
en.STORY_CH03_CAMP_04: Everyone's got one. But what about the Navigator? There's nothing underfoot. No reflection, no copy.
en.STORY_CH03_CAMP_05: Everyone looked down at the Navigator's feet. The glass reflected only firelight. The spot was empty.
en.STORY_CH03_CAMP_06: …Someone whose record is locked can't be copied. The mirror rails build copies by reading records.
en.STORY_CH03_CAMP_07: Locked means someone locked it. Whether it was you, or someone else.
en.STORY_CH03_CAMP_08: Then let it stay unknown. When the day comes that you find out, we'll be beside you.
en.STORY_CH03_CAMP_09: There's a lock layer beneath the three marks. Thick. A way to open it… none, for now.
en.STORY_CH03_CAMP_10: Copy or no copy, your pulse is beating. To me, that's the surest proof.
en.STORY_CH03_CAMP_11: Also means there's no copy to dump dish duty on. Poor thing.
en.STORY_CH03_CAMP_12: Okay, that's enough mysteries for tonight. Tomorrow, the lead car. Let's wake up before our copies do.
en.STORY_CH03_HARD_INTRO_01: At the edge of the plain lay a region where the sun never set. White light shone on everything, leaving not a single shadow.
en.STORY_CH03_HARD_INTRO_02: No sunset on record. Since the Blackout, night has never once fallen here.
en.STORY_CH03_HARD_INTRO_03: Observation signals from every direction. All watching us. Recording, doing nothing else.
en.STORY_CH03_HARD_INTRO_04: Being stared at nonstop tickles. Should I wink back?
en.STORY_CH03_HARD_INTRO_05: People can't last long without sleep. I wonder what happened to those who lived here.
en.STORY_CH03_HARD_INTRO_06: Hunting signs. Spear marks, snares, campfire ash. Recent.
en.STORY_CH03_HARD_INTRO_07: One life sign slipping through the observation grid. It's poking at the grid on purpose as it moves.
en.STORY_CH03_HARD_INTRO_08: If all those eyes do is watch, then our job is simple. We give this land back its night.
en.STORY_CH03_HARD_OUTRO_01: One by one, the White Dawn Observer's eyes closed. For the first time in twelve years, the sun sank over the plain's edge.
en.STORY_CH03_HARD_OUTRO_02: …I thought if I kept watching, no one would disappear… if I just kept watching…
en.STORY_CH03_HARD_OUTRO_03: Watching alone can't hold on to anyone. You have to reach out.
en.STORY_CH03_HARD_OUTRO_04: The sky reddened, turned violet, and at last went dark. For the first time, that land had a shadow of its own.
en.STORY_CH03_HARD_OUTRO_05: …So this is night. Best time for a hunter, and I'd forgotten it for twelve years.
en.STORY_CH03_HARD_OUTRO_06: Wow… I didn't know dark could be this pretty.
en.STORY_CH03_HARD_OUTRO_07: One point two million observation records. All white sky. Tonight will be the first one that's different.
en.STORY_CH03_HARD_OUTRO_08: Name's Dran. Decided—I'm coming with you. The best prey's always right in front of you lot!
en.STORY_CH03_HARD_OUTRO_09: Welcome, Dran. Next is the drowned signal yard. It'll be a long night's walk.
en.STORY_CH03_HARD_OUTRO_10: Let's get some sleep tonight. To celebrate the night coming back.
en.STORY_CH03_INTRO_01: Beneath the afterglow storm stretched an endless plain of glass. With every step, another foot beneath the surface stepped along.
en.STORY_CH03_INTRO_02: Glass all the way to the horizon. Nothing to scout, which is nice. Nowhere to hide, which isn't.
en.STORY_CH03_INTRO_03: There. A light crossing the plain. The night train. Constant speed. No sign of stopping.
en.STORY_CH03_INTRO_04: So that's the train my patient saw. It really doesn't stop.
en.STORY_CH03_INTRO_05: The signals are strange. The same call comes from the same train twice, a beat apart.
en.STORY_CH03_INTRO_06: Isn't it an echo? The glass is so shiny, the sound must bounce too!
en.STORY_CH03_INTRO_07: An echo would be weaker. These two signals are exactly the same strength.
en.STORY_CH03_INTRO_08: Then a voice rose from within the glass underfoot. There were no speakers anywhere.
en.STORY_CH03_INTRO_09: Attention, please. Welcome to the Glass Plains Night Line.
en.STORY_CH03_INTRO_10: Copies of all passengers have boarded as well. There is no risk of loss.
en.STORY_CH03_INTRO_11: 'No risk of loss'… It sounds oddly kind, and that makes it worse.
en.STORY_CH03_INTRO_12: …Um, there's a me in the glass. But she moves a little slower than I do.
en.STORY_CH03_INTRO_13: Copies or not, if there are people on that train, we're going for them. After the train.
en.STORY_CH03_INTRO_14: Chasing a train that never stops… Fine. When it comes to running, I'm the best.
en.STORY_CH03_MID_A_01: Mirror panels along the tracks replayed the battle just fought. The reflections stepped out of the glass.
en.STORY_CH03_MID_A_02: It's copying our combat records. Movements, weapons, even our habits.
en.STORY_CH03_MID_A_03: It'd be awkward if my copy shoots better than me. Matter of pride.
en.STORY_CH03_MID_A_04: …That copy's off. It's running down the right-hand path I almost took earlier.
en.STORY_CH03_MID_A_05: It copied the choices we abandoned. Even what we didn't do was on record.
en.STORY_CH03_MID_A_06: Then the overcharged charge I held back earlier… Whoa, she's actually doing it.
en.STORY_CH03_MID_A_07: Maeru, your copy is… running back the way we came. Alone, into the dark.
en.STORY_CH03_MID_A_08: …The direction I couldn't turn back to that day. It doesn't matter. Even regrets are ours. We deal with them ourselves.
en.STORY_CH03_MID_A_09: The night train's whistle sounded in the distance. As one, the copies turned toward it.
en.STORY_CH03_MID_A_10: The copies are all converging on the train. That's the heart of the duplication.
en.STORY_CH03_MID_B_01: The copies fell half a beat late. In that half beat, Toa carved one more mark.
en.STORY_CH03_MID_B_02: You pass. All on the beat. Sorry for doubting you. Out here, you verify before you say hello.
en.STORY_CH03_MID_B_03: Toa. Technician. The copies are perfect—form and voice. They're just always half a beat behind.
en.STORY_CH03_MID_B_04: And you've been using that half beat to tell the real trains from the copies?
en.STORY_CH03_MID_B_05: Yes. I carve relay marks only on the real ones. Follow a marked train, and you'll find people.
en.STORY_CH03_MID_B_06: I'm picking up the marks. Eighteen across the plain. …You carved all of them alone?
en.STORY_CH03_MID_B_08: Will you carve those marks with the Lamplighters? If every mark means a person.
en.STORY_CH03_MID_B_09: …Half a beat is enough to prove what's real. Let's write that proof together.
en.STORY_CH03_MID_B_10: The recorder glowed. As the third mark etched itself, Toa narrowed her eyes.
en.STORY_CH03_MID_B_11: Top-tier Directorate spec. Can I take it apart later? …Joking. Next mark first.
en.STORY_CH03_OUTRO_01: As the Glass Marshal crumbled, every mirror in the lead car shattered at once. The shards drifted down like quiet snow.
en.STORY_CH03_OUTRO_02: …Copies don't get hurt… so if everyone were a copy… no one would…
en.STORY_CH03_OUTRO_03: So no one would get hurt. …In a way no one could ever heal from.
en.STORY_CH03_OUTRO_04: Two hundred-odd passengers trapped behind the mirrors gasped for air, one after another. Every one of them was warm.
en.STORY_CH03_OUTRO_05: They're all real! They're warm! Iri, check their pulses!
en.STORY_CH03_OUTRO_06: All the distress calls are back with their originals. …Wait, there's one more. A very old one.
en.STORY_CH03_OUTRO_07: This is the drowned signal yard. There are still people here. Anyone, if you can hear…
en.STORY_CH03_OUTRO_08: …There's a mark inside this signal. It's mine.
en.STORY_CH03_OUTRO_09: Your mark is carrying that call? When did you carve it?
en.STORY_CH03_OUTRO_10: On the only train that ever made it off the plain. That train… went all the way there.
en.STORY_CH03_OUTRO_11: The copy service has ended. Of course, Navigator, you never needed it.
en.STORY_CH03_OUTRO_13: Ignore it. The call comes first. We head for the drowned signal yard. Toa, we'll find your train too.
en.STORY_CH03_OUTRO_14: …Right. Where there's a mark, there are people.
en.STORY_CH03_PREBOSS_01: When the lead car's doors opened, walls and floor were all mirror. Hundreds of Lamplighters raised their weapons in unison.
en.STORY_CH03_PREBOSS_02: I count about twenty Roans. The best one's right here, of course.
en.STORY_CH03_PREBOSS_03: Checking the beat. Most are half a beat late. …But a few are on time. They've stolen the originals' rhythm.
en.STORY_CH03_PREBOSS_04: The passengers' distress calls are trapped in the mirrors. Two hundred-odd real passengers are behind them.
en.STORY_CH03_PREBOSS_05: At the center of the mirrors, the Glass Marshal rose, decorated with medals. The Lamplighters' faces flickered across its body.
en.STORY_CH03_PREBOSS_06: Commencing inspection. All passengers will be aligned to a single reflection.
en.STORY_CH03_PREBOSS_07: Originals are unnecessary. Copies do not get hurt, do not age, and do not lose.
en.STORY_CH03_PREBOSS_08: They don't get hurt? That means they don't need healing—not that they're alive.
en.STORY_CH03_PREBOSS_09: My copy only does the charges I held back. I'm the one who held back. That's what makes me me!
en.STORY_CH03_PREBOSS_10: That half beat is the time it takes to choose. Copies don't have it. Only originals can choose.
en.STORY_CH03_PREBOSS_11: Choice is an error. Errors will be aligned.
en.STORY_CH03_PREBOSS_12: …No reflection. Not subject to alignment. Navigator, please stand aside.
en.STORY_CH03_PREBOSS_13: Three, two, one. …Good. Your beat doesn't waver.
en.STORY_CH03_PREBOSS_14: Those errors brought us here. Lamplighters—move on the original beat.
en.STORY_CH03_PREBOSS_15: Hundreds of mirrors, but only one center. One shot's enough.
en.STORY_CH04_CAMP_01: Wet diving suits hung over the fire. The smell of brine and smoke filled the signal yard's night.
en.STORY_CH04_CAMP_02: Chief. Down there, you dove in ahead of me. That's no job for a commander.
en.STORY_CH04_CAMP_03: …I figured being late once was enough.
en.STORY_CH04_CAMP_05: That rescue operation. On a collapsing platform, I boarded the train without Sio.
en.STORY_CH04_CAMP_06: I can't bring all of that night out yet. What's left is one empty seat.
en.STORY_CH04_CAMP_07: …So we're both people who arrived too late.
en.STORY_CH04_CAMP_08: Which is why this time, we won't be. Neither of us.
en.STORY_CH04_CAMP_09: …Funny. With someone beside me, I think about the water less.
en.STORY_CH04_CAMP_10: Thanks. …It's warm. It's been a while.
en.STORY_CH04_CAMP_11: Everyone, a moment. The switchyard water level's been rising all night. The records floor goes under first.
en.STORY_CH04_CAMP_12: Then we go down before dawn. This time, we won't be late.
en.STORY_CH04_HARD_INTRO_01: Beneath the deep floodgate, a deeper shaft continued. In the watery light, a single semaphore blinked slowly.
en.STORY_CH04_HARD_INTRO_02: Decoding the blinks. Three short, three long. 'Do not approach.' Over and over.
en.STORY_CH04_HARD_INTRO_03: …That's the signal rescuers hate most. Wherever it says don't come, someone's always there.
en.STORY_CH04_HARD_INTRO_04: One life sign near the semaphore. Very slow breathing. The kind for holding out underwater.
en.STORY_CH04_HARD_INTRO_05: That's dive breathing. Medics use it. Someone's working down there.
en.STORY_CH04_HARD_INTRO_06: It says don't come, but someone's there? Then we have to go!
en.STORY_CH04_HARD_INTRO_07: We cross the 'do not approach.' Liv, take point. You know the water best.
en.STORY_CH04_HARD_INTRO_08: Leave it to me. This time, I'll be first to arrive.
en.STORY_CH04_HARD_OUTRO_01: The Abyssal Semaphore's light faded. For a moment, the water sank into total darkness.
en.STORY_CH04_HARD_OUTRO_02: …Do not come… if you come here… you can never go back…
en.STORY_CH04_HARD_OUTRO_03: …I knew it. It wasn't trying to drive anyone away. It was trying to protect them.
en.STORY_CH04_HARD_OUTRO_04: The circuits still work. I can rewrite the blink pattern. What should it say?
en.STORY_CH04_HARD_OUTRO_05: 'You may return.' …The words every rescuer most wanted to say.
en.STORY_CH04_HARD_OUTRO_06: The semaphore lit again. Two short, one long. Its gentle light spread through the water to the surface.
en.STORY_CH04_HARD_OUTRO_07: …It's beautiful. With this signal, everyone can take a deep breath and come up.
en.STORY_CH04_HARD_OUTRO_08: Could I… come with you? I'll follow, slowly.
en.STORY_CH04_HARD_OUTRO_09: Slow is fine. We have too many fast ones anyway. You'll balance us out.
en.STORY_CH04_HARD_OUTRO_10: Welcome, Merin. We'll see you on the surface.
en.STORY_CH04_INTRO_01: The tracks ran down into black water. Beneath the surface, a signal box's red lamp blinked like a slow pulse.
en.STORY_CH04_INTRO_02: There are still people here. There are still… people here.
en.STORY_CH04_INTRO_03: Same sentence, same interval. Once every forty seconds. Not once missed in twelve years.
en.STORY_CH04_INTRO_04: It's like that mimicry at the end of the line. Is this an echoform too?
en.STORY_CH04_INTRO_05: No. Echoform signals carry no marks. This one's using my mark as its reception path.
en.STORY_CH04_INTRO_06: So someone's turned Toa's marked train into a relay. The source is under that water.
en.STORY_CH04_INTRO_07: Water this cold… could anyone survive twelve years in it?
en.STORY_CH04_INTRO_08: …And there's no breathing after the call. A human signal should breathe.
en.STORY_CH04_INTRO_09: The water trembled. A voice rose from a submerged speaker and burst like bubbles.
en.STORY_CH04_INTRO_10: Attention, please. Your request for rescue has been received.
en.STORY_CH04_INTRO_11: No rescue team will be dispatched. Passengers, please step back from the water's edge.
en.STORY_CH04_INTRO_12: No rescue team? That's meant for our ears, isn't it?
en.STORY_CH04_INTRO_13: We are the rescue team. We decide whether we go.
en.STORY_CH04_INTRO_14: Iri, prep for hypothermia. Roan, find a drained track. If anyone's down there, we reach them today.
en.STORY_CH04_MID_A_01: In the half-flooded control room, one console was still on. The same sentence scrolled up its screen without end.
en.STORY_CH04_MID_A_02: The source is this console. Not a person—the control log is replaying the call by itself.
en.STORY_CH04_MID_A_03: Log's open. Closure day entry: 'Water limit exceeded. Rescue dispatch impossible. Rescue abandoned.'
en.STORY_CH04_MID_A_04: Since then, it's replayed the last call it received every forty seconds. For twelve years.
en.STORY_CH04_MID_A_05: The log that gave up on rescue kept listening to the voice it gave up on. Like a punishment.
en.STORY_CH04_MID_A_06: So there's no one here? We can't save anyone?
en.STORY_CH04_MID_A_07: A machine that can't forget who it failed to save. More human than most people.
en.STORY_CH04_MID_A_08: Calling this a wasted trip… That voice sounded so real, though.
en.STORY_CH04_MID_A_09: It's not wasted. Records need rescuing too.
en.STORY_CH04_MID_A_10: Whatever happened to the owner of that voice, this log knows to the end. We go all the way down.
en.STORY_CH04_MID_B_01: The clank of the floodgate lock rang through the water. Only then did Liv let go and sink to the floor.
en.STORY_CH04_MID_B_02: Give me your arm. …Your muscles are about to tear. How long did you hold that?
en.STORY_CH04_MID_B_03: A day? Three? I don't know. I couldn't let go in case someone was behind that gate.
en.STORY_CH04_MID_B_04: Liv. Dive rescue. Twelve years ago, I came to this yard on a rescue. …Too late.
en.STORY_CH04_MID_B_05: By the time I arrived, the live calls had already stopped. All that was left was that recording.
en.STORY_CH04_MID_B_06: It felt like someone who came late had no right to leave. So I stayed.
en.STORY_CH04_MID_B_07: If you stop because you were late, the road to those people stops too. Come with us, Liv.
en.STORY_CH04_MID_B_08: …Even a late rescue, I'll see it through. This time, I want to be the one who arrives.
en.STORY_CH04_MID_B_09: The recorder glowed for the fourth time. On a soaked wrist, the new mark was strangely warm.
en.STORY_CH04_MID_B_10: Four. A pattern's starting to show. …I'm not sure yet, though.
en.STORY_CH04_MID_B_11: The Tidal Switchmaster is below. It's raising the water to sink the records. Let's go.
en.STORY_CH04_OUTRO_01: When the Switchmaster's gears stopped, the water slowly drained. Soaked record crates surfaced one by one.
en.STORY_CH04_OUTRO_02: …To keep hearing voices I couldn't save… it was… too painful…
en.STORY_CH04_OUTRO_03: It hurt. That's why it tried to sink it all. …A machine that knew pain.
en.STORY_CH04_OUTRO_04: Restoring rescue records. Four hundred twelve. Every call has a final forwarding address.
en.STORY_CH04_OUTRO_05: Final destination… the Ashen City blockade control. These should have been forwarded there.
en.STORY_CH04_OUTRO_06: Then I'll carry them. Late or not, I'll deliver. Even if no one's left to receive them—to the very end.
en.STORY_CH04_OUTRO_07: Liv shouldered the wet record crates. Only then did the red lamp under the water go out.
en.STORY_CH04_OUTRO_09: That voice doesn't have to wait anymore. We're taking it with us.
en.STORY_CH04_OUTRO_11: The next stop is the Ashen City. As it is a sealed zone, Navigator, please be careful with your memories.
en.STORY_CH04_OUTRO_12: 'Careful with your memories'… Is that a warning, or a threat?
en.STORY_CH04_OUTRO_13: Both, probably. Which is exactly why we have to go.
en.STORY_CH04_OUTRO_14: If it's blockade control, the doors will be shut. I'll knock until they open.
en.STORY_CH04_PREBOSS_01: The lowest switchyard was full of giant floodgate gears. With every turn, the water rose another hand's breadth.
en.STORY_CH04_PREBOSS_02: Water rising two centimeters a minute. Twelve minutes until the records room.
en.STORY_CH04_PREBOSS_03: Over four hundred rescue records in there. Who called, when it was received, why no one went—all of it.
en.STORY_CH04_PREBOSS_04: In the middle of the gears, the Switchmaster rose. Its rusted switch-arms all swung at once.
en.STORY_CH04_PREBOSS_05: Commencing water-level rise procedure. When the records sink, so does regret.
en.STORY_CH04_PREBOSS_06: Voices that could not be saved will no longer be played. This measure benefits everyone.
en.STORY_CH04_PREBOSS_07: Drown the regret? There are people in those records. Names. Last words!
en.STORY_CH04_PREBOSS_08: Forgetting would be easier. But that's not healing. That's burying a wound underwater.
en.STORY_CH04_PREBOSS_09: If I overcharge, will the water boil? …Probably not. I'll just smash it!
en.STORY_CH04_PREBOSS_10: However many gears, there's only one axle. Hit that and we're done.
en.STORY_CH04_PREBOSS_11: Rescue personnel, please exit. This area has already been abandoned.
en.STORY_CH04_PREBOSS_12: Giving up once, twelve years ago, was enough. This time we go all the way.
en.STORY_CH04_PREBOSS_13: …Good. This time I don't have to hold on alone.
en.STORY_CH04_PREBOSS_14: I'll open the records room gate. We'll protect the records.
en.STORY_CH04_PREBOSS_15: Twelve minutes. We finish before the records go under. Water or not—don't be late.
en.STORY_CH05_CAMP_01: Forty tents went up in a dead station at the corridor's end. Barley porridge cut through the smell of ash.
en.STORY_CH05_CAMP_02: Iri, the grandmother in tent three. Her lungs sound rough. Can we compare records?
en.STORY_CH05_CAMP_03: Mine says her breathing's fine… oh, the ash exposure date is off. Yours is right.
en.STORY_CH05_CAMP_04: It's faster with two. Alone, I spent every night checking for mistakes.
en.STORY_CH05_CAMP_05: All right, let's lift the mood. What sells best in a city where it rains ash? Umbrellas!
en.STORY_CH05_CAMP_06: No one laughed. Between the tents, someone kept crying quietly.
en.STORY_CH05_CAMP_08: These people knocked on a door for twelve years. An umbrella joke won't cover that.
en.STORY_CH05_CAMP_09: I know. That's why I tried. Felt like if I didn't do something, the weight would flatten me.
en.STORY_CH05_CAMP_10: …Thanks, Navigator. I'll have a proper joke ready next time.
en.STORY_CH05_CAMP_11: You're the first to ask their names here. Everyone's only ever been a number.
en.STORY_CH05_CAMP_12: The citadel counts these people as numbers. We count them by name. Tomorrow, we show it the difference.
en.STORY_CH05_HARD_INTRO_01: Beneath the wall, the ash stopped. Collapsed galleries and a judge's bench lined up in the dark.
en.STORY_CH05_HARD_INTRO_02: A courtroom. It opened the day after the Blackout. And the defendants are… all witnesses.
en.STORY_CH05_HARD_INTRO_03: Some of my patients are on it. Just for saying what they saw.
en.STORY_CH05_HARD_INTRO_04: A trial that punishes the witnesses. That's backward from start to finish.
en.STORY_CH05_HARD_INTRO_05: There's still a signal running at the bench. The verdicts never stopped.
en.STORY_CH05_HARD_INTRO_06: Targeting tone from the battery above. Someone has us in their sights.
en.STORY_CH05_HARD_INTRO_07: We stop the verdicts. A court that punishes witnesses closes today.
en.STORY_CH05_HARD_OUTRO_01: The bench went dark. Thousands of sealed boxes opened at once, and the rustle of paper filled the court.
en.STORY_CH05_HARD_OUTRO_02: …If dangerous memories stay locked away, the city can sleep quietly…
en.STORY_CH05_HARD_OUTRO_03: Over four thousand testimonies. Their classification is flipping from 'Hazard' to 'Public.'
en.STORY_CH05_HARD_OUTRO_04: Now what these people saw can be heard outside the city, too.
en.STORY_CH05_HARD_OUTRO_05: …So you really did open the gate. I'm not apologizing for aiming at you. Checking is my job.
en.STORY_CH05_HARD_OUTRO_06: But I'll watch the sky for you. Seems an anti-air gunner still has work to do.
en.STORY_CH05_HARD_OUTRO_07: I'll apologize for critiquing your angle. Call it even for the shot I took.
en.STORY_CH05_HARD_OUTRO_08: Not even. When I outshoot you, then we're even.
en.STORY_CH05_HARD_OUTRO_09: The testimony can walk on its own now. We go to the bridge.
en.STORY_CH05_INTRO_01: Ash fell like snow. For twelve years, someone had been knocking on the Ashen City's walls from the inside.
en.STORY_CH05_INTRO_02: This is the last address on the drowned yard's records. I know we're late. It still gets delivered.
en.STORY_CH05_INTRO_03: The knocking isn't evenly spaced. That's not a machine's rhythm. Those are hands.
en.STORY_CH05_INTRO_04: Gate's in lockdown. Not a crack. And the ash is too hot to climb over.
en.STORY_CH05_INTRO_05: They've been knocking and nobody opened up? For twelve years?
en.STORY_CH05_INTRO_06: Hundreds of signals behind the wall. All sending the same words: 'Please listen.'
en.STORY_CH05_INTRO_07: Attention, please. The Ashen City blockade exists for your protection.
en.STORY_CH05_INTRO_08: Navigator, kindly remain outside the walls. The count inside has already been completed.
en.STORY_CH05_INTRO_09: 'The count is complete.' Talks about people like warehouse stock.
en.STORY_CH05_INTRO_10: The knocking's getting weaker. That means the hands are, too.
en.STORY_CH05_INTRO_11: When the broadcast says stay, we go toward the knocking.
en.STORY_CH05_INTRO_12: There's a drainage channel under the wall. One body wide. We go in single file.
en.STORY_CH05_INTRO_13: One at a time in, and every one of us out. First, we count who's inside.
en.STORY_CH05_MID_A_01: The first quarantine door smelled of rust. Its seal read not 'Infection Risk' but 'Testimony in Storage.'
en.STORY_CH05_MID_A_02: Not one infection record. Every quarantine order gives the same reason: 'Witness.'
en.STORY_CH05_MID_A_03: …They locked people up not for sickness, but for what they saw?
en.STORY_CH05_MID_A_04: You don't have to open the door. Just listen. To what we saw.
en.STORY_CH05_MID_A_05: That night, every light in the control tower came on at once. And someone signed.
en.STORY_CH05_MID_A_07: We never saw a face. The whole city saw that light, and the next day the gates closed.
en.STORY_CH05_MID_A_08: So a whole city became a witness. And got locked up whole.
en.STORY_CH05_MID_A_09: Testimony isn't contagious. We find a way to open these doors. Air for these people comes first.
en.STORY_CH05_MID_A_10: There's a cluster of injured signals deeper in. Someone inside the blockade is still treating them.
en.STORY_CH05_MID_B_01: When the last stitch was tied, twenty-three people behind the barricade breathed evenly.
en.STORY_CH05_MID_B_02: They can be moved now. I'm Seon, field medic for this sector. Thank you for holding the line.
en.STORY_CH05_MID_B_03: Twenty-three, on your own? Where did you even find medicine and bandages?
en.STORY_CH05_MID_B_04: A discarded medical register. The citadel filed it as trash, but it lists who's lying where.
en.STORY_CH05_MID_B_05: Overlay the register on the map and… one corridor runs outside the citadel's firing range.
en.STORY_CH05_MID_B_06: Then we can separate the survivor wards from the corridor. The citadel counts people. It doesn't know who's sick.
en.STORY_CH05_MID_B_07: Lead the evacuation. We'll open the way ahead.
en.STORY_CH05_MID_B_08: No, I'll take the rear. I need eyes on the very last patient. Which means I'm coming with you.
en.STORY_CH05_MID_B_09: The voyage recorder glowed. Beside the first four marks, a fifth etched itself quietly.
en.STORY_CH05_MID_B_10: Number five. One more every time someone joins. Awfully diligent for a coincidence.
en.STORY_CH05_MID_B_11: We'll work out what it means later. Move the column before the corridor closes.
en.STORY_CH05_OUTRO_01: One by one the gunports went cold. Past the ash, the groan of the gate opening rang out for the first time in twelve years.
en.STORY_CH05_OUTRO_02: …Ending the count. If everyone could be counted, then no one would ever vanish…
en.STORY_CH05_OUTRO_03: The knocking hands fell still. Two thousand four hundred and ten people breathed air from beyond the wall.
en.STORY_CH05_OUTRO_04: Slowly, slowly! If walking's hard, raise your hand. I'll come to you.
en.STORY_CH05_OUTRO_05: …Late, but delivered. The drowned yard's records are in the blockade control office.
en.STORY_CH05_OUTRO_06: The city's reserve power is free. But the flow is wrong. It's all being drawn northeast.
en.STORY_CH05_OUTRO_07: Toward Skybridge. The evacuation power is rerouting there. Something is feeding on it.
en.STORY_CH05_OUTRO_08: Navigator, on that night, this city witnessed your command.
en.STORY_CH05_OUTRO_09: The broadcast ended there. Every gaze in the square slowly turned to the Navigator.
en.STORY_CH05_OUTRO_10: …A command? The Navigator? What is that supposed to mean?
en.STORY_CH05_OUTRO_11: It's trying to shake us. Speaking as a signal tracker, that's a broadcast, not evidence.
en.STORY_CH05_OUTRO_12: Whatever anyone did that night, the one who opened this gate today was the Navigator. I saw that myself.
en.STORY_CH05_OUTRO_13: I'll take down the testimony. Once it's all gathered, there's time enough to judge.
en.STORY_CH05_OUTRO_14: We head for Skybridge. It's a bridge these people will have to cross someday.
en.STORY_CH05_PREBOSS_01: Over a hundred citadel gunports swung toward the corridor at once. The air grew so heavy the ash seemed to stop falling.
en.STORY_CH05_PREBOSS_02: Passengers, please be advised. The survivor count is complete.
en.STORY_CH05_PREBOSS_03: Total: two thousand four hundred and ten. Threat level: maximum. The corridor is now designated a bombardment target.
en.STORY_CH05_PREBOSS_04: Twenty-four hundred… That's far more than I counted. There were people in other wards, too.
en.STORY_CH05_PREBOSS_05: Its threat formula is twisted. The more people, the higher it goes. Being alive is the threat.
en.STORY_CH05_PREBOSS_06: Why count people just to shoot them? The citadel was built to protect this city!
en.STORY_CH05_PREBOSS_07: Anyone moving beyond the blockade is unverified. Unverified persons cannot be protected.
en.STORY_CH05_PREBOSS_08: So if you can't protect them, you erase them? Even I, who came too late, never said that.
en.STORY_CH05_PREBOSS_09: A hundred gunports. I only need one shot. Question is who goes first.
en.STORY_CH05_PREBOSS_10: I'll hold the column together from the back. Not one person strays.
en.STORY_CH05_PREBOSS_11: Fully overcharged! I'll short out those gunports one by one!
en.STORY_CH05_PREBOSS_12: I'll open the way. Right to the citadel's feet.
en.STORY_CH05_PREBOSS_13: We stand in front of the corridor. Before any shell can count a single person, we're there.
en.STORY_CH06_CAMP_01: Beneath a pylon past the windless stretch, two battery lamps glowed side by side. For once, the wind was still.
en.STORY_CH06_CAMP_02: Cut the charge by a hair and the trajectory flattens. Isn't that better for hitting the pillars?
en.STORY_CH06_CAMP_03: Flatten it and the wind takes it. Better to fire one more. Gunners don't hoard shells.
en.STORY_CH06_CAMP_04: I'm a one-shot kind of gunner. Difference in philosophy.
en.STORY_CH06_CAMP_05: Not philosophy. Supply. Your Lamplighters are poor.
en.STORY_CH06_CAMP_06: Maeru left the fire and sat beside the Navigator. For a while she only watched the dark beyond the bridge.
en.STORY_CH06_CAMP_07: What Control said in the Ashen City. That the city witnessed your command that night. Does it bother you?
en.STORY_CH06_CAMP_08: You can be honest. It's just the two of us.
en.STORY_CH06_CAMP_09: …All right. I won't put anyone on trial for something they can't remember. Not me.
en.STORY_CH06_CAMP_10: Whatever happened that night, you're the one who got that column across today.
en.STORY_CH06_CAMP_11: You want to know. …I thought you might say that. It's a brave answer, and a frightening one.
en.STORY_CH06_CAMP_12: Fine. Wherever the truth is, we look for it together. Just don't go looking alone.
en.STORY_CH06_CAMP_13: I don't know all of that night either. I never even learned who we were sent to bring back.
en.STORY_CH06_CAMP_14: So let's not measure each other by what we don't know. Tomorrow, the end of the bridge.
en.STORY_CH06_HARD_INTRO_01: Below the bridge, all sound vanished. In the eye of the storm, a vast shadow was gathering lightning.
en.STORY_CH06_HARD_INTRO_02: The storm's core. The pressure's abnormally low. Something is holding the storm in place.
en.STORY_CH06_HARD_INTRO_03: That shadow is a pre-Blackout weather engine. It was built to scatter storms.
en.STORY_CH06_HARD_INTRO_04: Instead it gathered them up. Twelve years' worth.
en.STORY_CH06_HARD_INTRO_05: I hear bolts being tightened on the pylon. In this wind, who…?
en.STORY_CH06_HARD_INTRO_06: Repairs in the middle of a storm? Whoever that is, their circuits must be tougher than mine.
en.STORY_CH06_HARD_INTRO_07: We check that sound first. If there's a person in this storm, we bring them out first.
en.STORY_CH06_HARD_OUTRO_01: The eye of the storm broke apart. Through the torn clouds, small cold lights appeared one by one.
en.STORY_CH06_HARD_OUTRO_02: …If I held the storm here, the bridge would never shake…
en.STORY_CH06_HARD_OUTRO_04: No sightings recorded since the Blackout. First time in twelve years.
en.STORY_CH06_HARD_OUTRO_05: …Well, now. Twelve years staring at bolts, and I forgot to look up.
en.STORY_CH06_HARD_OUTRO_06: The pylon can hold itself now. Think I'll hold you lot up instead. Slow and sturdy.
en.STORY_CH06_HARD_OUTRO_07: Gunners once took their bearings from the stars. Now we can again.
en.STORY_CH06_HARD_OUTRO_08: I wonder if the people who crossed can see them. I hope they're all looking up.
en.STORY_CH06_HARD_OUTRO_09: If we can see the stars, we can find our way. North.
en.STORY_CH06_INTRO_01: Lightning struck every three seconds. Skybridge, floating above the clouds, appeared only in its flashes.
en.STORY_CH06_INTRO_02: Bridge length: forty-two hundred meters. Strike interval: 3.1 seconds. Even without stopping, you'd take twenty hits.
en.STORY_CH06_INTRO_03: There's an evacuation column at the bridgehead. The tents are worn. They've been here for years.
en.STORY_CH06_INTRO_04: People who tried to cross and turned back. Every tent has an empty spot.
en.STORY_CH06_INTRO_05: We tried once a year. Every time, a few of us never reached the other side.
en.STORY_CH06_INTRO_06: Lightning's my specialty! Should I go first and soak up the hits?
en.STORY_CH06_INTRO_07: Eda, that's not a specialty, that's reckless. If you play lightning rod, who do we bring home?
en.STORY_CH06_INTRO_08: Attention, please. Skybridge tolls are now being collected.
en.STORY_CH06_INTRO_09: The Navigator is exempt. All other passengers, please pay the designated fare.
en.STORY_CH06_INTRO_10: Exempt. Just the Navigator. …That broadcast is getting shameless about its favorites.
en.STORY_CH06_INTRO_11: I'm reading a power draw at the far end. The Ashen City's power is being sucked over there.
en.STORY_CH06_INTRO_12: First we find out what the fare is. If it's lives, we don't pay a cent.
en.STORY_CH06_INTRO_13: Thirty-two patients in that column. They can't wait here another year.
en.STORY_CH06_INTRO_14: Roan, to the first pylon. Measure a path between the strikes.
en.STORY_CH06_MID_A_01: The first pylon's control box was hot. Each strike ticked a number on its gauge up by one.
en.STORY_CH06_MID_A_02: One strike, one tick. This isn't weather. It's a device counting everyone who crosses.
en.STORY_CH06_MID_A_03: An automatic toll collector, installed when the bridge opened. It used to charge for electricity.
en.STORY_CH06_MID_A_04: But these people's vital signs… dropped a little every time they crossed. It's all in the records.
en.STORY_CH06_MID_A_05: Their heart rates step down like stairs. It's collecting the fare from people, not power.
en.STORY_CH06_MID_A_06: My sister crossed three times. On the third, she collapsed at the far end.
