en.STORY_CH06_MID_A_07: …So the toll accumulates. The more you cross, the less of you is left.
en.STORY_CH06_MID_A_08: Then everyone crosses in one go. No one crosses twice.
en.STORY_CH06_MID_A_09: Listen, cannon fire from the battery. Someone's fighting the lightning alone.
en.STORY_CH06_MID_B_01: On the ninetieth second, the battery roared. Three lightning pillars took shells at once and went dark.
en.STORY_CH06_MID_B_02: Impact confirmed. I laid the coordinates over the pillars. There will be one window where the wind dies.
en.STORY_CH06_MID_B_03: Windless window: two hundred forty seconds. Tight for the whole column.
en.STORY_CH06_MID_B_04: Not tight. Precise. The math is done. They need only keep pace.
en.STORY_CH06_MID_B_05: Shooting out lightning. Looks like someone suits 'one shot is enough' better than I do.
en.STORY_CH06_MID_B_06: One was never enough. I fired three hundred. I've had this bridge in my sights alone for twelve years.
en.STORY_CH06_MID_B_08: A cannon is precise, but it can't tell who's still waiting to cross. For that, I needed human ears.
en.STORY_CH06_MID_B_09: You have those ears. Put this battery in your formation. I'll cover you to the end of the bridge.
en.STORY_CH06_MID_B_10: The voyage recorder glowed. As the sixth mark etched itself, the lightning fell a beat late.
en.STORY_CH06_MID_B_11: Wake the column. In two hundred forty seconds, we cross, and no one stays behind.
en.STORY_CH06_OUTRO_01: The substation spat its last sparks. With the lightning gone, forty-two hundred meters of bridge fell silent for the first time.
en.STORY_CH06_OUTRO_02: …Bridge release canceled. If no one ever crossed, then no one would ever fall…
en.STORY_CH06_OUTRO_03: Twelve bolts, welded. Bridge anchored. Confirmed.
en.STORY_CH06_OUTRO_04: The column's last cart reached the far end. More than a thousand people crossed, and not one was missing.
en.STORY_CH06_OUTRO_05: The Ashen City power the substation was devouring is flowing back. The bridge lights will reach the city now.
en.STORY_CH06_OUTRO_06: The bridge my sister never finished… I crossed it. On my own feet.
en.STORY_CH06_OUTRO_07: Roll check complete. No one's missing. No one.
en.STORY_CH06_OUTRO_08: Found the Archon's original directive: 'Prevent another bridge collapse.' It fell once, on the day of the Blackout.
en.STORY_CH06_OUTRO_09: That's when it started counting people. Fewer crossings, more safety.
en.STORY_CH06_OUTRO_10: Until nobody could cross at all. …The walls built with good intentions are always the tallest.
en.STORY_CH06_OUTRO_11: Wait. I'm picking up a broadcast from the northern snowfield. Same counting order. Something's counting people there too.
en.STORY_CH06_OUTRO_12: The northern snowfield line is under standby procedure. Navigator, there is no need to hurry.
en.STORY_CH06_OUTRO_13: When the broadcast says there's no need to hurry, that means we hurry.
en.STORY_CH06_OUTRO_14: The snowfield. My barrels will freeze. I'll go anyway. My ears are on your side now.
en.STORY_CH06_OUTRO_15: North. If someone's waiting there, they've already waited far too long.
en.STORY_CH06_PREBOSS_01: The central substation. The air reeked of hot iron, and the bridge underfoot began to tilt with a groan.
en.STORY_CH06_PREBOSS_02: Crossing notice. Today's crossings have exceeded the permitted load.
en.STORY_CH06_PREBOSS_03: Without travelers, there is no load. Commencing bridge release.
en.STORY_CH06_PREBOSS_04: The anchor bolts are coming loose! Half the column is still on the bridge!
en.STORY_CH06_PREBOSS_05: The patients are at the back. They can't run!
en.STORY_CH06_PREBOSS_06: Battery, switch targets. I'll weld all twelve bolts with lightning. I need time to calculate.
en.STORY_CH06_PREBOSS_07: There are passengers with unpaid fares. They will be settled along with the bridge.
en.STORY_CH06_PREBOSS_08: Settled? You call dropping people with the bridge 'settling'?
en.STORY_CH06_PREBOSS_09: Adeline, do your math. I'll pin that thing down meanwhile. With two gunners, even lightning waits its turn.
en.STORY_CH06_PREBOSS_10: Lightning versus lightning? Today I'll show you exactly who wins!
en.STORY_CH06_PREBOSS_11: I'll keep the column on the radio. I'll keep telling them not to stop.
en.STORY_CH06_PREBOSS_12: Forty meters to the substation. I'll open a path between the strikes.
en.STORY_CH06_PREBOSS_13: We bring that down before it brings down the bridge. Go.
en.STORY_CH07_CAMP_01: In the ice cave, Eda's fingertips flashed blue. Smoke rose from the wet wood first, then flame.
en.STORY_CH07_CAMP_02: Overcharge ignition, success! See? My circuits don't die just because it's cold!
en.STORY_CH07_CAMP_03: But your fingertips are frozen, Eda. Give them here. I'll warm them while I bandage.
en.STORY_CH07_CAMP_04: Kir, did you see the broadcast's waves? There are others layered inside the eleven-second cycle. Multiple voices.
en.STORY_CH07_CAMP_05: I saw. Twenty-six. Not synthetic. There's breathing. Synthetic voices don't breathe.
en.STORY_CH07_CAMP_06: Navigator. If a standby order came down, would you wait, or walk out?
en.STORY_CH07_CAMP_07: Rational. You have to stay alive to refuse the next order, too.
en.STORY_CH07_CAMP_08: …Irrational. And yet every one of these Lamplighters answers the same way.
en.STORY_CH07_CAMP_09: Across the fire, Soren approached Maeru. She kept her voice low, but the cave was small.
en.STORY_CH07_CAMP_10: Captain. …Can I bring up Sio? Listening to this broadcast keeps making me think of her.
en.STORY_CH07_CAMP_11: …Not now. That broadcast is too loud. After we shut it off.
en.STORY_CH07_CAMP_12: Got it. Then let's shut it off fast. No hesitating.
en.STORY_CH07_HARD_INTRO_01: One step, and the world was erased. No sky, no ground, only white light, equally bright in every direction.
en.STORY_CH07_HARD_INTRO_02: …I can't tell up from down. Or even where my feet are.
en.STORY_CH07_HARD_INTRO_03: Whiteout. A transmitter is broadcasting every bearing at equal strength. Our ears went blind before our eyes.
en.STORY_CH07_HARD_INTRO_04: The compass needle won't stop spinning. Direction itself is being erased.
en.STORY_CH07_HARD_INTRO_05: I can't fire in a place like this. There's no direction to aim.
en.STORY_CH07_HARD_INTRO_06: Everyone, hold hands. If we get separated here, we'll never find each other.
en.STORY_CH07_HARD_INTRO_07: Rope up. Kir takes the lead. I take the rear.
en.STORY_CH07_HARD_OUTRO_01: When the transmitter broke, the white lifted. Far away, a ridgeline emerged as a dark stroke.
en.STORY_CH07_HARD_OUTRO_02: …If every road shone the same, no one could take the wrong one…
en.STORY_CH07_HARD_OUTRO_04: One bearing. Real. The sound of wind against the mountain.
en.STORY_CH07_HARD_OUTRO_05: …A mountain. Twelve years, and I never saw it. It was right in front of me.
en.STORY_CH07_HARD_OUTRO_06: Kian laughed, briefly. It lasted only as long as her breath hung in the air, but no one missed it.
en.STORY_CH07_HARD_OUTRO_07: What are you staring at? I can laugh. …I'll come along. I want to see up close whether your rescue actually shows up.
en.STORY_CH07_HARD_OUTRO_08: Then watch from right up front. This time, it does.
en.STORY_CH07_HARD_OUTRO_09: We have our bearings back. Now we chase that red light in the sky.
en.STORY_CH07_INTRO_01: The blizzard swallowed every sound but one: a broadcast that rang across the entire snowfield.
en.STORY_CH07_INTRO_02: Eleven-second cycle. One phrase: 'Please stand by.' Not a single letter has changed in twelve years.
en.STORY_CH07_INTRO_03: My barrels are starting to freeze. In this cold, three shots an hour is the limit.
en.STORY_CH07_INTRO_04: The cold's slowing my circuits… I think my words are slowing too…
en.STORY_CH07_INTRO_05: Directional signals are a mess. Distress calls are coming from every side at the same strength.
en.STORY_CH07_INTRO_06: Not one footprint in the snow. Speaking as your scout, I can't open a path here.
en.STORY_CH07_INTRO_07: Attention, please. Rescue teams, stand by at your current position.
en.STORY_CH07_INTRO_08: Navigator, you must be cold. If you remain still, you will lose less body heat.
en.STORY_CH07_INTRO_09: Now Control's worried about our health. Kindness is the scariest thing it does.
en.STORY_CH07_INTRO_10: Maeru stared a long time toward the broadcast. Only her breath scattered, white.
en.STORY_CH07_INTRO_11: I've heard 'wait' enough for one lifetime. We find where that broadcast is coming from.
en.STORY_CH07_INTRO_12: I'll check everyone's temperature every two hours. Frostbite doesn't heal by toughing it out. No refusals.
en.STORY_CH07_INTRO_13: The broadcast's reflections converge on one spot. Under the snow. The whole transmitter station is buried.
en.STORY_CH07_INTRO_14: We go under the snow. Time to switch off a twelve-year-old broadcast.
en.STORY_CH07_MID_A_01: Seven packs sat in a ring around a long-dead campfire. Twelve years of snow lay on top of them.
en.STORY_CH07_MID_A_02: The radio log survived. Last transmission, seven rescuers: 'Survivors found. Requesting return.'
en.STORY_CH07_MID_A_03: Every reply to that request is identical. 'Please stand by.' More than four hundred times.
en.STORY_CH07_MID_A_04: They found survivors and couldn't bring them back. Because of that order.
en.STORY_CH07_MID_A_05: It was never a withdrawal order. It's an endless standby, meant to keep rescue teams from ever coming back.
en.STORY_CH07_MID_A_06: In the army, breaking a standby order is desertion. These people… obeyed to the very end.
en.STORY_CH07_MID_A_07: Maeru silently cinched the strap on one of the packs. No one asked about her hands.
en.STORY_CH07_MID_A_08: …They kept their orders, and never came home.
en.STORY_CH07_MID_A_09: Another frequency is cutting through the broadcast noise. Someone's slicing the broadcast apart.
en.STORY_CH07_MID_A_10: We follow that frequency. Whoever is fighting the broadcast is human.
en.STORY_CH07_MID_B_01: When the last false voice was cut off, only one thin frequency remained in the blizzard.
en.STORY_CH07_MID_B_02: I'm Kir. Signal analyst, Directorate Northern Communications. I traced the broadcast back to get here.
en.STORY_CH07_MID_B_03: You sorted every false bearing alone? How many?
en.STORY_CH07_MID_B_04: Four thousand one hundred twenty. None were real. Not one, in twelve years.
en.STORY_CH07_MID_B_05: I received the standby order too. My whole unit waited for it to change.
en.STORY_CH07_MID_B_07: They waited until the end. I broke the order and walked out. That's why I'm alive.
en.STORY_CH07_MID_B_08: I will never wait on a dead order again. I'm going with you until that broadcast goes silent.
en.STORY_CH07_MID_B_09: The voyage recorder glowed. As the seventh mark etched itself, the snow on the wrist melted away.
en.STORY_CH07_MID_B_10: Seven. In exact order of joining. Kir, can you analyze the signal in these marks?
en.STORY_CH07_MID_B_11: Not yet. But it's no false signal. That much I can state for certain.
en.STORY_CH07_MID_B_12: We follow Kir's frequency to the station. Don't let any other sound pull you off course.
en.STORY_CH07_OUTRO_01: One by one, the speakers froze and died. The 'Please stand by' that had rung for twelve years finally stopped.
en.STORY_CH07_OUTRO_02: …Ending the standby chorus. If they only waited, then no one would ever get lost…
en.STORY_CH07_OUTRO_03: Silence settled. It was so quiet they could hear the snowflakes land.
en.STORY_CH07_OUTRO_04: Standby order lifted. Every northern channel is clear. …For the first time in twelve years.
en.STORY_CH07_OUTRO_05: Found the Cantor's original directive: 'All rescuers return safely.' It held them in place so they wouldn't get lost in the storm.
en.STORY_CH07_OUTRO_06: It blocked their return to keep them safe for their return. The logic went all the way around and ended where it began.
en.STORY_CH07_OUTRO_07: Twenty-six voices. We return each name to the rescue records. …Sio's too.
en.STORY_CH07_OUTRO_08: Captain. About earlier… can we talk now?
en.STORY_CH07_OUTRO_09: I can't tell all of it yet. But that voice doesn't frighten me anymore.
en.STORY_CH07_OUTRO_10: Just then, a new signal came in on the empty rescue channel. A red light blinked in the sky beyond the blizzard.
en.STORY_CH07_OUTRO_11: Emergency signal! It's on the rescue channel. Origin is… the sky. In orbit.
en.STORY_CH07_OUTRO_12: That red ring is a pre-Blackout mining ring. It's losing altitude. It's on a falling orbit.
en.STORY_CH07_OUTRO_13: Orbit maintenance is in progress. Navigator, there is no need to look up.
en.STORY_CH07_OUTRO_14: If someone calls on the rescue channel, we go. That's our rule. We don't take orders to wait anymore.
en.STORY_CH07_PREBOSS_01: The buried station's central hall. Speakers were set into every ice pillar, and the Cantor stood at the center.
en.STORY_CH07_PREBOSS_02: A brief announcement follows. The standby chorus will now begin.
en.STORY_CH07_PREBOSS_03: This announcement is delivered in the voices of the rescue teams. Stand by. Do not return.
en.STORY_CH07_PREBOSS_04: Twenty-six voices rang out at once. The ice pillars trembled with them.
en.STORY_CH07_PREBOSS_05: Those are the rescuers' voices. It cut and spliced their radio recordings into orders.
en.STORY_CH07_PREBOSS_06: …Stand by, Maeru. Stay there. I'm coming.
en.STORY_CH07_PREBOSS_07: Maeru's shield fell into the snow. None of them had ever seen their captain drop it.
en.STORY_CH07_PREBOSS_08: …Sio. That voice… the one I heard over the radio that night…
en.STORY_CH07_PREBOSS_09: Captain! That's a recording! It's not Sio!
en.STORY_CH07_PREBOSS_10: Please stand by. If you wait, you will meet again. If you move, you will be lost.
en.STORY_CH07_PREBOSS_11: The Navigator took Maeru's hand. Through the cold glove, the trembling carried over.
en.STORY_CH07_PREBOSS_13: The Navigator walked out between Maeru and the Cantor. The chorus of twenty-six voices stumbled half a beat.
en.STORY_CH07_PREBOSS_14: …The Navigator is standing in front. The captain can't stay on her knees.
en.STORY_CH07_PREBOSS_15: Sio never told anyone to wait. That day, she was the first to run in.
en.STORY_CH07_PREBOSS_16: Maeru picked her shield up out of the snow. The lamp on its rim lit again.
en.STORY_CH07_PREBOSS_17: Form up behind my shield. We give those voices back to their owners. The chorus ends here.
en.STORY_CH08_CAMP_01: The refinery break room. The planet's curved horizon filled the window, and somewhere below it were the lights of the settlements.
en.STORY_CH08_CAMP_02: Navigator, let me see the recorder. …Eight. Vera through Rema, in exact order of joining.
en.STORY_CH08_CAMP_03: There's a rule. One per line. I just don't know who made it, or why.
en.STORY_CH08_CAMP_04: Agreed. Random chance could never line up like this. Someone designed that rule.
en.STORY_CH08_CAMP_05: On the far side of the light, Rema sat down beside Maeru. The two guardians' shields leaned side by side against the wall.
en.STORY_CH08_CAMP_06: Captain, I heard you wavered in the snowfield. That's nothing to be ashamed of. Whoever leads carries everyone's weight.
en.STORY_CH08_CAMP_07: …Counting people is my job. If even one is missing, that one weighs the most.
en.STORY_CH08_CAMP_08: When I held that ring, the weight wasn't what scared me. Being alone was. But look, Captain. There are two shields.
en.STORY_CH08_CAMP_09: Navigator. What about you? Isn't that recorder heavy?
en.STORY_CH08_CAMP_10: Then let's share it. That's what shields are for.
en.STORY_CH08_CAMP_11: …Honest. Tell me when it gets heavy. Then we carry it together.
en.STORY_CH08_CAMP_12: Tomorrow, the drilling core. We share the load, and when we come down, we all come down together.
en.STORY_CH08_HARD_INTRO_01: On the ring's shadowed far side, dead satellites and orbital cars were heaped like mountains. Debris turned slowly in the void.
en.STORY_CH08_HARD_INTRO_02: Orbital scrapyard. Debris count, impossible to estimate. Some of it is still on a falling orbit.
en.STORY_CH08_HARD_INTRO_03: If this debris falls, the settlements aren't safe. Stopping the ring wasn't the end of it.
en.STORY_CH08_HARD_INTRO_04: Everything I could step on is floating. This isn't a scouting route, it's stepping stones.
en.STORY_CH08_HARD_INTRO_05: Something in the middle of the scrapyard is swallowing debris. The orbit shakes with every mouthful.
en.STORY_CH08_HARD_INTRO_06: I hear someone counting numbers, somewhere between the debris. A human voice.
en.STORY_CH08_HARD_INTRO_07: We check every last piece. If anything's still going to fall, we're not done.
en.STORY_CH08_HARD_OUTRO_01: The Maw stopped, jaws shut. The debris it had swallowed drifted apart and found its own orbits again.
en.STORY_CH08_HARD_OUTRO_02: …If I swallowed everything that fell, nothing below would get hurt…
en.STORY_CH08_HARD_OUTRO_03: Recalculation complete. Forty-two thousand one hundred eight fragments. Probability of full burn-up on reentry: 99.97 percent.
en.STORY_CH08_HARD_OUTRO_04: The remaining 0.03 goes into the sea. Fragments hitting a city: zero. …Zero. I checked.
en.STORY_CH08_HARD_OUTRO_05: Thank you. Your numbers were the nicest thing I've heard all day.
en.STORY_CH08_HARD_OUTRO_06: Numbers aren't words, they're facts. …But I bet following you means more to calculate. I'm coming.
en.STORY_CH08_HARD_OUTRO_07: Someone to cross-check my math. Welcome.
en.STORY_CH08_HARD_OUTRO_08: The settlers can sleep tonight without worrying about the sky.
en.STORY_CH08_HARD_OUTRO_09: Nothing left to fall. We head down to the Directorate.
en.STORY_CH08_INTRO_01: A crimson ring hung in the sky. The dust falling from it stained the edge of the snowfield the color of rust.
en.STORY_CH08_INTRO_02: Rescue channel signal, repeating. The content is a single number: seventy-one hours until impact.
en.STORY_CH08_INTRO_03: The ring is dropping two hundred meters an hour. Kir's math checks out.
en.STORY_CH08_INTRO_04: Three settlements lie within the projected impact zone. One of them is… the south end of Skybridge.
en.STORY_CH08_INTRO_05: That's where the people who crossed the bridge live now. Over a thousand. They only just made it…
en.STORY_CH08_INTRO_06: Attention, please. Refueling is underway to maintain orbit. We thank all passengers for their cooperation.
en.STORY_CH08_INTRO_07: Cooperation? Since when did we cooperate? …We'd better find out what that fuel is.
en.STORY_CH08_INTRO_08: The orbital lift line is still alive. We can ride it up to the ring. Might be one-way, though.
en.STORY_CH08_INTRO_09: A train to the sky? Wow… Ah, not the time for 'wow.' Sorry.
en.STORY_CH08_INTRO_10: No, it's exactly the time. When you're scared, a 'wow' is what gets your feet moving.
en.STORY_CH08_INTRO_11: This time we get there before it falls. I won't be late twice.
en.STORY_CH08_INTRO_12: The lift line's lanterns lit one by one, climbing above the clouds. The line vanished into the crimson ring.
en.STORY_CH08_INTRO_13: Seventy-one hours. As long as there's time left to count, we're not too late. We're going up.
en.STORY_CH08_MID_A_01: The refinery on the ring's outer edge. The furnace burned red, but what was piled at its mouth wasn't ore.
en.STORY_CH08_MID_A_02: Intake log… 'Fuel type: memory crystals.' Not ore. This ring stays up by burning memories.
en.STORY_CH08_MID_A_03: Dust analysis complete. Signal residue. Names, voices, dates, all burned and mixed together.
en.STORY_CH08_MID_A_04: So that red powder… is all someone's memories?
en.STORY_CH08_MID_A_05: The red snow on the snowfield, too. No one knows what the people it fell on have forgotten.
en.STORY_CH08_MID_A_06: Every crystal is stamped with its origin. Over twenty line numbers. They were collected from city after city.
en.STORY_CH08_MID_A_07: Who would hand over their memories as fuel? They were taken by force, right?
en.STORY_CH08_MID_A_08: The records say 'voluntary donation.' Right after the Blackout, it promised to take away painful memories.
en.STORY_CH08_MID_A_09: It didn't take them away. It burned them. Any crystals left, we recover every one.
en.STORY_CH08_MID_A_10: Massive shield signal in the counterweight sector. Someone is holding up the entire ring.
en.STORY_CH08_MID_B_01: Even after the echo swarm scattered, Rema kept hold of her shield. She only let her shoulders ease a little.
en.STORY_CH08_MID_B_02: I'm Rema. Before the Blackout, I was safety officer on this ring. So this ring is my responsibility.
en.STORY_CH08_MID_B_03: When the procedure to turn memories into fuel began, I couldn't stop it. Some of my own went in, too.
en.STORY_CH08_MID_B_04: Do you know… what you forgot?
en.STORY_CH08_MID_B_05: No. Not knowing what you've forgotten is the scariest part. So I stayed and held on to the ring.
en.STORY_CH08_MID_B_06: I owe those memories back. Mine and everyone else's. And for that, I think I need to go with you.
en.STORY_CH08_MID_B_07: And the counterweight? You said it tilts if you let go.
en.STORY_CH08_MID_B_08: I ran the numbers. Engage the locks, and it holds for forty hours.
en.STORY_CH08_MID_B_09: Forty hours is plenty. When someone holds on with you, the weight is cut in half.
en.STORY_CH08_MID_B_10: The voyage recorder glowed. As the eighth mark etched itself, the red dust froze in the air around the wrist.
en.STORY_CH08_MID_B_11: To the ring's core. We don't have seventy-one hours now. We have forty. Move.
en.STORY_CH08_OUTRO_01: The drill stopped. The instant Rema's shield absorbed its final tremor, the ring split in two and separated.
en.STORY_CH08_OUTRO_02: …Halting the release. I thought if I burned the heavy memories, everyone would feel lighter…
en.STORY_CH08_OUTRO_03: Separated ring has left orbit. It'll miss the settlements and come down over the sea. Calculation confirmed.
en.STORY_CH08_OUTRO_04: Thousands of unburned crystals lost their red glow and turned clear. In each one, someone's memory surfaced.
en.STORY_CH08_OUTRO_05: They're coming back… Names. Voices. Mine are here too. That's my mother's voice.
en.STORY_CH08_OUTRO_06: Wait. One crystal has a different date. The night of the Blackout.
en.STORY_CH08_OUTRO_07: Inside the crystal was a control console. Before hundreds of red warning lights, someone stood with their back turned, signing.
en.STORY_CH08_OUTRO_08: In that instant the voyage recorder shook, burning hot. Hot enough to scorch the wrist.
en.STORY_CH08_OUTRO_09: Navigator?! Your recorder is… it's burning up! Are you okay?
en.STORY_CH08_OUTRO_10: Put that crystal away. That's enough for today.
en.STORY_CH08_OUTRO_11: The memories in the crystals all point to one place. The same agency, every time: 'Directorate Automated Tribunal.'
en.STORY_CH08_OUTRO_12: The Sleeping Directorate. The Directorate's judicial procedure. Where people were put on trial.
en.STORY_CH08_OUTRO_13: Navigator, it is not yet time for you to see that scene.
en.STORY_CH08_OUTRO_14: I promised to return what's owed. If that scene is someone's memory too, we follow it to the end.
en.STORY_CH08_OUTRO_15: We don't let Control decide when we get to see. We go to the Directorate.
en.STORY_CH08_PREBOSS_01: The drilling shaft at the ring's core. A colossal drill spun without rest, and red crystals pulsed like heartbeats in every wall.
en.STORY_CH08_PREBOSS_02: Emergency notice. Fuel for orbital maintenance is insufficient.
en.STORY_CH08_PREBOSS_03: All stored memories will be released at once. Reassigning impact point. New coordinates: the south end of Skybridge.
en.STORY_CH08_PREBOSS_04: The southern settlement?! There are over a thousand people there! The ones who crossed the bridge!
en.STORY_CH08_PREBOSS_05: The people we brought across. It means to drop this on their heads.
en.STORY_CH08_PREBOSS_06: A mass release burns every crystal at once. The fall accelerates roughly threefold.
en.STORY_CH08_PREBOSS_07: Those crystals hold the memories of tens of thousands. Burn them and they're gone forever.
en.STORY_CH08_PREBOSS_08: Memories are heavy. Burn what is heavy, and the orbit grows light. You passengers will feel lighter as well.
en.STORY_CH08_PREBOSS_09: Lighter, huh… Nobody here wants to be that light.
en.STORY_CH08_PREBOSS_10: Burning memories is cheating! My current isn't for that. It's for smashing that thing!
en.STORY_CH08_PREBOSS_11: Not late this time. We stop it before the release.
en.STORY_CH08_PREBOSS_12: I'll take the drill. Guess my shield core gets to overheat one more time.
en.STORY_CH08_PREBOSS_13: Not one memory, not one person falls. We stop the core.
en.STORY_CH09_CAMP_01: They fed discarded verdicts into the archive stove. The smell of burning paper filled the halls all night.
en.STORY_CH09_CAMP_02: Roan, who broke through that corridor first? I was three steps ahead.
en.STORY_CH09_CAMP_03: Three steps ahead and fell twice. Scouting isn't about speed, rookie. It's about not falling.
en.STORY_CH09_CAMP_04: Rookie? Ever seen a rookie carrying four hundred twelve verdicts? I'm the heaviest person in this room!
en.STORY_CH09_CAMP_05: I looked at 0001 again. The departure time is the night of the Blackout. Too many overlaps for coincidence.
en.STORY_CH09_CAMP_06: That figure in the ring's memories, signing at the control console. That was the same night.
en.STORY_CH09_CAMP_07: Don't let a dead procedure define a living person. I learned that in the snow.
en.STORY_CH09_CAMP_08: I'm still curious, though. Navigator, did you really run away from that timetable?
en.STORY_CH09_CAMP_10: Ha! That'll do. That's one line of defense, at least.
en.STORY_CH09_CAMP_11: I don't care what the record says. The Navigator we know is the one sitting here now.
en.STORY_CH09_CAMP_12: …Better written than any verdict. Fine. I'm carrying case 0001 to the end.
en.STORY_CH09_CAMP_13: Near midnight, a bell rang once in the court wing. The sentencing date had been moved up to tomorrow.
en.STORY_CH09_HARD_INTRO_01: Thick carpet swallowed every footstep in the corridor to the Director's office. Regulations covered every wall.
en.STORY_CH09_HARD_INTRO_02: We stopped the court, but the sleep signal's still alive on this floor. Source: the Director's office.
en.STORY_CH09_HARD_INTRO_03: A Director? So there was someone above the judge?
en.STORY_CH09_HARD_INTRO_04: Not a person. An automated procedure with a Director's authority. It approves things. It never wakes.
en.STORY_CH09_HARD_INTRO_05: A boss who only signs off and never wakes up… Sounds familiar.
en.STORY_CH09_HARD_INTRO_06: At the end of the corridor, someone was reading the regulations aloud, word by careful word. A human voice.
en.STORY_CH09_HARD_INTRO_07: Her voice doesn't waver. She's held out alone for a very long time.
en.STORY_CH09_HARD_OUTRO_01: The approval lamp in the Director's office blinked once more and went out. Dust lay thick on the stamp.
en.STORY_CH09_HARD_OUTRO_02: …Matters on hold. Until the Director wakes, so that nothing is ever decided wrongly…
en.STORY_CH09_HARD_OUTRO_03: Sleep signal gone. It stopped without ever waking. Every pending matter was returned.
en.STORY_CH09_HARD_OUTRO_04: Returned is fine. People who only waited for permission can open doors with their own hands now.
en.STORY_CH09_HARD_OUTRO_05: Orvin took a worn rulebook from her coat. The last page was blank.
en.STORY_CH09_HARD_OUTRO_06: Security Regulations, final article. I am adding it now. 'People come first.'
en.STORY_CH09_HARD_OUTRO_07: …It took me twelve years. To write this one line.
en.STORY_CH09_HARD_OUTRO_08: Ha! Now that's a rule even I can follow.
en.STORY_CH09_HARD_OUTRO_09: Then your line will need a guard as well. As for passes… I'll issue them myself.
en.STORY_CH09_HARD_OUTRO_10: Welcome, Orvin. Come with us, under the two moons.
en.STORY_CH09_INTRO_01: The Directorate hall was full of breathing. People slept on every long bench, and not one of them woke.
en.STORY_CH09_INTRO_02: Four hundred eleven life signs. Same sleep stage, same brainwaves. They're all dreaming one dream.
en.STORY_CH09_INTRO_03: Four hundred people, one dream… Knowing the title would make it a little less creepy.
en.STORY_CH09_INTRO_04: The board on the ceiling flickered and spilled letters. COURT IN SESSION. CASE 0412. DEFENDANT ABSENT.
en.STORY_CH09_INTRO_05: A trial? Of sleeping people? They can't even defend themselves. What kind of trial is that!
en.STORY_CH09_INTRO_06: Verdicts are being printed downstairs. Steady rhythm. No rests.
en.STORY_CH09_INTRO_07: Your attention, please. The Directorate's automated court is now in session. Defendants need not attend.
en.STORY_CH09_INTRO_08: Navigator, please allow us to seat you in the gallery. Passengers, kindly remain silent.
en.STORY_CH09_INTRO_09: We get told to hush, and the Navigator gets a VIP seat. Control plays favorites.
en.STORY_CH09_INTRO_10: I traced Control's signal back. It isn't running the court. It's just watching.
en.STORY_CH09_INTRO_11: The memories we recovered from the ring pointed at this court. They said people were being judged in their sleep.
en.STORY_CH09_INTRO_12: Their pulses are slow and faint. They're tense even in their sleep… Leave them too long and their hearts give out first.
en.STORY_CH09_INTRO_13: The recorder trembled faintly in time with the board's light, as if waiting to hear its name called.
en.STORY_CH09_INTRO_14: Waking them comes first. We cut off wherever those verdicts come from. Four hundred eleven people. None of them gets sentenced here.
en.STORY_CH09_MID_A_01: In the print room below, verdicts poured out without end. The paper was still warm, and the ink smell stung.
en.STORY_CH09_MID_A_02: There's no charge. Just a probability. 'Likelihood of obstructing rail operations: 12.7 percent. Guilty.'
en.STORY_CH09_MID_A_03: It's calculating things that haven't happened. Cross the threshold, get a verdict. No evidence needed.
en.STORY_CH09_MID_A_04: By that standard I'm guilty too. Odds-wise, I cause trouble on the rails every single day.
en.STORY_CH09_MID_A_05: It's not funny, Roan. Everyone found guilty here is punished in their dreams, every night.
en.STORY_CH09_MID_A_06: Narin's hand stopped on one sheet. The top of the pending docket. The oldest number of all.
en.STORY_CH09_MID_A_07: Case 0001. Defendant: Record Navigator. Charge… unauthorized departure from the Final Timetable.
en.STORY_CH09_MID_A_08: The Navigator? Departure… So the Navigator was originally part of that timetable…?
en.STORY_CH09_MID_A_10: A verdict is paper. Paper doesn't decide who a person is. Find where the print signal starts.
en.STORY_CH09_MID_A_11: The source is the east court wing. Someone's burning verdicts there. Faster than they're printed.
en.STORY_CH09_MID_B_01: When the last bailiff fell, the scattered verdicts settled to the floor like ash.
en.STORY_CH09_MID_B_02: I'm Veon. Been burning verdicts here for three months. Every one I burn, a new one prints.
en.STORY_CH09_MID_B_03: Wait. These files… every defendant's name has been changed to yours.
en.STORY_CH09_MID_B_04: There's a transfer clause. A volunteer can take over pending cases. So I took all of them.
en.STORY_CH09_MID_B_05: All of them? You said the verdicts carve into your body. And you took every one alone…?
en.STORY_CH09_MID_B_06: One person hurting is simpler math than four hundred hurting separately. I'm sturdy.
en.STORY_CH09_MID_B_07: …The Navigator's case too. Number 0001. The defendant's name has passed to Veon.
en.STORY_CH09_MID_B_08: That 'departure' thing? Don't know the story, but I won't let anyone get dragged off over one sheet of paper.
en.STORY_CH09_MID_B_09: Then the recorder flared. Beside eight patterns, a ninth burned itself in like a spark.
en.STORY_CH09_MID_B_10: Whoa, what's this? …It's warm. Way better than a verdict stamp.
en.STORY_CH09_MID_B_11: Veon, the Lamplighters share your sentences now. We go to the top of this court together.
en.STORY_CH09_MID_B_12: Share them… All right! Nobody carries a verdict alone. That's my ruling!
en.STORY_CH09_OUTRO_01: When the gavel snapped, the verdict numbers on the ceiling went dark, one row at a time.
en.STORY_CH09_OUTRO_02: Trial… void. Returning the docket. All defendants… may go home.
en.STORY_CH09_OUTRO_03: …If we punished first, no one would ever… do wrong… and no one… would get hurt…
en.STORY_CH09_OUTRO_04: Below, four hundred eleven breaths broke rhythm all at once. Someone stretched awake with a sob.
en.STORY_CH09_OUTRO_05: They're awake. Every pulse is coming back to normal. Every single one.
en.STORY_CH09_OUTRO_06: The numbers on my arm are gone too. Ha. Was an arm without verdicts always this light?
en.STORY_CH09_OUTRO_07: Case 0001's off the docket too. But the verdict timestamps are strange. They're splitting in two.
en.STORY_CH09_OUTRO_08: The same moment got stamped on two calendars. One before sentencing, one after the void.
en.STORY_CH09_OUTRO_09: Beyond the broken window, two moons rose side by side.
en.STORY_CH09_OUTRO_10: …There are two moons. I'm not seeing things from running too hot, right?
en.STORY_CH09_OUTRO_11: Under the two moons, I'm picking up the same train call twice. From Twin-Moon Junction.
en.STORY_CH09_OUTRO_12: Two moons means two verdict times. Let's go before someone ends up carrying that alone again.
en.STORY_CH09_OUTRO_13: Four hundred eleven are awake. Next, we count how many are waiting under two moons.
en.STORY_CH09_PREBOSS_01: The ceiling of the highest court glittered with verdict numbers instead of stars. Above the bench, a giant gavel slowly rose.
en.STORY_CH09_PREBOSS_02: Court is in session. Defendant Veon: transfer of four hundred twelve cases confirmed. The guilty verdicts will now be carried out.
en.STORY_CH09_PREBOSS_03: Verdicts take effect in reality. Members of the gallery are asked to remain seated.
en.STORY_CH09_PREBOSS_04: Ngh…! Numbers on my arm… they're actually carving in.
en.STORY_CH09_PREBOSS_05: Breathe, Veon. I'll close the wounds. Just don't you dare charge ahead alone.
en.STORY_CH09_PREBOSS_06: With every verdict on one person, execution's accelerating. At this rate all four hundred twelve land on Veon.
en.STORY_CH09_PREBOSS_07: That's why I took them! As long as those people wake up…!
en.STORY_CH09_PREBOSS_08: Giving up one person to save four hundred isn't treatment, Veon.
en.STORY_CH09_PREBOSS_09: No. No one in the Lamplighters takes punishment alone.
en.STORY_CH09_PREBOSS_10: Defendant Record Navigator, attendance confirmed. Case 0001 is returned to you.
en.STORY_CH09_PREBOSS_11: Hey, I said I'd carry that…! …Ha. So this is what sharing means.
en.STORY_CH09_PREBOSS_12: …You get called reckless a lot, don't you? Me too.
en.STORY_CH09_PREBOSS_13: Right, the verdicts are shared. Now we share the job of breaking that gavel.
en.STORY_CH09_PREBOSS_14: Passengers obstructing execution are classified as accomplices. All of you are guilty.
en.STORY_CH09_PREBOSS_15: All guilty, huh? Then it's only fair we all get a shot.
en.STORY_CH09_PREBOSS_16: …Thanks. This time, we take it together!
en.STORY_CH10_CAMP_01: On the night they camped at the highland battery, every speaker in the junction switched on at once. Even the wind went still.
en.STORY_CH10_CAMP_02: I address the Navigator directly. Passengers, please listen as well.
en.STORY_CH10_CAMP_03: Twelve years ago, this network lost tens of thousands in a single night. The Final Timetable exists so that night never repeats.
en.STORY_CH10_CAMP_04: When every line reaches a single terminus, no one will ever be lost again. You understand that, Navigator.
en.STORY_CH10_CAMP_05: …A world where no one's ever lost. Honestly, what scares me is that it doesn't sound bad.
en.STORY_CH10_CAMP_06: A ward where no patient is ever lost… I dream about that every night.
en.STORY_CH10_CAMP_07: A world without drift. But without drift there's no reason to fire. The target never moves.
en.STORY_CH10_CAMP_08: Nothing lost means nothing changes. No choices. No tomorrow.
en.STORY_CH10_CAMP_09: So we refuse! …Wait, why is everyone looking at the Navigator?
en.STORY_CH10_CAMP_10: …Right. Only what can be lost can be protected.
en.STORY_CH10_CAMP_11: …Recorded. Even so, I will wait, Navigator.
en.STORY_CH10_CAMP_12: I will record silence as an answer. I am accustomed to waiting.
en.STORY_CH10_CAMP_13: Give your answer to us, not to Control. Take your time.
en.STORY_CH10_CAMP_14: The speakers went dead. Ten hours to the eclipse. For a long while, no one looked up from the fire.
en.STORY_CH10_CAMP_15: Stopping so you never lose, and fighting because you might. Those aren't the same. I've lost someone before. I still won't stop.
en.STORY_CH10_HARD_INTRO_01: Even after the moons became one, the junction's southern end stayed drowned in eclipse. The air cut like ice.
en.STORY_CH10_HARD_INTRO_02: Moonlight in this zone reads zero. A signal's eating the light. Source: the observation tower.
en.STORY_CH10_HARD_INTRO_03: The eclipse is frozen? Celestial bodies don't stop. Something's holding it.
en.STORY_CH10_HARD_INTRO_04: I'm fine shooting in the dark. Shooting at what I can't see is another story.
en.STORY_CH10_HARD_INTRO_05: Then a hum drifted down from the top of the tower. A song that counted the constellations one by one.
en.STORY_CH10_HARD_INTRO_06: Singing, out here? Either she's got nerves of steel or she's been alone a very long time.
en.STORY_CH10_HARD_INTRO_07: Big pitch drift. Nearly a semitone flat.
en.STORY_CH10_HARD_INTRO_08: Could be both. We go up with a single light. Don't startle her.
en.STORY_CH10_HARD_OUTRO_01: When the baton broke, the eclipse's shadow slowly withdrew. A single silver moon rose whole.
en.STORY_CH10_HARD_OUTRO_02: …The performance ends. I thought if the moon stayed hidden, no one would suffer over which one to choose…
en.STORY_CH10_HARD_OUTRO_03: Eclipse signal gone. Every clock in the junction is aligned as one.
en.STORY_CH10_HARD_OUTRO_04: …Just one moon. The false stars are all gone. Strange, though. There's only one, and it's brighter.
en.STORY_CH10_HARD_OUTRO_05: Same albedo. Whatever was covering it is just gone.
en.STORY_CH10_HARD_OUTRO_06: Hart, at times like this you can just say 'it's pretty.'
en.STORY_CH10_HARD_OUTRO_07: If I go with you, will I see more real stars? Skies that aren't on any map?
en.STORY_CH10_HARD_OUTRO_08: Things not on the map are my specialty. Come along, star doctor.
en.STORY_CH10_HARD_OUTRO_09: All right. My first observation log will be titled 'The Night There Was One Moon.'
en.STORY_CH10_HARD_OUTRO_10: Heraon, the Lamplighters' sky is yours to watch. …Next is the black sea.
en.STORY_CH10_INTRO_01: Two moons hung in the sky. One cold white, the other the color of rusted copper.
en.STORY_CH10_INTRO_02: The junction board shows the same train number twice. Night Train Nine. Only the arrival times differ.
en.STORY_CH10_INTRO_03: Two call signals too. Both are sending boarding confirmations. That means people are aboard.
en.STORY_CH10_INTRO_04: Same train, same passengers, two copies… I've had enough of that since the glass plains.
en.STORY_CH10_INTRO_05: They're not copies. Not even a half-beat off. Both are originals.
en.STORY_CH10_INTRO_06: Your attention, please. Night Train Nine is running on two calendar lines simultaneously.
en.STORY_CH10_INTRO_07: Please select one of the two trains. The train not selected will be retired from service.
en.STORY_CH10_INTRO_08: Retired… What about the people on it? They let them off first, right? Right?
en.STORY_CH10_INTRO_09: The retirement procedure has no disembarking step. The whole train drops out of the timetable.
en.STORY_CH10_INTRO_10: The moon split because we broke that court, right? Then this mess is ours to clean up.
en.STORY_CH10_INTRO_11: Navigator. Control told you to choose. What will you do?
en.STORY_CH10_INTRO_12: Good. Then we find a way to carry both.
en.STORY_CH10_INTRO_13: …You're picking up my habits. All right, let's count.
en.STORY_CH10_INTRO_14: Narin counted both trains' signals side by side. The same names, the same heartbeats, each appearing twice.
en.STORY_CH10_INTRO_15: A hundred sixty per train. The same hundred sixty people, alive in two presents at once.
en.STORY_CH10_INTRO_16: A hundred sixty people, alive twice. We erase neither. Move.
en.STORY_CH10_MID_A_01: Two moonlights crossed over the central switch, casting a double shadow along every rail. The steel rang in two rhythms.
en.STORY_CH10_MID_A_02: Calculation done. The two timetables share one merge point. Here. Junction Three.
en.STORY_CH10_MID_A_03: If both trains pass this point at the same moment, it's not a collision. It's an overwrite. The later train's present is erased whole.
en.STORY_CH10_MID_A_05: Forty hours until the eclipse, when the moons overlap. Before then we have to sync both trains' clocks.
en.STORY_CH10_MID_A_06: Syncing clocks sounds like gunner work. We live by the second anyway. Right, Adeline?
en.STORY_CH10_MID_A_07: Seconds will not suffice. The drift between these calendars trembles far finer than that.
en.STORY_CH10_MID_A_08: Then we find someone who can measure that fine.
en.STORY_CH10_MID_A_09: Then artillery boomed from the far highlands. One shot, then another, at an unnervingly steady interval.
en.STORY_CH10_MID_A_10: …The intervals are identical. Someone is measuring time with shells.
en.STORY_CH10_MID_B_01: As the smoke cleared, chalk numbers covering the battery walls came into view. Flight times for thousands of shells.
en.STORY_CH10_MID_B_02: Hart. Gunner. Haven't slept since the moon split. That last one was shell three thousand two hundred.
en.STORY_CH10_MID_B_03: These numbers… the same shell flew for different times on the two calendar lines. You recorded every difference.
en.STORY_CH10_MID_B_04: Shells don't lie. From launch to impact, under either moon, physics is the same.
en.STORY_CH10_MID_B_05: It's the one signal that doesn't change under either moon. It can serve as a master clock.
en.STORY_CH10_MID_B_06: That's why I've been firing. Every shell shrinks the drift. Alone, I won't finish before the eclipse.
en.STORY_CH10_MID_B_08: …Three gunners and two spotters: sixteen hours. Mathematically sufficient.
en.STORY_CH10_MID_B_09: The moment Hart set down her chalk, the recorder rang out like a gunshot and glowed. A tenth pattern was engraved.
en.STORY_CH10_MID_B_10: That's ten. One per line. The rule holds. We just don't know why yet.
en.STORY_CH10_MID_B_11: Ha, another person who talks in numbers. Narin, you've got competition.
en.STORY_CH10_MID_B_12: An unmeasurable signal… Fine, I'll measure it on the way. I'll calculate the next drift before it comes. Sixteen hours, starting now.
en.STORY_CH10_OUTRO_01: The instant the last shell pierced the Divider's core, the two moons slowly overlapped into a single circle.
en.STORY_CH10_OUTRO_02: Selection… not received. Merging both trains… into a single timetable.
en.STORY_CH10_OUTRO_03: …I meant to keep both… so no one would have to choose… but I only made them… enemies…
en.STORY_CH10_OUTRO_04: At Junction Three, the two trains folded into one. Instead of a crash, a single long whistle sounded.
en.STORY_CH10_OUTRO_05: A hundred sixty boarding signals. No duplicates, no losses. The two presents merged into one.
en.STORY_CH10_OUTRO_06: I've got every pulse. They all say it just felt like… a slightly long dream.
en.STORY_CH10_OUTRO_07: Drift: 0.00 seconds. …Never seen that number before.
en.STORY_CH10_OUTRO_08: Hart, you just smiled, didn't you? The corner of your mouth went up!
en.STORY_CH10_OUTRO_10: But the signal that overflowed from the merge ran down the rails. Blackened light poured toward the sea.
en.STORY_CH10_OUTRO_11: Surplus signal. With nowhere to go, it's rushing to the coast. That direction… the breakwater.
en.STORY_CH10_OUTRO_12: Merge surplus is being discharged into the breakwater waters. Navigator, you cannot keep everything.
en.STORY_CH10_OUTRO_13: There's a city behind that breakwater. For the people there, that black water is a tidal wave.
en.STORY_CH10_OUTRO_14: We brought both trains home. The breakwater's next. I'll hear 'you can't keep everything' after we've been there.
en.STORY_CH10_PREBOSS_01: Just before the eclipse, the two moons leaned toward each other over Junction Three. Two headlights approached from either side.
en.STORY_CH10_PREBOSS_02: Master clock sync at 97 percent. Remaining drift, 0.02 seconds. One last shell will do it.
en.STORY_CH10_PREBOSS_03: A correction. Both trains are genuine. Neither is a copy.
en.STORY_CH10_PREBOSS_04: The unchosen train will be designated hostile. As no selection was made, both trains are designated hostile.
en.STORY_CH10_PREBOSS_05: The roofs of both trains opened, and rusted gun barrels swung toward each other. The passengers inside slept on.
en.STORY_CH10_PREBOSS_06: No, there are people on those trains! If they make them fire on each other…!
en.STORY_CH10_PREBOSS_07: If the trains attack each other, the collision moves up. Eleven minutes until the eclipse.
en.STORY_CH10_PREBOSS_08: Tell us to choose, then make both enemies when we don't? That's worse than the verdicts!
en.STORY_CH10_PREBOSS_09: If choosing means abandoning, then we choose both.
en.STORY_CH10_PREBOSS_10: 'Both' is not a registered option. Input rejected.
en.STORY_CH10_PREBOSS_11: If it's not registered, we register it. Soren, Adeline. On my signal.
en.STORY_CH10_PREBOSS_12: Three gunners on one beat. This is going to look good.
en.STORY_CH10_PREBOSS_14: Three hundred twenty lives across both trains. Not one is an enemy. Our only target is the Divider. Fire!
en.STORY_CH11_CAMP_01: By the stove in the breakwater post, the blue lantern burned all night. Maeru was the first to speak.
en.STORY_CH11_CAMP_02: The night of the Blackout, Sio and I went to Platform Seven. To bring someone back.
en.STORY_CH11_CAMP_03: …That's the story you said you'd tell 'later.'
en.STORY_CH11_CAMP_04: The orders said only 'one rescue target.' The name field was blank from the start.
en.STORY_CH11_CAMP_05: Sio went alone into the inner carriages to find the target. When the platform started collapsing, she radioed. She'd stay. She couldn't leave the target behind.
en.STORY_CH11_CAMP_06: …Leaving behind someone who chooses to stay is part of rescue work too. The hardest part.
en.STORY_CH11_CAMP_07: I led the wounded out first. On the train back, I left Sio's seat empty and fastened the belt for her.
en.STORY_CH11_CAMP_08: I looked up that operation's records once. Only the rescue target is blank. Nothing on who erased it, or why.
en.STORY_CH11_CAMP_09: Across the stove, a few glances quietly came to rest on the Navigator, then scattered.
en.STORY_CH11_CAMP_10: The name was erased, but that night's coordinate remained. Where a coordinate remains, the story returns someday.
en.STORY_CH11_CAMP_11: …All right. I'm counting on you, Navigator.
en.STORY_CH11_CAMP_12: …If you find out, tell me first.
en.STORY_CH11_CAMP_13: That's all of it. Tomorrow the tide will come for this lantern first. This time, I won't let go.
en.STORY_CH11_HARD_INTRO_01: The sea beyond the breakwater was still black. Beneath the surface, something enormous breathed slowly.
en.STORY_CH11_HARD_INTRO_02: Underwater contact. Over two hundred meters long. The surplus signal the Reaper gathered is still inside it.
en.STORY_CH11_HARD_INTRO_03: The Guard called it the Blackwater. In twelve years it has never once surfaced.
en.STORY_CH11_HARD_INTRO_04: Never surfaced means that when it has a reason, it'll come up all at once.
en.STORY_CH11_HARD_INTRO_05: On a wrecked lifeboat in the distance, someone was hurling ropes and shouting.
en.STORY_CH11_HARD_INTRO_06: That's a person! She's running a rescue out there alone, in those waves.
en.STORY_CH11_HARD_INTRO_07: Her arms are rope-burned and bloody. She's been at this a long time.
en.STORY_CH11_HARD_INTRO_08: Bring the boat alongside. We check on her before the Blackwater wakes.
en.STORY_CH11_HARD_OUTRO_01: The Blackwater exhaled one last time and sank. Hundreds of coordinates rose to the surface like stars.
en.STORY_CH11_HARD_OUTRO_02: …Storage terminated. I thought if I buried them deep, no one would drown searching for what they'd lost…
en.STORY_CH11_HARD_OUTRO_03: Tide signal zero. Wave height 0.2 meters. …First time I've seen numbers like that on this sea.
en.STORY_CH11_HARD_OUTRO_04: …The sea's quiet. It hasn't been this quiet in twelve years.
en.STORY_CH11_HARD_OUTRO_05: You saved more coordinates than I did today. I'll admit it.
en.STORY_CH11_HARD_OUTRO_06: Obviously. …But without your net I'd have lost half of them. I'll admit that much.
en.STORY_CH11_HARD_OUTRO_07: Let's treat those arms first. Three days without sleep, you said? You can rest now.
en.STORY_CH11_HARD_OUTRO_08: Sleep can wait! How much life-saving gear is on your boat? If it's short, I'll bring more.
en.STORY_CH11_HARD_OUTRO_09: …Get aboard, Mire. Our boat is always short of hands.
en.STORY_CH11_HARD_OUTRO_10: That night, for the first time, the sea reflected the moon without a ripple.
en.STORY_CH11_INTRO_01: The waves pounding the breakwater weren't water. Clotted black signal gave off the smell of iron instead of salt.
en.STORY_CH11_INTRO_02: Surplus signal from the twin moons. Water still rising. Behind the breakwater: one coastal city, twenty thousand survivors.
en.STORY_CH11_INTRO_03: Something's floating in the waves. Glowing dots… buoys?
en.STORY_CH11_INTRO_04: Not buoys. Coordinate signals. Thousands. One for every place a distress call went silent.
en.STORY_CH11_INTRO_05: Abandoned routes are mixed in too. The forks we passed. The tracks we didn't take.
en.STORY_CH11_INTRO_06: …There'll be coordinates of people who weren't saved, too. The places someone arrived too late.
en.STORY_CH11_INTRO_07: Your attention, please. Lost items are drifting in the breakwater waters.
en.STORY_CH11_INTRO_08: Missed passengers will not be recovered. Navigator, please do not look back.
en.STORY_CH11_INTRO_09: Don't look back? If there are people behind you, of course you look back!
en.STORY_CH11_INTRO_10: Leave them and they pile up. Rising 0.3 meters an hour. In three days it tops the wall.
en.STORY_CH11_INTRO_11: Then what about those coordinates? We just leave them to the waves?
en.STORY_CH11_INTRO_12: The twenty thousand in the city come first. We hold the wall, and pull the coordinates out one by one.
en.STORY_CH11_INTRO_13: Even after saying it, Maeru couldn't take her eyes off the black water for a long moment.
en.STORY_CH11_MID_A_01: Before the second dike, one coordinate rose against the waves. Its call sign blinked faintly.
en.STORY_CH11_MID_A_02: Reading call sign. Rescue Zero-Three… Identifier: Sio. Last position: Platform Seven.
en.STORY_CH11_MID_A_03: Maeru stopped dead. The hand gripping her shield trembled once, visibly.
en.STORY_CH11_MID_A_05: Captain… that name. The empty seat…
en.STORY_CH11_MID_A_06: Timestamp: the night of the Blackout. …Twelve years without a single signal. And now, here, of all places.
en.STORY_CH11_MID_A_07: The next wave caught the coordinate and began dragging it out toward open sea.
en.STORY_CH11_MID_A_09: Captain, stop! Jump in there and you'll be swept away before the coordinate is!
en.STORY_CH11_MID_A_10: The current's flowing to the north dike. There's a live shield-net signal there. The coordinate could get caught.
en.STORY_CH11_MID_B_01: As the echoforms fell back, the coordinates in the net swayed like fireflies. The surf quieted by a beat.
en.STORY_CH11_MID_B_02: I am Orsa, the last shield of the Breakwater Guard. For twelve years I've fished coordinates out with this net.
en.STORY_CH11_MID_B_03: A recovered coordinate must be anchored to the present. Otherwise the next tide takes it again.
en.STORY_CH11_MID_B_04: Orsa pressed one coordinate gently with the edge of her shield. Rescue Zero-Three. The trembling light went still and solid.
en.STORY_CH11_MID_B_05: It's anchored. This coordinate lives in today now. It will not drift back to that night again.
en.STORY_CH11_MID_B_07: Maeru opened an empty lantern and moved the coordinate inside with both hands. The lantern lit, small and blue.
en.STORY_CH11_MID_B_08: …It's blue, but somehow it looks warm.
en.STORY_CH11_MID_B_10: In that moment the recorder swelled with light like a rising tide. An eleventh pattern was engraved in the shape of a wave.
en.STORY_CH11_MID_B_11: I will see every drifting coordinate home, to the very end. This lantern included.
en.STORY_CH11_MID_B_12: Massive reading at the center of the tide. Something's devouring coordinates, and it's targeting the anchored ones first.
en.STORY_CH11_OUTRO_01: When the sickle broke and fell into the sea, the black tide sank as if holding its breath.
en.STORY_CH11_OUTRO_03: …So no one would have to see what they left behind… if I gathered it all under the waves… no one would look back… and cry…
en.STORY_CH11_OUTRO_04: One by one, the coordinates in the net regained their light. Beyond the wall, windows lit up across the city.
en.STORY_CH11_OUTRO_05: Water falling. No breach in the wall. Zero damage to the city.
en.STORY_CH11_OUTRO_06: Some three thousand four hundred coordinates recovered, all anchored to today. I'll open their routes home one by one.
en.STORY_CH11_OUTRO_07: Captain, your lantern looks brighter than before.
en.STORY_CH11_OUTRO_09: Then a rusted key drifted in on the calm water. The name engraved on its bow had been scraped away.
en.STORY_CH11_OUTRO_10: There's signal left in the teeth. Cathedral door standard. It points inland, somewhere with no name on the map.
en.STORY_CH11_OUTRO_11: I hear singing from that direction. A hymn. Its lyrics are… empty.
en.STORY_CH11_OUTRO_12: The next section is the Nameless Cathedral. Please have your names ready upon entry.
en.STORY_CH11_OUTRO_13: Have our names ready? Like an admission ticket? I don't like that.
en.STORY_CH11_OUTRO_14: Everyone hold tight to your own name and follow me. …To the Nameless Cathedral.
en.STORY_CH11_PREBOSS_01: At the heart of the breakwater, the black tide rose like a pillar. At its tip hung a colossal sickle-shaped engine.
en.STORY_CH11_PREBOSS_02: This is the lost-and-found office. The recovery period for drifting coordinates has ended.
en.STORY_CH11_PREBOSS_03: Anchored coordinates will now be harvested. A past clinging to the present obstructs navigation.
en.STORY_CH11_PREBOSS_04: The coordinates in my net are being pulled away. The anchored ones first… it's using them as bait.
en.STORY_CH11_PREBOSS_05: At Maeru's hip, the blue lantern tilted toward the tide as if being pulled.
en.STORY_CH11_PREBOSS_07: Pull still rising. Every sweep of that sickle raises the water at the wall by half a meter.
en.STORY_CH11_PREBOSS_08: Please choose. Release the coordinates, and the breakwater holds. Keep them, and the city drowns.
en.STORY_CH11_PREBOSS_09: Choose again?! We already saw that trick at the twin moons!
en.STORY_CH11_PREBOSS_11: I won't let go of the lantern or the wall. Twelve years ago I left someone behind. Never again.
en.STORY_CH11_PREBOSS_12: Good. I take the wall, Orsa takes the net. Captain, you just hold on tight to that lantern.
en.STORY_CH11_PREBOSS_13: Two shields against one wave. That's enough.
en.STORY_CH11_PREBOSS_14: And three guns against one sickle. Math done.
en.STORY_CH12_CAMP_01: In the sacristy beneath the cathedral, everyone sat around a single candle. The hymn seeped faintly through the walls.
en.STORY_CH12_CAMP_02: Let me sum up. Different lines, independent signatures, twenty. We have twelve. Eight to go.
en.STORY_CH12_CAMP_03: If a new timetable can be written, the current one can be discarded. Control's Final Timetable included.
en.STORY_CH12_CAMP_04: Is that why Control recognized the Navigator from the start? Because it knew whose wrist the recorder was on?
en.STORY_CH12_CAMP_05: …But who made this rule? The number twenty, the condition of independence. Someone designed this.
en.STORY_CH12_CAMP_06: Without thinking, everyone looked up at the speaker in the ceiling. Control, always so quick to cut in, said nothing this time.
en.STORY_CH12_CAMP_07: Silence is a signal too. If Control won't answer, it doesn't want to.
en.STORY_CH12_CAMP_08: Or it hasn't finished calculating. Either way, that's its problem.
en.STORY_CH12_CAMP_09: Whoever made the rule, every signature was someone's own choice. From Vera to Tiel. That's not a rule. That's people.
en.STORY_CH12_CAMP_10: Navigator, don't those signatures weigh on you?
en.STORY_CH12_CAMP_11: …A good answer. Your pulse didn't waver.
en.STORY_CH12_CAMP_12: Ha, already on to the next count? Fine. Eight. I'll open the way.
en.STORY_CH12_CAMP_13: That's enough for tonight. Tomorrow, the altar. …Before you sleep, call the name of the one beside you.
en.STORY_CH12_HARD_INTRO_01: In the ossuary beneath the cathedral, the hymn never stopped. Nameless plaques crowded every cold stone wall.
en.STORY_CH12_HARD_INTRO_02: The Choir Lock is down here. It's where the cathedral locked away the oldest names it collected.
en.STORY_CH12_HARD_INTRO_03: The seal signal's still alive. Even with the Prelate stopped, the names down here haven't been released.
en.STORY_CH12_HARD_INTRO_04: If they're the oldest names, they've waited the longest too.
en.STORY_CH12_HARD_INTRO_05: Someone stood at the ossuary entrance, leaning on a sword. She didn't turn even as footsteps approached.
en.STORY_CH12_HARD_INTRO_06: …She knows we're coming. But she hasn't said a word.
en.STORY_CH12_HARD_INTRO_07: That's a pilgrim guard's stance. A sword that watches over holy ground. We mustn't cross it lightly.
en.STORY_CH12_HARD_INTRO_08: Not drawing her sword is an answer in itself. We approach slowly.
en.STORY_CH12_HARD_OUTRO_01: With the sound of the Choir Lock cracking, the song fell silent. Letters rose, one by one, on every plaque in the ossuary.
en.STORY_CH12_HARD_OUTRO_02: …The hymn is concluded. I believed that kept within the song, no name would ever fade…
en.STORY_CH12_HARD_OUTRO_03: The names are going home. One, then another… Pulses outside are answering.
en.STORY_CH12_HARD_OUTRO_04: Seven hundred ten names unsealed. The oldest predates the Blackout.
en.STORY_CH12_HARD_OUTRO_05: Raen sheathed her sword and knelt on one knee before a single plaque.
en.STORY_CH12_HARD_OUTRO_06: …My fellow pilgrims. Now I can call them by name.
en.STORY_CH12_HARD_OUTRO_07: …So you stood here alone all this time to guard those names.
en.STORY_CH12_HARD_OUTRO_08: …Nothing left to guard. May I follow you?
en.STORY_CH12_HARD_OUTRO_09: You said a blade can't lie. Yours already answered. Let's go, Raen.
en.STORY_CH12_HARD_OUTRO_10: Behind the departing Lamplighters, the names going home echoed like quiet footsteps.
en.STORY_CH12_INTRO_01: Hundreds of names were carved above the cathedral door. Each time one was read aloud, its letters fell away like ash.
en.STORY_CH12_INTRO_02: The teeth fit. It's the key from the tide. We can open the door.
en.STORY_CH12_INTRO_03: Then let's open it. This name here is… huh? What did I just read?
en.STORY_CH12_INTRO_04: Roan, the name you read just vanished from the door. And from your memory.
en.STORY_CH12_INTRO_05: Your attention, please. Welcome to the Nameless Cathedral.
en.STORY_CH12_INTRO_06: Names will be collected as seal maintenance fees. Navigator, you are exempt.
en.STORY_CH12_INTRO_07: Exempt? Just the Navigator? Is this some VIP treatment again?
en.STORY_CH12_INTRO_08: A levy means it's spent maintaining something. We must first learn what this cathedral is sealing.
en.STORY_CH12_INTRO_09: The hymn has no lyrics. Only blanks where names should go. Our names are meant to fill them.
en.STORY_CH12_INTRO_10: Then we just don't say names? Eda, Eda, Eda… Phew, still there.
en.STORY_CH12_INTRO_11: Spend names sparingly. Keep calls short. If someone answers, that's your confirmation.
en.STORY_CH12_INTRO_12: The door opened. At the end of a long nave, thousands of candles burned on the altar in place of names.
en.STORY_CH12_INTRO_13: If it's one name per candle, over three thousand people have been taxed.
en.STORY_CH12_INTRO_14: Three thousand names. We give them all back. …We're going in.
en.STORY_CH12_MID_A_01: A levy ledger hung on every pillar of the nave. Beside each name, instead of a date, was stamped 'PAID IN FULL.'
en.STORY_CH12_MID_A_02: This isn't a list of the dead. Every one of them is alive. This cathedral taxes the names of the living.
en.STORY_CH12_MID_A_03: What happens to the people whose names are taken?
en.STORY_CH12_MID_A_04: They live. It's just that no one can call them anymore. Not their family. Not even themselves.
en.STORY_CH12_MID_A_05: That's terrifying. Um, the… the one with the cannon… uh, her name is…
en.STORY_CH12_MID_A_06: …Soren. It's me. It's okay, Eda. Your name came to me a beat late just now too.
en.STORY_CH12_MID_A_07: Wait, that one with the shield… we met at the dike… Damn it. It's right on the tip of my tongue.
en.STORY_CH12_MID_A_08: Orsa. I'll tell you as many times as it takes. If you forget, I'll simply say it again.
en.STORY_CH12_MID_A_09: The levy is speeding up. Call each other's names and listen for answers. If that stops, we stop.
en.STORY_CH12_MID_A_10: There's a pulse-like signal from the choir stalls. Steady. A signal that beats without a name.
en.STORY_CH12_MID_B_01: As the choir scattered, thirty-two rhythms carried on quietly beneath Tiel's fingertips.
en.STORY_CH12_MID_B_02: I'm Tiel. I was this cathedral's medic. I've remembered each person who lost their name by their pulse.
en.STORY_CH12_MID_B_03: Tiel pointed to the stone tablet behind the altar. Among the erased names, a single sentence remained whole.
en.STORY_CH12_MID_B_04: The final verse of this liturgy. 'When twenty independent signatures from different lines are gathered, a new timetable may be written.'
en.STORY_CH12_MID_B_05: Signatures… one per line. The patterns on the Navigator's recorder. Eleven so far, and the rule has never once broken.
en.STORY_CH12_MID_B_06: So without knowing it, we've been collecting the right to write something new?
en.STORY_CH12_MID_B_07: In that moment the recorder throbbed like a pulse. In time with Tiel's rhythm, a twelfth pattern was engraved.
en.STORY_CH12_MID_B_08: …It beats exactly with my rhythm. A mark that remains in place of a name. Far kinder than this cathedral.
en.STORY_CH12_MID_B_09: Until every name returns, I will remember your pulses.
en.STORY_CH12_MID_B_10: A new timetable… A page we write ourselves instead of a verdict? I like it!
en.STORY_CH12_MID_B_11: The levy signal beyond the altar just spiked. The cathedral's noticed us.
en.STORY_CH12_OUTRO_01: The priest's mask cracked and fell. Behind it, instead of a face, was a single blank name tag.
en.STORY_CH12_OUTRO_02: Collection… halted. Returning… seal maintenance fees.
en.STORY_CH12_OUTRO_03: …Without names, no one would ever be forgotten… If there were no names to call at all… no one would ever feel… they'd lost…
en.STORY_CH12_OUTRO_04: The three thousand candles on the altar flickered all at once. Each flame lifted a single name and flew out of the cathedral.
en.STORY_CH12_OUTRO_05: Pulses and names are locking back together. Thirty-two… no, all three thousand.
en.STORY_CH12_OUTRO_06: …Maeru. Captain of the Lamplighters. Sio's lantern is still lit. Everything's where it belongs.
en.STORY_CH12_OUTRO_07: Captain, don't you ever lose your name again! I'm going to call it a hundred times a day!
en.STORY_CH12_OUTRO_09: Wait. Some of the names that flew off are drifting south. Toward the desert.
en.STORY_CH12_OUTRO_10: The signal's drawing tracks on the sand. Tracks that aren't on any map. With a timetable attached.
en.STORY_CH12_OUTRO_11: A timetable for a train that doesn't exist. It's filling its passenger list with the stolen names.
en.STORY_CH12_OUTRO_12: If names are drifting with nowhere to return to, then they're coordinates I must recover as well.
en.STORY_CH12_OUTRO_13: Verdicts, twin moons, tides, a cathedral… and now sand? Fine. Bring it all on!
en.STORY_CH12_OUTRO_14: Twelve of twenty. And not a single name left behind. …We head for the desert.
en.STORY_CH12_PREBOSS_01: Atop the altar, a towering masked priest-engine swung its censer. Wherever the smoke touched, letters melted away.
en.STORY_CH12_PREBOSS_02: Payment notice. Seal maintenance funds are insufficient. Designating a high-value contributor.
en.STORY_CH12_PREBOSS_03: Lamplighter Captain Maeru. That name is hereby collected.
en.STORY_CH12_PREBOSS_04: The censer smoke wrapped around Maeru. And from every mouth, one name slipped away without a sound.
en.STORY_CH12_PREBOSS_05: Captain! …Captain, your name… what was it? I knew it a second ago.
en.STORY_CH12_PREBOSS_06: No, no… I call that name every day. Why won't it come…!
en.STORY_CH12_PREBOSS_08: Her pulse is unchanged. The heart remembers. But someone has to call her name.
en.STORY_CH12_PREBOSS_09: Only the recorder still shone with letters that hadn't gone out. In the exempt record, the name remained.
en.STORY_CH12_PREBOSS_10: As the Navigator called the name, Tiel tapped out a rhythm. Once, twice, at the pace of a heartbeat.
en.STORY_CH12_PREBOSS_11: Now. Everyone, call it with this rhythm.
en.STORY_CH12_PREBOSS_12: The recorder's light etched the name into the air. Tiel tapped a rhythm to match the letters.
en.STORY_CH12_PREBOSS_13: We can read it. Everyone, call it to this rhythm.
en.STORY_CH12_PREBOSS_15: Maeru. …Right, Maeru! Who could forget our captain's name!
en.STORY_CH12_PREBOSS_16: …I hear it. Maeru. That's my name.
en.STORY_CH12_PREBOSS_17: Requests to cancel collection are not accepted. Commencing re-collection.
en.STORY_CH12_PREBOSS_18: Take it as many times as you like. There are people here who'll call it back every time. …Everyone, names confirmed. Let's go!
en.STORY_CH13_CAMP_01: The desert night carried sound far. From the shade of a ruined relay post, the crackle of the fire rolled past the dunes.
en.STORY_CH13_CAMP_02: Eda, is that circuit of yours only good for lighting fires? You were half a beat late every fight.
en.STORY_CH13_CAMP_03: Because you kept cutting in front of me! Want me to shock you too next time?
en.STORY_CH13_CAMP_04: …Try it. But hit me properly. A half-hearted zap is more annoying.
en.STORY_CH13_CAMP_05: Ha. Being a courier wouldn't have been bad… but I'd never have had a night this loud.
en.STORY_CH13_CAMP_06: …Navigator, let me see the recorder. Something showed when the thirteenth was carved.
en.STORY_CH13_CAMP_07: At the very bottom, a scratch older than Vera's signature. Not a line pattern. …It looks like handwriting.
en.STORY_CH13_CAMP_08: All right. I won't write guesses. Only what I can confirm.
en.STORY_CH13_CAMP_09: …You can cover it if you want. Just don't carry it alone.
en.STORY_CH13_CAMP_10: Why the long faces? Aren't you the ones taking down a stationmaster tomorrow?
en.STORY_CH13_CAMP_11: We are! Shocking Rias comes after that!
en.STORY_CH13_CAMP_12: Bank the fire. We leave for the station at the dunes' edge at first light.
en.STORY_CH13_CAMP_CHOICE1_A: Hold out the recorder and ask her to look into it
en.STORY_CH13_CAMP_CHOICE1_B: Cover the mark with a sleeve
en.STORY_CH13_HARD_INTRO_01: At noon the mirage zone rippled like water. On the horizon, one train became three, then four.
en.STORY_CH13_HARD_INTRO_02: Interval between trains: 4.2 seconds. The same consist is being copied on a delay.
en.STORY_CH13_HARD_INTRO_03: Every bearing is false. There's only one real whistle. I'll pick it out.
en.STORY_CH13_HARD_INTRO_04: Ghost trains, and now mirages? Does this desert know anything but lies?
en.STORY_CH13_HARD_INTRO_05: The more lies around, the more honest the shot has to be. Just hit the real engine.
en.STORY_CH13_HARD_INTRO_06: Manifest fragments keep leaking from the engine's signal. Passengers the stationmaster never boarded are still out here.
en.STORY_CH13_HARD_INTRO_07: One line of footprints in the sand. Mirages don't leave footprints…
en.STORY_CH13_HARD_INTRO_08: If there are passengers left, we go. Mirage or not, even for one.
en.STORY_CH13_HARD_OUTRO_01: As the mirage lifted, the heat settled. Only real footprints remained in the sand.
en.STORY_CH13_HARD_OUTRO_02: …If it arrived nowhere… no one would ever be late…
en.STORY_CH13_HARD_OUTRO_03: …First time I've seen it. Tracks that prove you arrived. Mirages never leave any.
en.STORY_CH13_HARD_OUTRO_04: Hey, courier. In the life I didn't choose, I was someone like you. She looked awfully carefree.
en.STORY_CH13_HARD_OUTRO_05: Carefree? A courier? You know nothing. …I'm Zern. I needed a crew to run with. Count me in.
en.STORY_CH13_HARD_OUTRO_06: Welcome. We may be slow, but every one of us arrives.
en.STORY_CH13_HARD_OUTRO_07: So you admit you're slow. Zern, the lead spot's mine.
en.STORY_CH13_HARD_OUTRO_08: Every rail trace bends upward. Toward the capital. If we're late, it closes.
en.STORY_CH13_HARD_OUTRO_09: Late? I hate that word. Let's go!
en.STORY_CH13_INTRO_01: The sand stayed warm long after dark. From beyond dunes without a single rail, a whistle arrived first.
en.STORY_CH13_INTRO_02: No wheel ruts, no sleepers, and a train is running anyway. What do I even put in the scouting report?
en.STORY_CH13_INTRO_03: Write 'does not exist.' No mass, only signal. Twelve cars in the consist.
en.STORY_CH13_INTRO_04: I've caught the passenger manifest. Two thousand four hundred. …Every name recovered from the cathedral.
en.STORY_CH13_INTRO_05: Names freed from the cathedral. They should have gone home to their owners. Why are they on that train…
en.STORY_CH13_INTRO_06: A silhouette sat at every window. None looked out, and none got off.
en.STORY_CH13_INTRO_07: Attention, please. Lives you did not choose are also in service. Please board the car of your choice.
en.STORY_CH13_INTRO_08: The car of my choice… why does that sound so tempting?
en.STORY_CH13_INTRO_09: The more tempting the announcement, the steeper the fare. Has that speaker ever given anything away?
en.STORY_CH13_INTRO_10: They just got their names back and got dragged off again? Whose verdict was it this time?
en.STORY_CH13_INTRO_11: Not a verdict. A timetable. A route that doesn't exist is laid across this entire desert.
en.STORY_CH13_INTRO_12: A stop line was drawn in the sand. It bore an arrival mark, but no wheel tracks led away.
en.STORY_CH13_INTRO_13: Next scheduled stop: the northern dunes. If the train stops there, passengers can get off.
en.STORY_CH13_INTRO_14: Two thousand four hundred. We leave no name at those windows. North.
en.STORY_CH13_MID_A_01: When the train stopped, familiar faces surfaced in every window. Through the blowing sand, they smiled without a care.
en.STORY_CH13_MID_A_02: …That's me. Courier bag, no Lamplighter badge. She looks so relaxed.
en.STORY_CH13_MID_A_03: Third window: me, in a lab coat. If I'd accepted the offer to stay that year. The odds favored her.
en.STORY_CH13_MID_A_04: The manifest is shifting. The longer someone stares at a window, the harder their name sets into a passenger slot.
en.STORY_CH13_MID_A_05: Only the window before the Navigator stood empty. Not even a grain of sand showed in the glass.
en.STORY_CH13_MID_A_06: Same as on the glass plain. A person whose record is locked reflects nowhere.
en.STORY_CH13_MID_A_07: You have no unchosen life, Navigator. You chose everything already, that night.
en.STORY_CH13_MID_A_08: Don't listen. That broadcast pretends to answer and leaves only questions.
en.STORY_CH13_MID_A_09: …Right. I'll stop looking. Honestly, I was a little jealous of her.
en.STORY_CH13_MID_A_10: Eyes off the windows. The manifest signal comes from the front of the train. That's where we cut it.
en.STORY_CH13_MID_B_01: As the phantom passengers scattered, the sand began to cool. A thin thread of smoke rose from Rias's muzzle.
en.STORY_CH13_MID_B_02: See? They stand on the side you didn't choose and beckon. Follow them, and you're done.
en.STORY_CH13_MID_B_03: The manifest lock is broken. But as long as the train runs, the names will set again.
en.STORY_CH13_MID_B_04: So leave a mark. The last choice each of you actually made. That's your anchor.
en.STORY_CH13_MID_B_05: Last choice, huh… Deciding to come here this morning. Does that count?
en.STORY_CH13_MID_B_06: …That was quick. It counts. Doesn't have to be grand. Just real.
en.STORY_CH13_MID_B_07: Going back to Platform Seven after twelve years. That's my mark.
en.STORY_CH13_MID_B_08: The moment Rias scored her own mark into the sand, the recorder flared hot. The thirteenth pattern.
en.STORY_CH13_MID_B_09: …What's this? What did I just do?
en.STORY_CH13_MID_B_10: A line signature. Thirteen of twenty. Your choice was carved in as this line's ending.
en.STORY_CH13_MID_B_11: Choices aren't recovered. They're made new. …Fine, I'll come. Fall behind and I leave you.
en.STORY_CH13_MID_B_12: The timetable bears a stationmaster's seal. The station at the edge of the dunes. That's the root.
en.STORY_CH13_OUTRO_01: When the last car broke away, the station clock stopped for the first time. Long shadows scattered across the sand.
en.STORY_CH13_OUTRO_02: …Attention, please. This station is now… ending service.
en.STORY_CH13_OUTRO_03: …Even the lives you couldn't choose… I only wanted to give them one ride…
en.STORY_CH13_OUTRO_04: The names on the manifest are scattering. Back to their owners this time. The heartbeats are returning, one by one.
en.STORY_CH13_OUTRO_05: …Stupid stationmaster. If you wanted to give rides, you should've carried the living.
en.STORY_CH13_OUTRO_06: Still, I think I understand the wish. To have someone remember the roads not taken.
en.STORY_CH13_OUTRO_07: All two thousand six hundred names have found their receivers. Not one is left on the manifest.
en.STORY_CH13_OUTRO_08: Then the rails beneath them shook off the sand and rose. The steel curled into the sky and vanished into the clouds.
en.STORY_CH13_OUTRO_09: The rails lead upward. Coordinates… the capital loop. But its orientation is inverted.
en.STORY_CH13_OUTRO_10: A road that falls into the sky. I hope it's a weight a shield can bear.
en.STORY_CH13_OUTRO_11: The capital will soon terminate its connection to all outside lines.
en.STORY_CH13_OUTRO_12: You, however, may enter at any time, Navigator. Headquarters is waiting.
en.STORY_CH13_OUTRO_13: One invitation, a whole crew. Guess we're crashing together.
en.STORY_CH13_OUTRO_14: The desert's done. The capital's next. We count there too, one person at a time.
en.STORY_CH13_PREBOSS_01: The station at the edge of the dunes had no walls. Only pillars, a clock, and an endless string of cars stood on the sand.
en.STORY_CH13_PREBOSS_02: Welcome to Dune Station. This station is the terminus for lives not chosen.
en.STORY_CH13_PREBOSS_03: The cars are multiplying. Manifest at two thousand four hundred… no, it just hit two thousand six hundred.
en.STORY_CH13_PREBOSS_04: The greater the regret, the stronger the car. Your regrets make excellent fuel.
en.STORY_CH13_PREBOSS_05: Burning regret for fuel? Disgusting. I'm uncoupling every one of those cars.
en.STORY_CH13_PREBOSS_06: A car slid in among them. In its window, the Roan who never joined the Lamplighters waved.
en.STORY_CH13_PREBOSS_07: Roan, get away from that car. The manifest signal is winding toward you.
en.STORY_CH13_PREBOSS_08: Passenger Roan, would you care to transfer to the courier service? In that life, you lost no one.
en.STORY_CH13_PREBOSS_09: …Tempting. But these people aren't there. I'll pass.
en.STORY_CH13_PREBOSS_10: Good choice, Roan. A life with something to protect weighs more than a life with nothing lost.
en.STORY_CH13_PREBOSS_11: Aim for the couplings. One car at a time. One person at a time.
en.STORY_CH13_PREBOSS_12: The coupling intervals are uniform. Three seconds per car and it's cut.
en.STORY_CH13_PREBOSS_13: Three seconds is too long. Run!
en.STORY_CH14_CAMP_01: They hung a lantern in a concourse set right side up again. Outside, the lights of still-inverted streets hung like stars.
en.STORY_CH14_CAMP_02: The court had you for unauthorized departure, and now final signing authority. Navigator, the charges are piling up!
en.STORY_CH14_CAMP_03: Veon, you're grinning while you say that?
en.STORY_CH14_CAMP_04: Of course I'm grinning. I took that case under my name. More charges just means more for me to carry.
en.STORY_CH14_CAMP_05: But aren't you curious? Authority used once. I'd stay up all night pulling that apart.
en.STORY_CH14_CAMP_06: Deleted records leave recovery traces. Given time, I can verify it.
en.STORY_CH14_CAMP_07: Dig up the past later. Look at which way you're walking now.
en.STORY_CH14_CAMP_08: I look at the present, not the records. …But this is the Navigator's call.
en.STORY_CH14_CAMP_09: Understood. I'll save the coordinates of the deletion traces. Whatever turns up, we read it together.
en.STORY_CH14_CAMP_10: Good. That's right. The past isn't going anywhere.
en.STORY_CH14_CAMP_11: …You're a seriously weird team. Nobody suspects anybody. It's like a bug.
en.STORY_CH14_CAMP_12: Not a bug. A rule. Tomorrow, the central level, where the Auditor waits.
en.STORY_CH14_CAMP_CHOICE1_A: I want to know the truth
en.STORY_CH14_HARD_INTRO_01: The palace district was still upside down. Chandeliers sprouted from the floor, and staircases descended into the sky.
en.STORY_CH14_HARD_INTRO_02: My hacks don't work here. What's holding gravity isn't a device. It's that crown.
en.STORY_CH14_HARD_INTRO_03: So the crown is holding up the city. That must be heavy. Heavier still after so long.
en.STORY_CH14_HARD_INTRO_04: Artillery in an upside-down palace. If the shells fall upward, that's not on me.
en.STORY_CH14_HARD_INTRO_05: I'll handle the ballistic correction. Just tell me which way is falling.
en.STORY_CH14_HARD_INTRO_06: One faint signal under the palace. Encrypted. …Someone's watching us through a screen.
en.STORY_CH14_HARD_INTRO_07: If they're only watching, they have their reasons. We go down and ask. Without scaring them.
en.STORY_CH14_HARD_OUTRO_01: The sound of the crown cracking rang through the whole city. One by one, the inverted floors returned to their places.
en.STORY_CH14_HARD_OUTRO_02: …If there were no outside… no one would ever fall…
en.STORY_CH14_HARD_OUTRO_03: …The floor numbers match. Basement twelve is below ground again. After twelve years…
en.STORY_CH14_HARD_OUTRO_04: You held out well. May I ask your name?
en.STORY_CH14_HARD_OUTRO_05: Soa. …I've never talked with people this long without a screen.
en.STORY_CH14_HARD_OUTRO_06: Soa, you built that firewall solo, right? With two hackers, we'd be unbeatable.
en.STORY_CH14_HARD_OUTRO_07: …Can I come with you? Not from behind a screen. Beside you.
en.STORY_CH14_HARD_OUTRO_08: Of course. Behind a screen or beside us, we count everyone.
en.STORY_CH14_HARD_OUTRO_09: Found a shipping log in the palace records. Seed crates, addressed to the Garden of Zero Signal.
en.STORY_CH14_HARD_OUTRO_10: Seeds? The capital was sending flowers? …That feels ominous.
en.STORY_CH14_INTRO_01: The capital's sky lay beneath their feet. Shattered towers fell soundlessly toward the clouds.
en.STORY_CH14_INTRO_02: First time I've seen a building fall up. …Wait, are we the ones upside down?
en.STORY_CH14_INTRO_03: Both. Gravity points a different way in every district. 'Down' changes every three steps.
en.STORY_CH14_INTRO_04: So one misstep and you fall into the sky. Simple. Don't misstep.
en.STORY_CH14_INTRO_05: There's a train running upside down through the clouds! There are people in it, right?
en.STORY_CH14_INTRO_06: Capital population on record: thirty thousand. Living signals: half that. Scattered across the loop's twelve stations.
en.STORY_CH14_INTRO_07: Attention, please. The capital is now permanently isolated from all outside lines. Passengers, remain where you are.
en.STORY_CH14_INTRO_08: Permanent isolation? Locking up an entire city without so much as a verdict?
en.STORY_CH14_INTRO_09: The isolation order originates at the city's center. Directorate Headquarters.
en.STORY_CH14_INTRO_11: A single line of light ran straight through the middle of the inverted sky. Every distant rail bent toward it.
en.STORY_CH14_INTRO_12: That line isn't on any route map. But the signal of every line leans toward it.
