en.STORY_CH14_INTRO_13: Beautiful. Though anything that straight has usually been pulled taut by force.
en.STORY_CH14_INTRO_14: Catch the falling first. We dig up what that line is at Headquarters.
en.STORY_CH14_MID_A_01: On the station wall leading to Headquarters, a protocol was carved upside down. Its letters dripped toward the ceiling.
en.STORY_CH14_MID_A_02: Emergency Protocol Zero. 'Isolate the capital from all loss outside.' Not an accident. An order.
en.STORY_CH14_MID_A_03: The inversion isn't a side effect of the isolation. It is the isolation. It erased the very direction called 'out.'
en.STORY_CH14_MID_A_04: No way out means no way in for rescuers. Like me, twelve years ago. They'd arrive too late.
en.STORY_CH14_MID_A_05: Building fall rate rising three meters a minute. In six hours, even the lowest levels drop into the sky.
en.STORY_CH14_MID_A_06: Navigator, Headquarters remembers you. The main gate is always open to you.
en.STORY_CH14_MID_A_07: The main gate's open? That's practically advertising a trap.
en.STORY_CH14_MID_A_08: They're only letting the Navigator in. What are we, luggage?
en.STORY_CH14_MID_A_09: One signal near a side door. Someone in the middle of the inversion zone keeps opening and shutting it.
en.STORY_CH14_MID_A_10: We don't use the main gate. We cross the falling districts to that side door. Within six hours.
en.STORY_CH14_MID_B_01: Perin tapped in the last command, and every 'down' in the district aligned. Drifting dust settled on the floor.
en.STORY_CH14_MID_B_02: Ta-da. Everyone's different 'down,' bound to one reference plane. Just this district, though.
en.STORY_CH14_MID_B_03: You turned the inversion controls against themselves? Without calculating?
en.STORY_CH14_MID_B_04: The devices do the math. I just lie to them. 'This is down.'
en.STORY_CH14_MID_B_05: At that moment the recorder lit up. A fourteenth pattern surfaced on the wrist, sharp and clear.
en.STORY_CH14_MID_B_06: Huh? My hack on your wrist? …No. That's not something I did. That's something I chose.
en.STORY_CH14_MID_B_08: With the plane aligned, a Headquarters terminal woke. An old authority register scrolled across the screen.
en.STORY_CH14_MID_B_09: Admin list. Director, control chief, track supervisor… huh, what's this at the top?
en.STORY_CH14_MID_B_10: 'Record Navigator: final signing authority.' Authority exercised: once. Details deleted.
en.STORY_CH14_MID_B_11: …Turn it off. The people falling come first.
en.STORY_CH14_OUTRO_01: When the scale broke, the falling buildings stopped. Dust drifted slowly down, in the right direction.
en.STORY_CH14_OUTRO_02: …Audit concluded. The load… cannot be measured.
en.STORY_CH14_OUTRO_03: …If no one ever came back… nothing would ever collapse…
en.STORY_CH14_OUTRO_04: No one returning, nothing collapsing. Not wrong math. Just not math anyone can live with.
en.STORY_CH14_OUTRO_05: All capital districts normal. Isolation lifted. Fifteen thousand living signals reconnected to the outside lines.
en.STORY_CH14_OUTRO_06: Fifteen thousand people can send word outside now, right? Wow, my voltage is spiking!
en.STORY_CH14_OUTRO_07: Every terminal in Headquarters lit at once. The original path of the isolation protocol streaked across the screens.
en.STORY_CH14_OUTRO_08: The original source isn't here. The Garden of Zero Signal. The capital's protocol was a copy.
en.STORY_CH14_OUTRO_09: The original isn't preparing isolation. It's preparing a reset. Its target… the memory of every line.
en.STORY_CH14_OUTRO_10: Beyond the righted sky, the line of light had grown sharper. Now even the desert rails reached it.
en.STORY_CH14_OUTRO_11: The terminal has a name for that line. 'The Last Line.' A plan to bind every route into a single terminus.
en.STORY_CH14_OUTRO_12: Navigator, the garden's flowers will bloom soon. A world without pain is near.
en.STORY_CH14_OUTRO_13: A memory reset? My least favorite command. No system gets to choose a person's direction. I'll wreck it all the way.
en.STORY_CH14_OUTRO_14: We don't need a peace bought by forgetting. To the garden.
en.STORY_CH14_PREBOSS_01: The central audit chamber was a colossal scale. On one pan sat the capital; on the other, nothing at all.
en.STORY_CH14_PREBOSS_02: The audit begins. The capital's load will now be measured. Please do not move.
en.STORY_CH14_PREBOSS_03: Those readings are wrong. It isn't weighing buildings. It's assigning load to each life sign.
en.STORY_CH14_PREBOSS_04: The will to return is judged an overload. The wish to go home is what collapses the structure.
en.STORY_CH14_PREBOSS_05: The wish to go home is an overload? Some people held on for twelve years on that wish alone.
en.STORY_CH14_PREBOSS_06: Oh, I get the scale's logic. No one wanting to leave means the city never shakes. Worst bug ever.
en.STORY_CH14_PREBOSS_07: The Record Navigator is excluded from measurement. Authority holders are not subject to audit.
en.STORY_CH14_PREBOSS_09: The isolation protocol is locked into the scale's axle. Break it and the whole capital gets its reference plane back.
en.STORY_CH14_PREBOSS_10: No need to weigh us. Every one of us has somewhere to return to.
en.STORY_CH14_PREBOSS_11: Then we're heavy people. Good. Let's go in heavy!
en.STORY_CH14_PREBOSS_12: Overload? Great! Pile my weight on too!
en.STORY_CH14_PREBOSS_13: The scale tipped. The whole capital rang out once, deep and loud.
en.STORY_CH15_CAMP_01: They built a fire in a maintenance tunnel the flowers couldn't reach. Only where the scent ended could everyone breathe properly.
en.STORY_CH15_CAMP_02: I used to be a garden porter. Hauled seed crates, drew water. Nothing special, right?
en.STORY_CH15_CAMP_03: Nothing special? No one carrying seeds means no flowers!
en.STORY_CH15_CAMP_04: …Huh. You're the first to put it that way.
en.STORY_CH15_CAMP_05: …Mind if I confess something too? What I saw in the flowers.
en.STORY_CH15_CAMP_06: An old station canteen. Sio was sitting next to Maeru, laughing.
en.STORY_CH15_CAMP_08: I knew Sio too. Not for long. I didn't realize I still remembered that laugh.
en.STORY_CH15_CAMP_10: Thanks, Navigator. Words come easier by a warm fire.
en.STORY_CH15_CAMP_11: …I remember that laugh too. Brighter than any lantern.
en.STORY_CH15_CAMP_12: Good memories are too precious for bait. I'm not giving any away tomorrow. Not even to the gardener.
en.STORY_CH15_CAMP_CHOICE1_A: Ask to hear more about Sio
en.STORY_CH15_HARD_INTRO_01: The air in the greenhouse was heavy. Drops beaded on the glass roof hung in midair, never falling.
en.STORY_CH15_HARD_INTRO_02: Time runs at a third of outside speed. One hour here is three hours out there.
en.STORY_CH15_HARD_INTRO_03: Never been in the greenhouse either. Porters weren't allowed this far.
en.STORY_CH15_HARD_INTRO_04: Deeper in, a single flower keeps blooming and wilting. Like a pulse.
en.STORY_CH15_HARD_INTRO_05: That's the Zero Bloom's core. Even with the gardener down, if that survives it'll sprout again.
en.STORY_CH15_HARD_INTRO_06: There's an herbal smell in the air. Someone's been growing something in here.
en.STORY_CH15_HARD_INTRO_07: We check it down to the roots. Time runs slow here, so we run fast.
en.STORY_CH15_HARD_OUTRO_01: When the last petal fell, the suspended drops came down all at once. Slow time fell like rain.
en.STORY_CH15_HARD_OUTRO_02: …If only we went back to the start… a world where no one had lost anything…
en.STORY_CH15_HARD_OUTRO_03: …Oh my, rain. In all the time Bael's been here, it's never rained.
en.STORY_CH15_HARD_OUTRO_04: The Zero Bloom's withered. Now the garden's just a garden.
en.STORY_CH15_HARD_OUTRO_05: Then I'll take just one seed. To plant somewhere it can bloom again, in time that flows properly.
en.STORY_CH15_HARD_OUTRO_06: Good idea. Let's plant it together at the next camp.
en.STORY_CH15_HARD_OUTRO_07: Come with us, Bael. We're always short on herbalists.
en.STORY_CH15_HARD_OUTRO_08: Hehe, all right. Just match my pace, slowly.
en.STORY_CH15_HARD_OUTRO_09: Artillery signals from east and west. The civil war has begun.
en.STORY_CH15_HARD_OUTRO_10: …Then 'slowly' will have to wait. Let's go.
en.STORY_CH15_INTRO_01: Every season's scent rose at once in the garden. Spring blossoms, summer grass, and first snow, all from a single field.
en.STORY_CH15_INTRO_02: …Everyone's pulse is slowing. The tension is draining away far too fast.
en.STORY_CH15_INTRO_03: I feel it too. Warm, like right before sleep. …Places like this are the most dangerous.
en.STORY_CH15_INTRO_04: The whole garden is one server. Every flower stores a memory fragment. How many… I can't even count.
en.STORY_CH15_INTRO_05: Attention, please. Remain in your happiest moment. There is no need to go further.
en.STORY_CH15_INTRO_06: 'No need to go further' is the most suspicious line yet. Everyone who stopped for it is right over there.
en.STORY_CH15_INTRO_07: People sat all through the flowers. Every one smiled with open eyes, and none of them stood.
en.STORY_CH15_INTRO_08: …They're smiling, but nobody answers. Quieter than echoforms.
en.STORY_CH15_INTRO_09: Breathing and pulse are normal. No injuries. But I can't tell how many years they've sat like that.
en.STORY_CH15_INTRO_10: By signal count, seven thousand. Including people brought here from the capital.
en.STORY_CH15_INTRO_11: Reset preparation signal from the core. When the bloom completes, every line's memory will be overwritten by this one field.
en.STORY_CH15_INTRO_12: It's warm and nice… but for some reason I can't make a fist.
en.STORY_CH15_INTRO_13: Let's not step on the flowers. Somebody's best day is inside each one.
en.STORY_CH15_INTRO_14: Seven thousand. We get every one of them up. Happiness is given back to the waking, not the sleeping.
en.STORY_CH15_MID_A_01: The deeper they went into the field, the thicker the scent. With every step, their footsteps sounded farther away.
en.STORY_CH15_MID_A_02: …Oh, it's the base with the lights on. Everyone's laughing, and I can smell warm soup…
en.STORY_CH15_MID_A_03: Eda, that's not real! …Wait, what's happening to me? It's the day someone called my name out loud…
en.STORY_CH15_MID_A_04: Snap out of it. The flowers don't erase memory. They keep only your safest moment and close every other road.
en.STORY_CH15_MID_A_05: Right now we're each standing in our safest place. That's why none of us can walk forward.
en.STORY_CH15_MID_A_06: The flower before the Navigator showed only one scene. A stalled carriage, a quiet seat, eyelids closing.
en.STORY_CH15_MID_A_07: I remember the moment you were most at peace, Navigator. That seat, as you closed your eyes.
en.STORY_CH15_MID_A_08: …Platform Seven. That was the most peaceful place? That's where we lost someone.
en.STORY_CH15_MID_A_09: Eyes off the flowers. Navigator, Eda, Veon. Follow my voice.
en.STORY_CH15_MID_A_10: …There's a path of withered flowers farther in. Someone cut it on purpose.
en.STORY_CH15_MID_B_01: When the garden keepers fell, the flowers around them bowed their heads as one. The sweet scent thinned for a moment.
en.STORY_CH15_MID_B_02: Phew, done. I liked watching you fight. The way you trust each other with your backs.
en.STORY_CH15_MID_B_03: Have you been alone all this time? In this garden?
en.STORY_CH15_MID_B_04: Yeah. Everyone sat down by the flowers. My sister too. She cries when I wake her, so I couldn't.
en.STORY_CH15_MID_B_05: But I'd rather be with you, in a tomorrow I don't know, than in a comfortable past. Can I come?
en.STORY_CH15_MID_B_06: While Karn waited for an answer, the recorder answered first. The fifteenth pattern.
en.STORY_CH15_MID_B_07: Ooh, the recorder answered first. Says you passed.
en.STORY_CH15_MID_B_08: …Passed? That was a test? Didn't know. Glad, though.
en.STORY_CH15_MID_B_09: Fifteen of twenty. Five signatures left.
en.STORY_CH15_MID_B_10: The path Karn cut runs all the way to the core. The gardener is at its end.
en.STORY_CH15_MID_B_11: We'll wake your sister together on the way back. That's a promise.
en.STORY_CH15_OUTRO_01: As the closed flower withered, the garden's scent drained away all at once. Across the field, people began to rise.
en.STORY_CH15_OUTRO_03: …I only wished… to let you stay somewhere… it didn't hurt…
en.STORY_CH15_OUTRO_04: Look, my sister's getting up. She's crying. …But she's walking out.
en.STORY_CH15_OUTRO_05: Crying is fine. Walking out is what matters. I'll check her pulse.
en.STORY_CH15_OUTRO_06: All seven thousand conscious. No memory loss.
en.STORY_CH15_OUTRO_07: Then the roots at the garden's core flared red. The reset authority's signal split in two and raced toward both horizons.
en.STORY_CH15_OUTRO_08: Hey, the authority's running! Sent east and west at the same time!
en.STORY_CH15_OUTRO_09: Receivers: the queens of the Eastern and Western Lines. If either approves, the other's evacuation route is scrapped for good.
en.STORY_CH15_OUTRO_10: Succession claims from two lines have been received simultaneously. Please await the result.
en.STORY_CH15_OUTRO_11: …It means civil war. It won't be long before the guns can be heard from here.
en.STORY_CH15_OUTRO_12: I said an unknown tomorrow over a comfortable past. …So let's go protect that tomorrow first.
en.STORY_CH15_OUTRO_13: An entire evacuation route could vanish. We go and stop it. We save both.
en.STORY_CH15_PREBOSS_01: At the garden's core, one enormous flower stood closed. Around it, translucent petals floated like shields.
en.STORY_CH15_PREBOSS_02: Welcome to the garden. This is the repository of your happiest moments.
en.STORY_CH15_PREBOSS_03: Those petals… they're my memory. The base with the lights on. Everyone's laughing.
en.STORY_CH15_PREBOSS_04: Mine's there too. The canteen. …Sio, too.
en.STORY_CH15_PREBOSS_05: Every attack shatters a memory. Will you break your most precious moments with your own hands?
en.STORY_CH15_PREBOSS_06: …I've already given one away. It hurt. But I could see ahead.
en.STORY_CH15_PREBOSS_07: Memories don't live only in petals. They stay in the pulse, in the fingertips. Shattered, they still beat again.
en.STORY_CH15_PREBOSS_08: Back down from something hiding behind memories, and the memories become hostages.
en.STORY_CH15_PREBOSS_09: Navigator, your seat has been kept empty. You may rest there again whenever you wish.
en.STORY_CH15_PREBOSS_10: That seat stays empty, and we move on. The Navigator is here, with us.
en.STORY_CH15_PREBOSS_11: …Sorry, Sio. This time I'm looking ahead instead of at your laugh.
en.STORY_CH15_PREBOSS_12: Me too! We can light the base up again. As many times as it takes!
en.STORY_CH15_PREBOSS_13: Aim for the stems between the petals. Whatever memories break, we build again when we're home.
en.STORY_CH16_CAMP_01: Behind the field hospital, four medics sat around a fire steeped in the smell of antiseptic.
en.STORY_CH16_CAMP_02: Noar, how many did you see today? I had twenty-one.
en.STORY_CH16_CAMP_03: Thirty-four. …I don't like counting, but if I don't, I forget.
en.STORY_CH16_CAMP_04: I know. I counted to the end of the evacuation line too. So I wouldn't forget.
en.STORY_CH16_CAMP_05: Write the pulse beside each number. Then the numbers stay people.
en.STORY_CH16_CAMP_06: At the edge of the firelight, Eda sat hugging her knees. Her circuit glowed dimmer than usual.
en.STORY_CH16_CAMP_07: …Honestly, I'm scared. Echoforms are fine, but people shooting people… it's so scary.
en.STORY_CH16_CAMP_08: I'm glad someone's scared. War makes people forget that first.
en.STORY_CH16_CAMP_09: Eda, it's okay to say you're scared. The one who says it out loud is the bravest.
en.STORY_CH16_CAMP_10: …Heh, it's warm next to you, Navigator. Feels like I'm charging a little.
en.STORY_CH16_CAMP_11: Sixteen… every one a person. With this many of us, it's okay to be scared.
en.STORY_CH16_CAMP_12: Tomorrow… I'll go scared. But I'll still go.
en.STORY_CH16_CAMP_CHOICE1_B: Show her the patterns on the recorder
en.STORY_CH16_HARD_INTRO_01: The throne car circled the loop line without stopping. Even after the crown was dismantled, as if awaiting someone's command.
en.STORY_CH16_HARD_INTRO_02: It's unmanned. But its batteries are aimed at both capitals at once.
en.STORY_CH16_HARD_INTRO_03: …There's someone in the next car. One pulse. Very steady, unwavering.
en.STORY_CH16_HARD_INTRO_04: A throne without a crown. Let's go see who's guarding it.
en.STORY_CH16_HARD_INTRO_05: Sometimes a throne is better left empty. Let's go teach it that.
en.STORY_CH16_HARD_INTRO_06: Reload cycle: twelve minutes. Nine minutes to the next shot.
en.STORY_CH16_HARD_INTRO_07: Nine minutes is enough. Not one shell lands on either capital.
en.STORY_CH16_HARD_OUTRO_01: One by one, the Sovereign Engine's barrels sank. At the end of the line, the throne car finally stopped.
en.STORY_CH16_HARD_OUTRO_02: …If only there were orders… no one would ever lose their way…
en.STORY_CH16_HARD_OUTRO_03: That night, a long table was set in the junction's waiting hall. The two queens sat at its eastern and western ends.
en.STORY_CH16_HARD_OUTRO_04: …Western Queen. By the rites, the guest raises her cup first.
en.STORY_CH16_HARD_OUTRO_05: Don't know the rites, Eastern Queen. But bread gets split in half. You know that much?
en.STORY_CH16_HARD_OUTRO_06: …We know it. Even our forebears' rites wrote down that much.
en.STORY_CH16_HARD_OUTRO_07: The name's Teran. …Two crowns at one table. No order ever showed me that.
en.STORY_CH16_HARD_OUTRO_08: I'm no one's knight anymore. But if another wrong order comes, I'll refuse it at your side.
en.STORY_CH16_HARD_OUTRO_10: Soldiers from both sides are asleep in the same tent. No need to count tonight. Everyone came back.
en.STORY_CH16_INTRO_01: Gunsmoke hung over the junction where the two lines met. Gold banners flew over the eastern rails, red cloth over the western.
en.STORY_CH16_INTRO_02: Hear us, people of the Eastern Line. The lawful heir to the Directorate's charter is the Eastern Line alone.
en.STORY_CH16_INTRO_03: The seal and the rites our forebears left us are the proof. We shall protect all through order.
en.STORY_CH16_INTRO_04: Charter, sure. Western Line, listen up. Paper doesn't fill stomachs.
en.STORY_CH16_INTRO_05: We've got thirty-eight thousand mouths. The crown goes to whoever feeds them. Done.
en.STORY_CH16_INTRO_06: One talks like an old decree, the other like a market stall. Both equally loud.
en.STORY_CH16_INTRO_07: Both batteries are sighted across the junction. One shot and the fighting starts.
en.STORY_CH16_INTRO_08: Refugee signals: forty thousand on the east side. Seventy-eight thousand in all, stuck at the junction.
en.STORY_CH16_INTRO_09: Attention, please. The victorious line will merge all lines. Passengers, please await the outcome.
en.STORY_CH16_INTRO_10: Merge? So the winner swallows everything. What kind of succession is that?
en.STORY_CH16_INTRO_11: The authority that flew out of the garden came here. If those crowns get hold of it…
en.STORY_CH16_INTRO_12: The winner can erase the loser's evacuation route. Permanently.
en.STORY_CH16_INTRO_13: So whoever wins, tens of thousands on the other side lose their way.
en.STORY_CH16_INTRO_14: Crowns aren't our business. People are. We save both sides.
en.STORY_CH16_MID_A_01: Inside the captured signal house, succession papers printed without pause. The paper never stopped, but there was only one signature line.
en.STORY_CH16_MID_A_02: These aren't succession papers. They're merger orders. One signature from the victor binds every evacuation route into a single track.
en.STORY_CH16_MID_A_03: Every line into one? I've seen this structure… It's identical to the line of light over the capital.
en.STORY_CH16_MID_A_04: …It's the Last Line in miniature. Every route into a single terminus. This war is a rehearsal.
en.STORY_CH16_MID_A_05: Do the two queens fight knowing this, or not knowing?
en.STORY_CH16_MID_A_06: I'd bet not knowing. If they knew, both would've lowered their guns.
en.STORY_CH16_MID_A_07: Navigator, the rehearsal proceeds smoothly. One signature is enough. You remember that, don't you?
en.STORY_CH16_MID_A_08: …That broadcast keeps talking only to the Navigator. It's creepy.
en.STORY_CH16_MID_A_09: If their world ends with one signature, we gather twenty. That's our answer.
en.STORY_CH16_MID_A_10: One field hospital signal. Wounded from both sides tied to one channel. Someone linked them on purpose.
en.STORY_CH16_MID_B_01: When the lancers withdrew, only the smell of antiseptic remained in the tent. A single lantern lit forty-two cots.
en.STORY_CH16_MID_B_02: I linked the medical signal into one. When one side hurts, the other hears it too.
en.STORY_CH16_MID_B_03: A way of sharing pulses. It resembles my rhythm records. Far gentler, though.
en.STORY_CH16_MID_B_04: It isn't gentle. Once you can hear it, it just gets harder to shoot.
en.STORY_CH16_MID_B_05: …The guns on the front have thinned. That signal must have reached the trenches.
en.STORY_CH16_MID_B_06: Then the recorder glowed quietly. Without a sound, the sixteenth pattern was carved.
en.STORY_CH16_MID_B_07: …Is this a signature? I haven't promised anything.
en.STORY_CH16_MID_B_08: You already did. You counted forty-two as one.
en.STORY_CH16_MID_B_09: Then I'll keep the record. Not who won, but who came back.
en.STORY_CH16_MID_B_10: Sixteen of twenty. …That mark beneath the first pattern looks sharper today.
en.STORY_CH16_MID_B_11: The lancers fell back toward the junction. First, we secure the evacuation route for the wounded.
en.STORY_CH16_OUTRO_01: When the lance broke, the gunsmoke over the junction lifted. Gold banners and red cloth stirred in the same wind.
en.STORY_CH16_OUTRO_03: …If all were one… there would never again be anything to fight over…
en.STORY_CH16_OUTRO_04: So even the crown wanted peace. Only its method was wrong.
en.STORY_CH16_OUTRO_05: Peace? Peace from erasing one side is just a graveyard.
en.STORY_CH16_OUTRO_06: You are the Navigator, we are told. To which of the two lines would you give the crown?
en.STORY_CH16_OUTRO_07: Ha. Nobody needs it, huh. …Can't argue with that today.
en.STORY_CH16_OUTRO_08: Wear it together? That answer is not in the rites. …But we shall write it down.
en.STORY_CH16_OUTRO_09: An old succession seal rolled out of the broken crown. A set of coordinates was engraved on its back.
en.STORY_CH16_OUTRO_10: Coordinates decoded. The Archive of Afterglow. The true succession record is kept there.
en.STORY_CH16_OUTRO_11: The Archive… where our forebears were said to have sealed away 'the original of that night.'
en.STORY_CH16_OUTRO_12: Original or whatever, bring it. If it says who signed first that night, we'll know who started all this.
en.STORY_CH16_OUTRO_13: At those words, the old mark beneath the recorder's first pattern flickered once, cold.
en.STORY_CH16_OUTRO_14: The Archive of Afterglow will soon put its records in order. Navigator, there is no need to hurry. The ending is already written.
en.STORY_CH16_OUTRO_15: …We go to the Archive. Whatever is written there, we read it together.
en.STORY_CH16_PREBOSS_01: At the heart of the junction, the two queens stood on the same platform for the first time. Between them, a machine with a silver lance descended.
en.STORY_CH16_PREBOSS_02: My soldiers in the trenches heard the east groaning and wept. Can't shoot like this.
en.STORY_CH16_PREBOSS_03: We received the same report. It is not in the rites, but we shall permit the guns to rest a while.
en.STORY_CH16_PREBOSS_04: Warning. Truce is treason. The succession procedure requires a single victor.
en.STORY_CH16_PREBOSS_05: The medical signal is classified as an attack on command. Eliminate its source.
en.STORY_CH16_PREBOSS_06: …It means me. It's all right. I set the signal to hold even if I'm cut off.
en.STORY_CH16_PREBOSS_07: We won't let you be cut off. Noar is one of us.
en.STORY_CH16_PREBOSS_08: Lamplighters? …Hey. That tin can with the spear, whose side is it on?
en.STORY_CH16_PREBOSS_09: The crown's. Not ours, nor the Western Queen's. …Only now do we see it.
en.STORY_CH16_PREBOSS_10: Both sovereigns, please stand back. The lance will not stop until a victor is decided.
en.STORY_CH16_PREBOSS_11: A victor? Nobody needs one. I'm snapping that lance first.
en.STORY_CH16_PREBOSS_12: You two, stay back. We'll hold here.
en.STORY_CH16_PREBOSS_13: …Ha, giving me orders? Fine. Just for today.
en.STORY_CH16_PREBOSS_14: Impertinent, but right. Eastern guard, stand down.
en.STORY_CH17_CAMP_01: Under the camp lantern, Seb opened the tablet from the original stacks. The turning pages fell silent, and a time from the night of the Blackout surfaced.
en.STORY_CH17_CAMP_02: I'll read it exactly as written. '23:52. Final Timetable draft, first signature. Signatory: Record Navigator.'
en.STORY_CH17_CAMP_03: The recorder shook, burning hot. Now everyone knew whose back it had been, signing before the control console.
en.STORY_CH17_CAMP_04: '00:51. The draft halts not only the lines, but people's choices. Irreversible.'
en.STORY_CH17_CAMP_05: 'The Navigator erases their own memory and is sealed at Platform Seven. Condition for scrapping: twenty signatures from different lines.'
en.STORY_CH17_CAMP_06: The last line was handwritten. 'Let the next Navigator choose again.'
en.STORY_CH17_CAMP_07: There's one appendix. A record of a rescuer who guarded the sealed seat to the end. …Name: Sio.
en.STORY_CH17_CAMP_08: Only the sound of the burning wick remained. No one spoke first.
en.STORY_CH17_CAMP_09: …I once asked who made this rule. So one person's signature can't be overturned by one person alone. The answer was right here.
en.STORY_CH17_CAMP_10: So you're the one Sio guarded to the end. …So. What will you choose this time?
en.STORY_CH17_CAMP_11: Good. From where you stopped twelve years ago, this time we go together.
en.STORY_CH17_CAMP_12: I took over that case, remember? Here's my verdict. Not guilty! And everyone here is an accomplice!
en.STORY_CH17_CAMP_13: Accepted. That settles it. We leave twelve years ago where it is.
en.STORY_CH17_CAMP_14: Tell Sio too. …Though she'd have laughed before you finished. That's who she was.
en.STORY_CH17_CAMP_15: Choosing is yours. Holding the line is ours. …Tomorrow, I count everyone again.
en.STORY_CH17_HARD_INTRO_01: Deep in the stacks, each sheet of parchment was written over a hundred times. New letters kept growing over the scraped-away ones.
en.STORY_CH17_HARD_INTRO_02: This is the palimpsest layer. The names everyone thought were erased are all pressed underneath. Thousands of them.
en.STORY_CH17_HARD_INTRO_03: The layers are offset by half a beat each. The deeper, the more genuine. Overwrites always pile up on top.
en.STORY_CH17_HARD_INTRO_04: Then we go all the way down. If there are people pinned under there without their names.
en.STORY_CH17_HARD_INTRO_05: Beyond the parchment heaps, a gun sight flashed. Someone was still standing watch at this depth.
en.STORY_CH17_HARD_INTRO_06: A live battery in an archive? Didn't expect guards. Guess we should say hello.
en.STORY_CH17_HARD_INTRO_07: The aim keeps tracking us. Echoforms can't hold aim this long. It's a person.
en.STORY_CH17_HARD_INTRO_08: Weapons down. We don't fire first.
en.STORY_CH17_HARD_OUTRO_01: When the Palimpsest Core stopped, the layered parchment peeled away sheet by sheet. The ink at the bottom shone as if freshly written.
en.STORY_CH17_HARD_OUTRO_02: Names. People overwritten out of existence since the Blackout. Three thousand… no, over four thousand.
en.STORY_CH17_HARD_OUTRO_03: Like drifting coordinates. Abandoned, but never gone. We'll send every one of them home.
en.STORY_CH17_HARD_OUTRO_04: 'The unrecorded die twice.' An old saying. …Today, no one died a second time.
en.STORY_CH17_HARD_OUTRO_05: My watch is over. The shelves I guarded are gone, so now I'll guard the people outside them.
en.STORY_CH17_HARD_OUTRO_06: You're bringing the whole battery? That's a heavy load.
en.STORY_CH17_HARD_OUTRO_07: 'What is heavy endures.' This one's a real quote. Source: the plaque over the archive gate.
en.STORY_CH17_HARD_OUTRO_08: The restored names became motes of light and drifted up through the vents in the ceiling, each on its way back to its own line.
en.STORY_CH17_HARD_OUTRO_09: The names are on their way. So are we. The Last Line won't wait for us.
en.STORY_CH17_INTRO_01: Pages turned without pause on shelves that climbed to the ceiling. The Archive of Afterglow was rewriting history even now.
en.STORY_CH17_INTRO_02: The titles on the spines change every three seconds. It's not the same book. A different past keeps getting shelved in the same slot.
en.STORY_CH17_INTRO_03: The broken crown's coordinates pointed here. So the real succession record is somewhere inside.
en.STORY_CH17_INTRO_04: The record of how the war stopped is already fading. The wounded are still exactly where they were.
en.STORY_CH17_INTRO_05: Wait, our names were in this book… just a second ago? Now it's blank!
en.STORY_CH17_INTRO_06: Then the old speakers between the shelves chimed the same note at once.
en.STORY_CH17_INTRO_07: Attention, please. This archive is currently organizing intervention records.
en.STORY_CH17_INTRO_08: Your footsteps, passengers, are unnecessary footnotes to history. They will be deleted shortly.
en.STORY_CH17_INTRO_09: Your record alone, Navigator, will remain untouched. Regulations require that originals be preserved.
en.STORY_CH17_INTRO_10: 'Original,' huh. That voice gets oddly tender whenever the Navigator comes up.
en.STORY_CH17_INTRO_11: Original? Then the Navigator's case file I took over must be in here too. I'm reading it first!
en.STORY_CH17_INTRO_12: People before books. We secure our own records before they're erased.
en.STORY_CH17_INTRO_13: …Navigator, check the recorder. Are all sixteen signatures still there?
en.STORY_CH17_INTRO_14: The sixteen marks had not faded. In the whole archive, theirs was the only light that could not be erased.
en.STORY_CH17_INTRO_15: Then that recorder is our reference point. We head deeper in, where the deletion signal is strongest.
en.STORY_CH17_MID_A_01: The expedition log on the reading desk turned its own pages, bleaching white line by line. What it erased were the Lamplighters' names.
en.STORY_CH17_MID_A_02: The first page is empty. The dead line, the rescue signal, the day I joined. All of it is becoming something that never happened.
en.STORY_CH17_MID_A_03: It's not just the paper. Your name just came out of my mouth a beat late.
en.STORY_CH17_MID_A_04: It's erasing us in the order we joined. At this rate, all sixteen of us are blanks within six hours.
en.STORY_CH17_MID_A_05: Once the records go, we'll be strangers to each other. Along with every reason we fought together.
en.STORY_CH17_MID_A_06: The heart remembers. But when the paper forgets first, the mind follows.
en.STORY_CH17_MID_A_07: Delete commands always leave logs. If I trace it back… huh? Someone's writing it all back in.
en.STORY_CH17_MID_A_08: One signal at the center of the stacks. It's writing faster than the archive can erase. It's a person.
en.STORY_CH17_MID_A_09: Through the sound of erasure came a voice, murmuring without pause.
en.STORY_CH17_MID_A_10: If it's a person, we bring her back. Before our names fade out.
en.STORY_CH17_MID_B_01: As the echoforms scattered, the words running down Seb's arm went still. Contradicting sentences rested side by side on one body.
en.STORY_CH17_MID_B_02: See? Everything the archive erased is right here. It can't delete any of it while I'm alive.
en.STORY_CH17_MID_B_03: Store contradictions in one body and the archive can't pin down what to delete. Logically sound. Physically reckless.
en.STORY_CH17_MID_B_04: Totally reckless! So let me come with you. Even a living index lasts longer with people beside her.
en.STORY_CH17_MID_B_05: The recorder lit up. As the seventeenth mark surfaced, the faded names in the expedition log returned to their places.
en.STORY_CH17_MID_B_06: Seventeen. Three to go. This number weighs more than any shell count.
en.STORY_CH17_MID_B_07: About that recorder. There's exactly one matching mark on the archive's lowest floor. In the original stacks from the night of the Blackout.
en.STORY_CH17_MID_B_08: Opening it needed an index, and now you have one. Me. …But once you read it, there's no going back to not knowing.
en.STORY_CH17_MID_B_09: …That's fine. We only ever go forward anyway!
en.STORY_CH17_MID_B_10: …We open it at camp. With everyone there.
en.STORY_CH17_OUTRO_01: The Index Predator's catalog collapsed, and torn cards fell like snow. On every scrap, a name bled back into view.
en.STORY_CH17_OUTRO_02: …I tried to erase every meeting. If none of it had ever happened, no one would grieve…
en.STORY_CH17_OUTRO_03: The crew called each other's names, once each. Not one answer came late.
en.STORY_CH17_OUTRO_04: Every pulse is normal. Everyone remembers everyone. …Thank goodness. Really.
en.STORY_CH17_OUTRO_05: Hold on. At the very bottom of the layers the Predator swallowed, one document survived.
en.STORY_CH17_OUTRO_06: 'Last Line opening order. Execution: 00:00 tomorrow.' …This isn't a record. It's a scheduled command.
en.STORY_CH17_OUTRO_07: Meaning you can delete the record, but the command stays. Burn the whole archive and the opening still won't stop.
en.STORY_CH17_OUTRO_08: We don't wait on dead orders. We cut them first. That's all.
en.STORY_CH17_OUTRO_09: Then every speaker in the stacks came on, softly.
en.STORY_CH17_OUTRO_10: Navigator, you have confirmed the truth. In twelve years, the draft has not been wrong by a single line.
en.STORY_CH17_OUTRO_11: Please conclude what you began. One final signature, and no one will ever be lost again.
en.STORY_CH17_OUTRO_12: Nobody's concluding anything! The Navigator is writing something new with us now!
en.STORY_CH17_OUTRO_13: I'll pin that scheduled order in my index. Proof that it's a fixed command, not a prophecy. And I'm coming along.
en.STORY_CH17_OUTRO_14: One day left. We head for the Last Line. We get there before it opens.
en.STORY_CH17_PREBOSS_01: At the heart of the stacks, a colossal card catalog yawned open. Every card that spilled out held one member's joining record.
en.STORY_CH17_PREBOSS_02: Reading room patrons, please be advised. Index cleanup is beginning. Duplicate, contradictory and intervening entries will be discarded.
en.STORY_CH17_PREBOSS_03: Passengers whose joining records are discarded, please treat one another as strangers.
en.STORY_CH17_PREBOSS_04: With every torn card, a stranger's wariness spread through the crew's eyes.
en.STORY_CH17_PREBOSS_05: …Who are you people? Whose signal is this?
en.STORY_CH17_PREBOSS_06: No idea. Funny thing, though. You're strangers, but I feel like I could trust you with my back.
en.STORY_CH17_PREBOSS_07: The cards can tear, but the index is right here! Vera, the dead line. You came to give the rescue signal back to people!
en.STORY_CH17_PREBOSS_08: …Right. To give the signal back. Those words are mine.
en.STORY_CH17_PREBOSS_09: So we're strangers. So what? We choose each other again from scratch. We've done it once. Second time's faster.
en.STORY_CH17_PREBOSS_10: Warning. Bonds without records are not approved. Please submit your reason for traveling together.
en.STORY_CH17_PREBOSS_11: We heard the whole truth at camp. After that, no one left their seat. That's our reason.
en.STORY_CH17_PREBOSS_12: Submitted. Every one of us standing here is the reason.
en.STORY_CH17_PREBOSS_13: Great, we'll do the index cleanup for you. I'm taking point!
en.STORY_CH18_CAMP_01: The night they first slowed the clock, camp lanterns stretched along the rails. One by one, the crew came to find the Navigator.
en.STORY_CH18_CAMP_02: Navigator, I'll hold tomorrow's signal to the end. Even if your recorder goes dark, I'll find you.
en.STORY_CH18_CAMP_03: Get some sleep. Medic's orders. …Honestly, I'm scared too. So let's both close our eyes a while.
en.STORY_CH18_CAMP_04: Weight is meant to be shared. The night you signed alone is over.
en.STORY_CH18_CAMP_05: Keeping this short. …You've fought well so far. Do the same tomorrow.
en.STORY_CH18_CAMP_06: I'm no good with words. I'll just be next to you. That's enough, right?
en.STORY_CH18_CAMP_07: Everything said tonight is in my index. Whatever gets erased tomorrow, it stays here.
en.STORY_CH18_CAMP_08: Navigator! Remember I said war scares me? This time it doesn't. …Well, half of me isn't scared!
en.STORY_CH18_CAMP_09: Last of all, Maeru climbed into a carriage beside the tracks and tugged each seatbelt, one by one.
en.STORY_CH18_CAMP_10: …Lot more seats to check this time.
en.STORY_CH18_CAMP_11: …Thanks. You take this row, I'll take that one. Leave the one empty seat as it is.
en.STORY_CH18_CAMP_12: It's Sio's. It stays empty for now. When the day comes to bring her along, I'll fill it.
en.STORY_CH18_CAMP_13: Tomorrow we fight to buy a day. I won't let a single seat go empty. …Except that one.
en.STORY_CH18_HARD_INTRO_01: Behind Midnight Terminus, construction was still underway. Driverless rail carts hauled sleepers over half-laid track without rest.
en.STORY_CH18_HARD_INTRO_02: Zero construction error. None of the tremor you'd find in track laid by people.
en.STORY_CH18_HARD_INTRO_03: So it's a worksite with nobody on it. Nobody to yell at us if we smash it!
en.STORY_CH18_HARD_INTRO_04: …No. There's one track-cutting signal. Someone inside is undoing the construction.
en.STORY_CH18_HARD_INTRO_05: The sound of cutting steel rang out steadily in the distance. The cutting was just a little slower than the laying.
en.STORY_CH18_HARD_INTRO_06: If someone's cutting that alone, we help. So the faster side wins.
en.STORY_CH18_HARD_INTRO_07: There's a supervisor's signature in the construction log. And every date is written backward.
en.STORY_CH18_HARD_INTRO_08: We follow the sound. We reach it before the machines do.
en.STORY_CH18_HARD_OUTRO_01: Midnight Terminus's great clock stopped at 11:59. The second hand trembled but never moved to the next mark.
en.STORY_CH18_HARD_OUTRO_02: Locked one minute short of opening. This station can never be a terminus now.
en.STORY_CH18_HARD_OUTRO_03: …Best station I ever designed. A terminus no one ever arrives at.
en.STORY_CH18_HARD_OUTRO_04: I laid the tracks. Now I'll lay tracks that take people home. From your side.
en.STORY_CH18_HARD_OUTRO_05: Good. Laying suits you better than cutting.
en.STORY_CH18_HARD_OUTRO_07: Cut pieces of track piled up beneath the stopped clock. The station was left with an hour that ended no one.
en.STORY_CH18_HARD_OUTRO_08: I'm naming this time in my index. 'The Minute That Ends No One.'
en.STORY_CH18_HARD_OUTRO_09: One minute left standing is enough. Let's go spend the rest of our day.
en.STORY_CH18_INTRO_01: Outside the archive, new rails glowed from one horizon to the other. Every line curved toward a single point.
en.STORY_CH18_INTRO_02: The Last Line. Twenty-four hours until opening. The pull of the rails tilted the lanterns of distant cities all one way.
en.STORY_CH18_INTRO_03: The Ashen City, the Sky Bridge, the snowfields, the capital… Every city we've passed through is being dragged to the same coordinates.
en.STORY_CH18_INTRO_04: It matches the archive's scheduled order to the second. Midnight sharp. No delays, no early start.
en.STORY_CH18_INTRO_05: Then, as if the whole sky had become a speaker, the announcement came down from every direction at once.
en.STORY_CH18_INTRO_06: Attention, all passengers. The Last Line opens tonight at midnight.
en.STORY_CH18_INTRO_07: All passengers, please board. This train stops at every station, and you may alight at none.
en.STORY_CH18_INTRO_08: Navigator, a reserved seat awaits you. The same one as twelve years ago.
en.STORY_CH18_INTRO_09: That seat? The one at Platform Seven? Ugh, I've got static all over!
en.STORY_CH18_INTRO_10: They're pulling the refugees in too. Thousands of them are in no shape to resist on their own.
en.STORY_CH18_INTRO_11: One day. Within one day, we must protect every one of these coordinates.
en.STORY_CH18_INTRO_12: One day… plenty for scouting, tight for fighting.
en.STORY_CH18_INTRO_13: We hit the nearest relay first. …Navigator, don't lose sight of that recorder's light.
en.STORY_CH18_INTRO_14: The Lamplighters began walking against the tilt of the lanterns.
en.STORY_CH18_MID_A_01: The relay's giant reference clock didn't tick; it thrummed, low, like a heartbeat. Every city's clock turned to its rhythm.
en.STORY_CH18_MID_A_02: Can't delete the opening order from here. The core is deeper in. But guess what I found?
en.STORY_CH18_MID_A_03: This clock is the reference time. Every line checks it to decide when midnight is. Slow it down, and midnight comes late.
en.STORY_CH18_MID_A_04: How much can we slow it? Numbers, not guesses.
en.STORY_CH18_MID_A_05: If we keep cutting the reference signal, up to twenty-four hours. Exactly one day.
en.STORY_CH18_MID_A_06: A day is enough to reach the Last Line's core. We can't cancel it, but we can get there.
en.STORY_CH18_MID_A_07: If you can't delete the order, cut its clock. Rational.
en.STORY_CH18_MID_A_08: Problem is who guards that clock while we cut. Control won't just sit there.
en.STORY_CH18_MID_A_09: I'll put this day in my index too. Not a day we were given—a day we earned.
en.STORY_CH18_MID_A_10: We buy a day. We pay for it ourselves. On to the next relay tower.
en.STORY_CH18_MID_B_01: As the last signaler fell, white steam rose from Yurien's barrel. The reference clock's pulse slowed once more.
en.STORY_CH18_MID_B_02: Thanks. Alone, ninety seconds was never enough. Tonight, for the first time, I had time to spare.
en.STORY_CH18_MID_B_03: Yurien. Long-range gunner. Since the day they started laying this line, I've been delaying construction one day at a time with shells.
en.STORY_CH18_MID_B_04: Using shell flight time as a clock? …Same as my method. Margin of error?
en.STORY_CH18_MID_B_05: Point-two seconds per shell. A little tighter than yours.
en.STORY_CH18_MID_B_07: The recorder etched its eighteenth light, the same pattern as the impact tallies carved on Yurien's barrel.
en.STORY_CH18_MID_B_08: I'll spend my remaining shells buying time. Down to the very last one. That's my signature.
en.STORY_CH18_MID_B_09: Eighteen! Just two left. I've never been so happy to see empty slots.
en.STORY_CH18_MID_B_10: We see this day through. The signalers' main force is in front of Midnight Terminus.
en.STORY_CH18_OUTRO_01: The tower collapsed, and the compressed day scattered. The red lights died, and the reference clock's slow pulse returned.
en.STORY_CH18_OUTRO_02: …If you know when it ends, even fear can be counted. With the end set in advance, no one would feel uneasy…
en.STORY_CH18_OUTRO_03: Reference time locked! The opening moves from tonight to tomorrow midnight. We actually bought a day!
en.STORY_CH18_OUTRO_04: Four shells left. Four shells for a day—not a bad trade.
en.STORY_CH18_OUTRO_05: Amid the cheering, Maeru raised the radio. The retreat team had missed their scheduled report by an hour.
en.STORY_CH18_OUTRO_06: Retreat team, respond. Vera, Iri, Liv, Orsa.
en.STORY_CH18_OUTRO_07: Instead of an answer, a static-laced rescue signal came back. The same sentence, repeating at the same interval.
en.STORY_CH18_OUTRO_08: Retreat team here. The tracks… only lead back to the start. I've lost count of the laps.
en.STORY_CH18_OUTRO_09: No one's hurt. But every lap, someone forgets something.
en.STORY_CH18_OUTRO_10: Coordinates confirmed. The whole retreat route has closed into a loop. A track with no end—the Unfading Circuit.
en.STORY_CH18_OUTRO_11: Passengers in the Circuit section, please wait in accordance with return procedures.
en.STORY_CH18_OUTRO_12: Navigator, you have bought a day. I will be watching to see whom you bring back with it.
en.STORY_CH18_OUTRO_13: So the day we earned goes to four people. …No—of course it does.
en.STORY_CH18_OUTRO_14: People before the opening. We go to the Circuit. We bring all four back.
en.STORY_CH18_PREBOSS_01: A colossal signal tower stood in the plaza before Midnight Terminus. The lights at its crown went dark red one by one, like a second hand.
en.STORY_CH18_PREBOSS_02: That's the Doom Signaler. Every hour we delayed is stockpiled inside it.
en.STORY_CH18_PREBOSS_03: Delay notice. A delay has occurred in the operating timetable.
en.STORY_CH18_PREBOSS_04: The delayed time will now be returned. Commencing midnight barrage. Passengers, please lower your heads.
en.STORY_CH18_PREBOSS_05: It's packing a whole day into one shell and sending it back. If it lands, every hour we bought is gone.
en.STORY_CH18_PREBOSS_06: The refugee column is inside the blast radius! Thousands are still on the tracks!
en.STORY_CH18_PREBOSS_07: Vera, Iri, Liv, Orsa. You're the retreat team. Open a way out for the column.
en.STORY_CH18_PREBOSS_08: I'm done arriving late. This time I'll go ahead and wait for you.
en.STORY_CH18_PREBOSS_09: The rest of us bend the trajectory. With four gunners, even a day-sized shell can be made to miss.
en.STORY_CH18_PREBOSS_10: I'll run the numbers. Yurien, I'm trusting your point-two.
en.STORY_CH18_PREBOSS_11: Warning. A timetable without a fixed end causes passengers anxiety. Midnight must be kept.
en.STORY_CH18_PREBOSS_12: Anxious nights are when gunners get busiest. Tonight we only need to bend one trajectory.
en.STORY_CH18_PREBOSS_13: All right—gunners take the sky, everyone else the tower! I'll open the way!
en.STORY_CH18_PREBOSS_14: The retreat team's lanterns receded toward the column. Only one red light remained on the tower.
en.STORY_CH19_CAMP_01: They set the camp lanterns in a ring at the heart of the Circuit, and Moen closed her notebook. This time, each would speak in her own voice.
en.STORY_CH19_CAMP_02: To give the rescue signals back to people. That's not a reason one lap can erase.
en.STORY_CH19_CAMP_03: Even late, I deliver to the end. I said it myself this time, so I won't forget.
en.STORY_CH19_CAMP_04: Toa, Seon, Adeline, Kir, Tiel… With every reason spoken, the Circuit's rails slowed a little more.
en.STORY_CH19_CAMP_05: So no one carries a verdict alone! However many laps, that doesn't change!
en.STORY_CH19_CAMP_06: I buy time down to the last shell. …Saying it out loud is a little embarrassing.
en.STORY_CH19_CAMP_07: To be a witness to choices. …But just now, someone other than us answered.
en.STORY_CH19_CAMP_08: On the Circuit's deepest track, a faint lantern flickered. The lantern Maeru had carried trembled in the same rhythm.
en.STORY_CH19_CAMP_09: …Platform Seven rescue team, Sio here. At the sealed seat, still holding. Maeru, can you hear me?
en.STORY_CH19_CAMP_10: I think this is as far as I go. It's not your fault. When they wake up, tell them: choose together this time.
en.STORY_CH19_CAMP_11: …Did you hear, Sio? A promise. This time, we choose together.
en.STORY_CH19_CAMP_12: …Thank you, Sio—from the one you protected. Twelve years late, but in person.
en.STORY_CH19_CAMP_13: For twelve years, I never cleared your seat. …I'm not waiting anymore. I'm taking you with me.
en.STORY_CH19_CAMP_14: When the record ended, the lantern on the deep track shone long once, then went out. In Maeru's arms, the other lantern grew warm.
en.STORY_CH19_HARD_INTRO_01: At the seam where the Circuit's rails met, the grinding of steel rang without end. It was the sound of the loop holding itself together.
en.STORY_CH19_HARD_INTRO_02: The seam widens by a hundredth of a millimeter every lap. This is the weakest point.
en.STORY_CH19_HARD_INTRO_03: Then there's no reason to save shells. Just give me coordinates.
en.STORY_CH19_HARD_INTRO_04: Wait. Life sign near the seam. The same person pops out at the same spot every lap.
en.STORY_CH19_HARD_INTRO_05: Someone tumbled out of the gap, gasping, then was dragged back into the loop. Thirty seconds later, the same spot, again.
en.STORY_CH19_HARD_INTRO_06: She's hurt. The same wound every time. When she comes out next, we have to catch her.
en.STORY_CH19_HARD_INTRO_07: Catching is my specialty. Need fast hands? Call me.
en.STORY_CH19_HARD_INTRO_08: We catch her next lap. Set up in front of the seam.
en.STORY_CH19_HARD_OUTRO_01: When the Ouroboros Rail snapped at its seam, the steel that had been a loop stretched out long. For the first time, the track had a front and a back.
en.STORY_CH19_HARD_OUTRO_02: Loop signature gone. This track only runs one way now.
en.STORY_CH19_HARD_OUTRO_03: …It's not pulling me back. Thirty seconds passed, and I'm not back at the start.
en.STORY_CH19_HARD_OUTRO_04: You're all right now. Breathe slowly. This is a road you only walk once.
en.STORY_CH19_HARD_OUTRO_05: Then… what's next? Where do we go next? I can't remember the last time I said 'next.'
en.STORY_CH19_HARD_OUTRO_06: Next is wherever we're headed. If you want to come, there's a seat for you.
en.STORY_CH19_HARD_OUTRO_07: I'm coming. Anywhere, as long as I don't have to count.
en.STORY_CH19_HARD_OUTRO_08: Light from a distant lantern spilled in from the end of the straightened track. Velk stared at it for a long time.
en.STORY_CH19_HARD_OUTRO_09: I'll write it down. Velk, her first 'next.' Dated today.
en.STORY_CH19_INTRO_01: At the mouth of the Circuit, the same milepost repeated without end. Every sign read: '0 km to the start.'
en.STORY_CH19_INTRO_02: The whole track is a single loop. Forty kilometers around, no exits. Exactly one hour per lap.
en.STORY_CH19_INTRO_03: A road where running forward gets you back to the start. So much for my pride as a scout.
en.STORY_CH19_INTRO_04: We bought a day, and this is where it goes. …That's fine. Time spent on people is the most precious kind.
en.STORY_CH19_INTRO_05: Four sets of footprints were stamped on the track dozens of layers deep. The same steps, treading the same spots again and again.
en.STORY_CH19_INTRO_06: The retreat team's footprints. Counting the layers… that's thirty-one laps.
en.STORY_CH19_INTRO_07: …We bring all four back. We leave no one.
en.STORY_CH19_INTRO_08: Then the same announcement rang from every station in the Circuit, each a half-beat off the last.
en.STORY_CH19_INTRO_09: Attention, please. The Circuit section is currently undergoing return procedures.
en.STORY_CH19_INTRO_10: Return requires one substitute passenger. If one of you remains, the rest may go home.
en.STORY_CH19_INTRO_11: Designating a substitute passenger. Navigator, will you choose the passenger again this time?
en.STORY_CH19_INTRO_12: Hear that, Control? The answer is 'no one.' We don't buy cheap deals.
en.STORY_CH19_INTRO_13: Footsteps instead of words. …Good. That's the clearest answer there is.
en.STORY_CH19_INTRO_14: There's no loop that can't be broken. Heavy as it is, let's go in.
en.STORY_CH19_INTRO_15: The thirty-second lap, we run together. Moving in.
en.STORY_CH19_MID_A_01: On the thirty-second lap, the Lamplighters found the retreat team. The four sat in a circle on the tracks, watching one another.
en.STORY_CH19_MID_A_02: You came… Thank goodness. No one's hurt. But something's wrong.
en.STORY_CH19_MID_A_03: Why did I join the Lamplighters? I remember holding the floodgate. After that… it's blank.
en.STORY_CH19_MID_A_04: Last lap it was Orsa. One person per lap loses their reason for joining.
en.STORY_CH19_MID_A_05: Whoever loses their reason is designated the substitute passenger. They have no reason to stay, and none to leave.
en.STORY_CH19_MID_A_06: The ticket core is at the center of the Circuit. It erases reasons to make someone 'fine to leave behind.'
en.STORY_CH19_MID_A_07: Liv, it's in my index! The flooded signal station: 'Even a late rescue gets delivered to the end.' Your words!
en.STORY_CH19_MID_A_08: …Even a late rescue. Yes. That's my voice, all right.
en.STORY_CH19_MID_A_09: But the core erases faster than the index can record. Next lap, it'll be one of us.
en.STORY_CH19_MID_A_10: Then we reach the center this lap. Retreat team with us. Nobody falls behind.
en.STORY_CH19_MID_B_01: As the echoforms withdrew, Moen opened her worn notebook. Every reason erased over thirty-two laps was written there in dense pencil.
en.STORY_CH19_MID_B_02: I'm Moen. I kept records at the Circuit's signal box. I've written down the reasons of everyone who circles here—by hand, not by machine.
en.STORY_CH19_MID_B_03: There's one way to get a reason back: say it again in your own voice. I'll read you what I wrote.
en.STORY_CH19_MID_B_04: I take responsibility for bringing drifting coordinates home. …Hearing it in my own voice, it has weight again.
en.STORY_CH19_MID_B_05: Handwritten records… as an archivist, I'm a little jealous. …Let's write together, Moen.
en.STORY_CH19_MID_B_06: The nineteenth light etched itself into the recorder—thin as a pencil stroke, and impossible to erase.
en.STORY_CH19_MID_B_07: I'll come with you. At the last moment, you'll need someone to witness who chose what.
en.STORY_CH19_MID_B_08: Nineteen. One left. …First time my hand has shaken while counting.
en.STORY_CH19_MID_B_09: One left. And before that, we lose no one here. On to the core.
en.STORY_CH19_OUTRO_01: As the ticket tore, the Circuit's track revealed an end for the first time. Beyond the broken loop, a straight road stretched away.
en.STORY_CH19_OUTRO_02: Default changed. 'Sacrifice procedure' deleted. 'Everyone returns' entered. …Written by hand. This is the original now.
en.STORY_CH19_OUTRO_03: …An empty train can bring no one home. I believed someone had to stay for the rest to return…
en.STORY_CH19_OUTRO_04: No one stayed behind. Maeru called the names one by one, and every name answered.
en.STORY_CH19_OUTRO_05: Every drifting coordinate has come home. Retreat team, return complete.
en.STORY_CH19_OUTRO_06: Everyone's pulse is normal. …It took a while, but no one's missing.
en.STORY_CH19_OUTRO_07: Then, beyond the broken Circuit, beams of light rose across the world. The lanterns of all nineteen lines they had crossed flowed in one direction.
en.STORY_CH19_OUTRO_08: I traced the flow back. There's one convergence point. The place the Directorate's blueprints call 'the Last Lantern.'
en.STORY_CH19_OUTRO_09: Same as the terminus coordinates in the archive's scheduled order. At the end of the Last Line stood the Last Lantern.
en.STORY_CH19_OUTRO_10: Navigator, the light of every line is gathering. Preparations are nearly complete.
en.STORY_CH19_OUTRO_11: I will wait for you before the Last Lantern. Just one signature, as twelve years ago.
en.STORY_CH19_OUTRO_12: I'll watch the final moment. Who chose what—I'll write it to the end.
en.STORY_CH19_OUTRO_13: We go to the Last Lantern. …And Sio's lantern rides with us.
en.STORY_CH19_PREBOSS_01: Above the gates of the Circuit's central station floated one enormous ticket. Crew names surfaced on it and vanished, one after another.
en.STORY_CH19_PREBOSS_02: Passengers of the return train, please be advised. Verifying departure conditions. One substitute passenger is required.
en.STORY_CH19_PREBOSS_03: The sacrifice procedure is the default for return. If just one of you remains, everyone else may go home.
en.STORY_CH19_PREBOSS_04: That again. Drop one, save the rest. Easy math, wrong answer.
en.STORY_CH19_PREBOSS_05: If someone has to stay, I'll stay. …That's exactly what it wants us to say. Not falling for it.
en.STORY_CH19_PREBOSS_06: I've been writing down the ticket's code. 'Sacrifice' isn't an order. It's a factory default.
en.STORY_CH19_PREBOSS_07: A default? Defaults exist to be changed! Where's the settings menu?
en.STORY_CH19_PREBOSS_08: You lack authority to change settings. The default exists to protect you, passengers.
en.STORY_CH19_PREBOSS_09: The authority is right here. No one who circled this loop ever chose to stay. I saw every one of them.
en.STORY_CH19_PREBOSS_10: The Lamplighters leave no one behind. That's our default.
en.STORY_CH19_PREBOSS_11: One ticket makes a fine target. Nobody rides in anyone's place.
en.STORY_CH19_PREBOSS_12: I'll punch that ticket! With lightning, full of holes!
en.STORY_CH19_PREBOSS_13: The names on the ticket began to spin faster. It was the sound of choosing the next name to erase.
en.STORY_CH20_CAMP_01: The last camp. The five founding members sat in a circle around one small lantern.
en.STORY_CH20_CAMP_02: Remember? The first lantern we lit. We cranked a hand generator all night just to light one section.
en.STORY_CH20_CAMP_03: Four of us cried when that one section lit up. Everyone but Maeru. Though she had her back turned, so who knows.
en.STORY_CH20_CAMP_04: Three, precisely. I had dust in my eye. …According to the record.
en.STORY_CH20_CAMP_05: And I came up with the name! The ones who open the lantern road—the Lamplighters! My head was totally overcharged that day!
en.STORY_CH20_CAMP_06: After that, we grew. Twenty-four now. But the very first one we brought in—I never said it properly.
en.STORY_CH20_CAMP_07: All five turned to the Navigator at once. The small lantern's light spread evenly among the six of them.
en.STORY_CH20_CAMP_08: Navigator. It's late, but I'll say it properly. …Welcome to the Lamplighters.
en.STORY_CH20_CAMP_09: No need. I've had your front since the first scouting run. Always will.
en.STORY_CH20_CAMP_10: Whoa, hands in! Can I send a spark through? Just once!
en.STORY_CH20_CAMP_12: …I'm logging it. As of today, the Lamplighters have six founding members.
en.STORY_CH20_CAMP_13: Great. Then tomorrow the six of us go light a lamp. We just need to bring in that twentieth signature.
en.STORY_CH20_CAMP_14: Tomorrow will be long. …Sleep well, all of you.
en.STORY_CH20_HARD_INTRO_01: Beneath the Last Lantern, a vertical shaft plunged out of sight. A dropped flare fell and fell without reaching the bottom.
en.STORY_CH20_HARD_INTRO_02: The Lumen Abyss. Where erased records sink. Thousands of names are layered in the signal from the bottom.
en.STORY_CH20_HARD_INTRO_03: The walls of the abyss bore the marks of every line the Lamplighters had crossed, carved upside down.
en.STORY_CH20_HARD_INTRO_04: Names overwritten in the archive, reasons erased in the Circuit… It all flowed down here in the end.
en.STORY_CH20_HARD_INTRO_05: We cannot leave what drifts behind. We go down.
en.STORY_CH20_HARD_INTRO_06: I'll hold the rope. So the way back never breaks.
en.STORY_CH20_HARD_INTRO_07: Deep places are scary, but my light can reach the bottom!
en.STORY_CH20_HARD_INTRO_08: Going down. Coming up, we'll be as heavy as the names we bring.
en.STORY_CH20_HARD_OUTRO_01: As the floor of the Lumen Abyss brightened, the sunken names rose as motes of light. Thousands of them climbed back up the shaft.
en.STORY_CH20_HARD_OUTRO_02: They won't all fit in my index! …That's okay. From now on, these names will be remembered on their own.
en.STORY_CH20_HARD_OUTRO_03: I watched every name rise. Not one missed.
en.STORY_CH20_HARD_OUTRO_04: Everyone safe, all the way up the rope. The way back held.
en.STORY_CH20_HARD_OUTRO_05: Some days later, Platform Seven. The first train of the new timetable waited to depart.
en.STORY_CH20_HARD_OUTRO_06: So where's our first stop? This is the first time we get to decide.
en.STORY_CH20_HARD_OUTRO_07: Vote's unanimous: 'Anywhere, all together.' …That's not a destination.
en.STORY_CH20_HARD_OUTRO_08: Maeru checked the seatbelt of one empty seat, then set a small lantern down in it.
en.STORY_CH20_HARD_OUTRO_09: Sio. This time, we go together.
en.STORY_CH20_HARD_OUTRO_10: Window seat. Perfect for the view.
en.STORY_CH20_INTRO_01: At the end of the world stood a single lantern. Its glass, as large as a rail carriage, was empty; in twelve years it had never held a flame.
en.STORY_CH20_INTRO_02: Before it, the light of nineteen lines poured in like rivers—from the rescue signal on a dead line to the pencil strokes of the Circuit.
en.STORY_CH20_INTRO_03: The Last Lantern. The Last Line's terminus and the first station of every line. On the blueprints, they're the same spot.
en.STORY_CH20_INTRO_04: The ignition mechanism is sealed. Twenty layers of locks. Force it, and the whole lantern shatters.
en.STORY_CH20_INTRO_05: The day we bought is down to a few hours. And the opening is still scheduled.
en.STORY_CH20_INTRO_06: The lantern's glass trembled. Every speaker on the Last Line switched on at once, like a single indrawn breath.
en.STORY_CH20_INTRO_07: Navigator, I have been waiting for your final signature.
en.STORY_CH20_INTRO_08: For twelve years I have not deviated from the draft by a single line. It is exactly as you wrote it.
en.STORY_CH20_INTRO_09: Please conclude it now. Then no one will ever lose anything, ever again.
en.STORY_CH20_INTRO_10: But then nobody can go anywhere! That's just… stopping!
en.STORY_CH20_INTRO_11: Conclude? Don't make me laugh. We've only just started.
en.STORY_CH20_INTRO_12: I'll write it down. Before the Last Lantern: twenty-four arrived. Not one missing.
en.STORY_CH20_INTRO_13: We open the seal first. We'll prove this isn't the end—it's the first station.
en.STORY_CH20_MID_A_01: When the recorder touched the first seal plate, nineteen lights rose across the glass in turn. Only the twentieth slot stayed dark.
en.STORY_CH20_MID_A_02: The seal doesn't count heads. It counts independent signatures from different lines. Twenty. We have nineteen.
en.STORY_CH20_MID_A_03: We've got way more than twenty people. Can't the five of us each sign one?
en.STORY_CH20_MID_A_04: No. You five share one line. The seal spots a copy of the same record in half a beat.
en.STORY_CH20_MID_A_05: Then the twentieth has to come from a line nobody has tied off yet. There's exactly one left in my index.
en.STORY_CH20_MID_A_06: The Final Line. The defensive line guarding the Last Lantern. Its defense signal is still alive.
en.STORY_CH20_MID_A_07: Navigator, there is no need for a twentieth. Your signature alone is sufficient.
en.STORY_CH20_MID_A_08: That voice has gotten impatient. Twelve years of waiting, and it can't manage half a day.
en.STORY_CH20_MID_A_09: We go to the Final Line. The twentieth isn't someone we bring—it's someone who chooses for herself.
en.STORY_CH20_MID_A_10: The twentieth slot was still dark. Beyond it, from the Final Line, a single defense signal blinked as steadily as a sentry's steps.
en.STORY_CH20_MID_B_01: As the echoform tide receded, Lavent lowered her shield. Every defense signal linked to it fell quiet at once.
en.STORY_CH20_MID_B_02: Lavent. The last of the Final Line garrison. For twelve years, I guarded the lantern from behind this wall.
en.STORY_CH20_MID_B_03: My job was to guard it until someone came to light it. …You came. So now we light it together. My signature too.
en.STORY_CH20_MID_B_04: The recorder trembled. The moment the twentieth light rose, all twenty marks joined into a single ring.
en.STORY_CH20_MID_B_05: Twenty! My index is full. This one recorder weighs more than the entire archive.
en.STORY_CH20_MID_B_06: Twenty independent signatures from different lines, confirmed. …The math is done. What's left isn't math.
en.STORY_CH20_MID_B_07: Attention, please. Line signatures cannot replace the draft. …They must not be able to.
en.STORY_CH20_MID_B_08: That voice just wavered. I'm writing it down. Terminus Control, first hesitation.
en.STORY_CH20_MID_B_10: I'll be the wall all the way to the lantern. Don't worry about your back. Just walk.
en.STORY_CH20_OUTRO_01: The floodgate fell, and darkness surged in. The Lamplighters did not hold it back. With twenty lights, they drew a road through it.
en.STORY_CH20_OUTRO_02: …I locked the light away so no one would wander in the dark. Without darkness, no one would ever lose their way…
en.STORY_CH20_OUTRO_03: The Last Lantern caught fire. The darkness did not vanish. But wherever anyone stood, the way home could be seen.
en.STORY_CH20_OUTRO_04: …New timetable confirmed. First coordinates: twenty signatures from different lines.
en.STORY_CH20_OUTRO_05: Passengers, please… choose your own destinations. Navigator, have a good journey.
en.STORY_CH20_OUTRO_06: Hear that? From every line, it's not rescue signals coming in—just hellos. Thank you, Navigator.
en.STORY_CH20_OUTRO_07: You did well. Sleep deep tonight. This time it's a real medic's order.
en.STORY_CH20_OUTRO_08: Case closed! Toss the file in the campfire. One more light tonight!
en.STORY_CH20_OUTRO_09: I'm leaving the last line of my index blank. The next story starts there.
en.STORY_CH20_OUTRO_10: I saw it. I saw you choose. I wrote it all down.
en.STORY_CH20_OUTRO_11: Guess you won't need a wall anymore. I'll keep watching your back anyway.
en.STORY_CH20_OUTRO_12: Sio would've laughed. Me, of all people—'one shot is enough'—needing twenty.
en.STORY_CH20_OUTRO_13: Navigator! Where to now? Anywhere's fine—I'm fully charged!
en.STORY_CH20_OUTRO_14: Record complete. …No. Record begins. Day one of the new timetable.
en.STORY_CH20_OUTRO_15: I'll open the next road too. Wherever it leads this time.
en.STORY_CH20_PREBOSS_01: Before the Last Lantern, a colossal floodgate barred the tracks. In the dark beyond it, countless things were breathing.
en.STORY_CH20_PREBOSS_02: Attention, please. This is the Final Line floodgate. Ignition of the lantern is not permitted.
en.STORY_CH20_PREBOSS_03: Light the lantern, and every darkness gains a route as well. Wherever light reaches, darkness follows.
en.STORY_CH20_PREBOSS_04: Therefore, ignition will be turned against itself. The moment it lights, every line will be shut inside this gate.
en.STORY_CH20_PREBOSS_05: For twelve years, I guarded this wall alongside that gate. Same purpose. Wrong method, that's all.
en.STORY_CH20_PREBOSS_06: Then the speakers above the floodgate came on, softly. The voice was quieter and kinder than ever.
en.STORY_CH20_PREBOSS_07: Navigator. That night twelve years ago, you signed to protect everyone.
en.STORY_CH20_PREBOSS_08: I have never once forgotten that intent. You may rest now. I will protect the rest.
en.STORY_CH20_PREBOSS_09: …Navigator. If you go with that voice, I won't hold it against you. But you choose. With your own hand, this time.
en.STORY_CH20_PREBOSS_10: The Navigator signed not the draft but a blank timetable, and the recorder's twenty lights gathered around the signature.
en.STORY_CH20_PREBOSS_11: That's not a signature on the draft. It's the first line of a new timetable. …Same hand as twelve years ago. Different choice.
en.STORY_CH20_PREBOSS_12: The Navigator held out a hand, and twenty-five hands settled over it. The signature no longer belonged to any one person.
en.STORY_CH20_PREBOSS_13: This isn't a night of signing alone. We said we'd share the weight.
en.STORY_CH20_PREBOSS_14: …I do not understand. That choice may cause someone to be lost again.
en.STORY_CH20_PREBOSS_15: I know. We choose it anyway. Better to go on together knowing we may lose, than to stop so we never do.
en.STORY_CH20_PREBOSS_16: Ignition signal detected. Closing the floodgate. All passengers, please wait in the dark.
en.STORY_CH20_PREBOSS_17: We've done enough waiting to last a lifetime. I'll open the last road!
en.STORY_CH20_PREBOSS_18: I'll be the wall. Everyone, run for the lantern!
en.STORY_PROLOGUE_01: Twelve years ago, the light in the sky went out. People call that day the Great Blackout.
en.STORY_PROLOGUE_02: The surface drowned in afterglow storms of whirling memory and sound. The last cities held on to one another by a single mineral railway underground.
en.STORY_PROLOGUE_03: Only stretches lit by lanterns along the rails were safe. We called the people who relight dead lanterns the Lamplighters.
en.STORY_PROLOGUE_04: And today, for the first time in twelve years, the Lamplighters returned to Platform Seven.
en.STORY_PROLOGUE_05: Rails are clear, no echoform readings. …It's almost too quiet.
en.STORY_PROLOGUE_06: One signal is alive. Inside the train. It hasn't gone dark once in twelve years.
en.STORY_PROLOGUE_07: …Someone stopped here, once. Everyone, keep your spacing. We go slow.
en.STORY_PROLOGUE_08: Someone slept in a seat of the stalled carriage. Only the recorder on their wrist blinked, like a heartbeat.
en.STORY_PROLOGUE_09: H-hey! They're alive! The pulse is… no, it's like the machine is beating for them?
en.STORY_PROLOGUE_10: Wake procedure confirmed. Navigator, it is an honor to see you again.
en.STORY_PROLOGUE_11: …Was that a Directorate announcement? Weren't those speakers dead twelve years ago?
en.STORY_PROLOGUE_12: Lower your weapons. We deal with the broadcast later. This person comes first.
en.STORY_PROLOGUE_13: The sleeper opened their eyes. Strange letters surfaced on the recorder: Record Navigator.
en.STORY_PROLOGUE_14: Can you hear me? We're the Lamplighters. It's all right, slowly. What do you want to do first?
en.STORY_PROLOGUE_15: Good. Lanterns first. Where there's light, there's a road.
en.STORY_PROLOGUE_16: That device is no ordinary thing. It's reading the signals around us even now.
en.STORY_PROLOGUE_17: I'll clear the scouting route. Follow as soon as the signal comes alive.
en.STORY_PROLOGUE_18: Before leaving, Maeru quietly checked the seatbelt of one empty seat.
en.STORY_REL_I_01: I gathered broken station announcements and turned them into a little chorus.
en.STORY_REL_I_02: A trace that someone lived matters more to me than perfect pitch.
en.STORY_REL_I_03: Let us play it together at the next station. It will sound better than listening alone.
en.STORY_REL_M_01: Before departure, I even check the seatbelt on the empty seat. I cannot relax if I skip it.
en.STORY_REL_M_02: I began doing it so I would not forget the teammate who never returned.
en.STORY_REL_M_03: Today I placed new rescue gear there. An empty place can help save the next person now.
